'''Jokes''' on [[Decipher]] Star Wars CCG cards sit in a card's title, lore or game text and have no effect on play. They include nods to the films' cast and crew, references to songs, films, books and advertising, puns, Decipher in-jokes, jokes about scenes in the films, deadpan lore, gags that the card itself acts out, and running gags repeated across several cards. Hidden pictures and icons are listed at [[Easter eggs]], and titles that scramble real names at [[Anagrams]].

Each joke shows the card, with its original [[Decipher]] face from the card lists on Decipher's own website, beside a picture of what it refers to, then explains the reference. Jokes are grouped by type and listed alphabetically within each type, and each one names the set its card comes from. Cards that share one joke are shown together in one block, and each running gag is one block that takes its cards one at a time.

== <span id="type-pop-culture-reference"></span>Pop-culture references ==
=== [[All My Urchins]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-allmyurchins-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=All My Urchins|alt=All My Urchins original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - All My Children logo.png|350x450px|alt=The title logo of the soap opera All My Children]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The title logo of the soap opera ''All My Children''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Ten Little Injuns 1868 chorus.png|350x450px|alt=The chorus of Ten Little Injuns (1868): One little, two little, three little, four little]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The chorus of "Ten Little Injuns" (1868): "One little, two little, three little…"</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Ten Little Injuns 1868 cover.jpg|350x450px|alt=The cover of Ten Little Injuns (1868): the title above ten dancing Indians]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The cover of "Ten Little Injuns" (1868): the title above ten dancing Indians</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "One little, two little, three little Bespinites."

''All My Children'' was a long-running ABC soap opera.<ref name="wp-amc">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_My_Children All My Children], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261006070347/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_My_Children Internet Archive], 6 October 2026.</ref> The title swaps "Children" for "Urchins", meaning ragged street children. The lore follows the counting rhyme "One little, two little, three little Indians" with Bespinites. The rhyme goes back to Septimus Winner's 1868 song "Ten Little Injuns", whose cover shows the ten "Injuns" of the title dancing in a row and whose chorus begins "One little, two little, three little, four little, five little 'Injun' boys".<ref name="levy-tli">[https://levysheetmusic.mse.jhu.edu/collection/106/203 Ten Little Injuns. Comic Song and Chorus.] (Philadelphia: Lee & Walker, 1868), Lester S. Levy Sheet Music Collection, Johns Hopkins University. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20240225045353/https://levysheetmusic.mse.jhu.edu/collection/106/203 Internet Archive], 25 February 2024.</ref><ref name="wp-tenlittle">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Little_Indians Ten Little Indians], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260910173023/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Little_Indians Internet Archive], 10 September 2026.</ref>

=== [[Bespin Motors Void Spider THX 1138]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-bespinmotorsvoidspiderthx1138-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bespin Motors Void Spider THX 1138|alt=Bespin Motors Void Spider THX 1138 original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - THX 1138 film poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=The poster of the 1971 film THX 1138]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The poster of the 1971 film ''THX 1138''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' Bespin Motors Void Spider THX 1138 (title)

''THX 1138'' (1971) is George Lucas's first major film, named after its hero's serial number. THX is also Lucas's sound company and theatre sound system, and Luke told the Imperial officer they were transferring Chewie from cellblock 1138.<ref name="artshow-bespin-motors-void-spider-thx-1138">[http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/anewhope/dark/ebespinmotorsvoidspider.html Bespin Motors Void Spider THX 1138], Art Show: Easter Eggs, Decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991105102202/http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/anewhope/dark/ebespinmotorsvoidspider.html Internet Archive], 5 November 1999.</ref> The card gives the shuttle that number as part of its model name. [[Decipher]]'s Art Show listed the title among its Easter eggs.<ref name="artshow-bespin-motors-void-spider-thx-1138" />

=== [[Blow Parried]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref3-D-blowparried-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Blow Parried|alt=Blow Parried original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Bear Bryant 1977.jpg|350x450px|alt=Bear Bryant in 1977]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Bear Bryant (1977), often credited with "defense wins championships"</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]] · '''Text:''' "Offense may win battles, but defense keeps you alive long enough to mount an offense."

The lore reworks the sports saying "offense sells tickets, defense wins championships", also quoted as "offense wins games, defense wins championships" and often credited to Alabama football coach Bear Bryant.<ref name="wp-defense">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_wins_championships Defense wins championships], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260211053005/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_wins_championships Internet Archive], 11 February 2026.</ref> To parry is to block a blow, here in a lightsaber duel.

=== [[Boba Fett With Blaster Rifle]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:EP-D-bobafettwithblasterrifle-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Boba Fett With Blaster Rifle|alt=Boba Fett With Blaster Rifle original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Princess Bride film poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=The poster of the 1987 film The Princess Bride]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The poster of the 1987 film ''The Princess Bride''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Enhanced Premiere]] · '''Text:''' "Notorious bounty hunter. 'As you wish.'"

The lore is a double reference. In ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980), Darth Vader tells the bounty hunters "No disintegrations", and Boba Fett answers "As you wish."<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The same words are the catchphrase of Westley in ''The Princess Bride'', William Goldman's 1973 novel and the 1987 film, where the farm boy answers every order from Buttercup with "As you wish".<ref name="wp-pbnovel">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Princess_Bride_(novel) The Princess Bride (novel)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261007181745/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Princess_Bride_(novel) Internet Archive], 7 October 2026.</ref><ref name="wq-pb">[https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/The_Princess_Bride_(film) The Princess Bride (film)], Wikiquote. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260705104709/https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/The_Princess_Bride_(film) Internet Archive], 5 July 2026.</ref>

=== [[Boelo]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-boelo-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Boelo|alt=Boelo original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Simon and Garfunkel 1968.jpg|350x450px|alt=Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel in 1968]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Simon & Garfunkel (1968), "The Boxer"</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "Naroon Cuthus' predecessor as Jabba's right hand man. Sees what he wants to see. Hears what he wants to hear. Has a pet womp rat named Worra."

"Hears what he wants to hear" echoes Simon & Garfunkel's "The Boxer" (1968): "Still, a man hears what he wants to hear / And disregards the rest".<ref name="ps-boxer">[https://www.paulsimon.com/track/the-boxer-5/ The Boxer (lyrics)], The Paul Simon Official Site. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260120130554/https://www.paulsimon.com/track/the-boxer-5/ Internet Archive], 20 January 2026.</ref> "Sees what he wants to see" is a common saying.

=== [[Brainiac]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-brainiac-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Brainiac|alt=Brainiac original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Brainiac Action Comics 544.png|350x450px|alt=Brainiac with a huge robotic skull]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">DC Comics' Brainiac in his robot body, ''Action Comics'' #544 (1983), art by Ed Hannigan</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' "BoShek nicknamed this male Siniteen 'Brainiac' due to his ability to calculate hyperspace coordinates in his head. 'He's the brains, sweetheart!'"

Brainiac is a DC Comics supervillain, first seen in ''Action Comics'' #242 (1958), an alien artificial intelligence; in 1983 he was given a robot body with a giant skull.<ref name="c12-wp-brainiac">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brainiac Brainiac], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010035816/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brainiac Internet Archive], 10 October 2026.</ref> The Siniteen on the card has an oversized, exposed brain. The lore ends with Han's line about Luke in ''Star Wars'', "He's the brains, sweetheart."<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> The game text does the calculating: the card's power is the square root of a formula that ends "+ π", with π printed to 27 decimal places, and its destiny number is π.

=== [[Captain Yutani]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-L-captainyutani-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Captain Yutani|alt=Captain Yutani original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Weyland-Yutani logo from Aliens.png|350x450px|alt=The Weyland-Yutani Corp logo]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The Weyland-Yutani logo, as seen in ''Aliens'' (1986)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] · '''Text:''' Name. Lore: "Scout and heavy weapons specialist. Carries custom repulsorlift compensators to allow fluid movement with light artillery weapons."

Yutani is a background Rebel officer at the briefing in ''Return of the Jedi''; Decipher's Endor card gave him his name and lore.<ref name="wook-yutani">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Yutani Yutani], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251202031805/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Yutani Internet Archive], 2 December 2025.</ref> Weyland-Yutani is the corporation in the ''Alien'' films.<ref name="wp-weyland">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weyland-Yutani Weyland-Yutani] (redirects to Alien (franchise)), Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261011074629/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weyland-Yutani Internet Archive], 11 October 2026.</ref> Ron Cobb, who designed for ''Alien'' (1979), made up the name from "Weylan", one letter away from British Leyland, and "Yutani", the surname of a Japanese neighbor of his.<ref name="ss-cobb">[https://alienseries.wordpress.com/2016/01/31/crew-logs-ron-cobb/ Crew Logs: Ron Cobb], Strange Shapes (31 January 2016), quoting Cobb in John Mollo and Ron Cobb's ''Authorized Portfolio of Crew Insignias from the United States Commercial Spaceship Nostromo''. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260219083446/https://alienseries.wordpress.com/2016/01/31/crew-logs-ron-cobb/ Internet Archive], 19 February 2026.</ref> Cobb had earlier designed several of the creatures in the Mos Eisley cantina for ''Star Wars''.<ref name="wp-cobb">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Cobb Ron Cobb], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260924182622/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Cobb Internet Archive], 24 September 2026.</ref> The lore fits the sequel ''Aliens'' (1986) as well: the Colonial Marines' heavy "smart guns" were machine guns mounted on a Steadicam, a camera support that keeps movement smooth,<ref name="wp-aliens">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliens_(film) Aliens (film)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261013173645/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliens_(film) Internet Archive], 13 October 2026.</ref> much as Yutani's "repulsorlift compensators" allow "fluid movement" with his heavy weapons.

=== [[Cyborg Construct]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-cyborgconstruct-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Cyborg Construct|alt=Cyborg Construct original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-lobot-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Lobot|alt=Lobot, who wears the implant]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Lobot]], who wears the implant</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Advertised as, 'Artificial intelligence worth shaving your head for.'"

The lore is written as an advertising slogan for the implant. [[Lobot]], who wears it around the back of his head, is bald, so the ad calls it "worth shaving your head for".

=== [[Dash]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-dash-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Dash|alt=Dash original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Fun with Dick and Jane page 8.jpg|350x450px|alt=Page 8 of Fun with Dick and Jane: Run, Dick. See me run, said Sally. See Spot run.]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Page 8 of ''Fun with Dick and Jane'': "Run, Dick." … "See Spot run."</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Go, Dog. Go! cover.jpg|258x323px|alt=The cover of P. D. Eastman's Go, Dog. Go! (1961)]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The cover of P. D. Eastman's ''Go, Dog. Go!'' (1961)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "See Luke run. Run Luke, run!"

''Dick and Jane'' were simple American reading books for young children, known for lines like "See Spot run."<ref name="wp-dickjane">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_and_Jane Dick and Jane], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260928041909/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_and_Jane Internet Archive], 28 September 2026.</ref> Page 8 of the reader ''Fun with Dick and Jane'' has both halves of the lore's pattern on one page: "Run, Dick." and "'See me run,' said Sally. 'See Spot run.'"<ref name="fwdj">William S. Gray and May Hill Arbuthnot, ''[https://archive.org/details/funwithdickjane0000gray/page/n11/mode/1up Fun with Dick and Jane]'' (Toronto: W. J. Gage, undated), p. 8. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/funwithdickjane0000gray Internet Archive] (item funwithdickjane0000gray).</ref> An earlier reader, ''More Dick and Jane Stories'' (1934), has "How Spot ran! Dick saw Spot run."<ref name="dj1934">William H. Elson and William S. Gray, ''[https://archive.org/details/moredickjanestor00elso/page/n13/mode/1up More Dick and Jane Stories]'' (Chicago: Scott, Foresman, 1934), p. 12. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250426205730/https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:More_Dick_and_Jane_Stories_(IA_moredickjanestor00elso).pdf Internet Archive], 26 April 2025.</ref>

P. D. Eastman's picture book ''Go, Dog. Go!'' (1961) is another possible model.<ref name="wp-gdg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go,_Dog._Go! Go, Dog. Go!], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026150849/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go,_Dog._Go! Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref> Its title has the same shape as the lore's second sentence: a verb, the one spoken to, then the verb again, "Go, Dog. Go!" beside "Run Luke, run!" Only the Dick and Jane readers also match the first sentence, "See Luke run.", so they are the closer match, but both readings are possible.

=== [[Don't Tread On Me]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-donttreadonme-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Don't Tread On Me|alt=Don't Tread On Me original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Gadsden flag.png|350x450px|alt=The Gadsden flag, a coiled rattlesnake above the words DONT TREAD ON ME]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The Gadsden flag of 1775</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' Don't Tread On Me (title). Lore: "Han did not take kindly to Jabba's posturing."

"Don't Tread on Me" is the motto of the Gadsden flag of 1775, written under a coiled rattlesnake.<ref name="wp-gadsden">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gadsden_flag Gadsden flag], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261023090453/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gadsden_flag Internet Archive], 23 October 2026.</ref> The 1997 Special Edition of ''Star Wars'' put back a deleted scene in which Han meets Jabba in the Mos Eisley docking bay. Harrison Ford had walked through the place where the computer-made Jabba's tail would be, so Han was moved digitally to step on Jabba's tail, and Jabba squeals.<ref name="wp-swchanges">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changes_in_Star_Wars_re-releases Changes in Star Wars re-releases], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261007025821/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changes_in_Star_Wars_re-releases Internet Archive], 7 October 2026.</ref> The card shows that scene, and its title is the snake's warning, from a Hutt whose tail has just been stepped on.

=== [[Eventually You'll Lose]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Tat-L-eventuallyyoulllose-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Eventually You'll Lose|alt=Eventually You'll Lose original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Tat-D-watto-decipher-archive.jpg|350x450px|link=Watto|alt=Watto]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Watto]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Wide World of Sports logo.png|350x450px|alt=The logo of ABC's Wide World of Sports]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The logo of ABC's ''Wide World of Sports''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] · '''Text:''' "In the end, Watto finally came to understand the agony of defeat."

ABC's ''Wide World of Sports'' opened each show with "the thrill of victory ... and the agony of defeat".<ref name="wp-wwos">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_World_of_Sports_(American_TV_program) Wide World of Sports (American TV program)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261007024112/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_World_of_Sports_(American_TV_program) Internet Archive], 7 October 2026.</ref> In ''The Phantom Menace'', Watto bets on the podrace and loses Anakin to Qui-Gon.<ref name="film-tpm">''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace'' (film), directed by George Lucas, 20th Century Fox, 1999.</ref> The lore borrows the show's phrase for his loss.

=== [[Frozen Dinner]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-frozendinner-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Frozen Dinner|alt=Frozen Dinner original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Tony the Tiger mascot.jpg|350x450px|alt=Tony the Tiger, the Kellogg's Frosted Flakes mascot]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Tony the Tiger, the Kellogg's Frosted Flakes mascot</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Tony the Tiger and Groucho Marx Frosted Flakes ad 1955.jpg|350x450px|alt=A 1955 Frosted Flakes ad: You bet your life they're Gr-r-reat!]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A 1955 Frosted Flakes ad: "You bet your life they're Gr-r-reat!"</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "They're Gr-r-reat!"

Tony the Tiger is the cartoon mascot of Kellogg's Frosted Flakes cereal, and his catchphrase is "They're gr-r-reat!"<ref name="wp-tony">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_the_Tiger Tony the Tiger], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026024623/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_the_Tiger Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref> A 1955 Kellogg's magazine ad has Tony tell Groucho Marx "You bet your life they're Gr-r-reat!"<ref name="ca-ff1955">[https://clickamericana.com/topics/food-drink/vintage-1950s-breakfast-cereals Vintage 1950s breakfast cereals], Click Americana. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260521015343/https://clickamericana.com/topics/food-drink/vintage-1950s-breakfast-cereals Internet Archive], 21 May 2026.</ref> The lore describes a frozen Rebel served as a meal, then ends with Tony's cry.

=== [[Furry Fury]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-furryfury-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Furry Fury|alt=Furry Fury original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Mourning Bride 1697 title page.jpg|350x450px|alt=The title page of the first edition (1697) of William Congreve's play The Mourning Bride]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The title page of the first edition (1697) of Congreve's ''The Mourning Bride''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Mourning Bride 1697 Woman scorn'd line.jpg|350x450px|alt=The line Nor Hell a Fury, like a Woman scorn'd, in the 1697 edition]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Page 39 of the 1697 edition: "Nor Hell a Fury, like a Woman scorn'd."</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "Hoth hath no fury like a Wookiee scorned."

The saying "Hell hath no fury like a woman scorned" means no anger is fiercer than that of a woman rejected. It comes from William Congreve's 1697 play ''The Mourning Bride'': "Nor Hell a fury like a woman scorn'd."<ref name="encyc198">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 198. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref><ref name="congreve1697">William Congreve, ''[https://archive.org/details/mourningbridetra00cong The Mourning Bride]'' (London: Jacob Tonson, 1697), end of Act III. Transcription: [https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Mourning_Bride/Act_III Wikisource]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20120308172619/https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Mourning_Bride/Act_III Internet Archive], 8 March 2012.</ref> The lore swaps "Hell" for Hoth and the woman for a Wookiee, after Han's line "All right, don't lose your temper." The bullwhip on Han's hip is listed at [[Easter eggs]].

=== [[High Anxiety]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-highanxiety-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=High Anxiety|alt=High Anxiety original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - High Anxiety film poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=The poster of the 1977 film High Anxiety]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The poster of Mel Brooks's 1977 film ''High Anxiety''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke candidate - Mel Brooks in High Anxiety 1977.jpg|350x450px|alt=Mel Brooks in High Anxiety]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Mel Brooks in his film ''High Anxiety'' (1977)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' High Anxiety (title)

''High Anxiety'' is Mel Brooks's 1977 comedy, a parody of Alfred Hitchcock's films.<ref name="wp-highanx">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Anxiety High Anxiety], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261011082449/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Anxiety Internet Archive], 11 October 2026.</ref> The card has the same title. Decipher's artists also hid Alfred Hitchcock references in card art: the lights on [[Retract The Bridge]] spell "VERTIGO", and [[Undercover]] has "Good Evening", the opening words of ''Alfred Hitchcock Presents'' (see [[Easter eggs]]).<ref name="artshow-retract">[http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/anewhope/dark/eretractthebridge.html Retract The Bridge], Art Show: Easter Eggs, Decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991105181513/http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/anewhope/dark/eretractthebridge.html Internet Archive], 5 November 1999.</ref><ref name="artshow-undercover">[http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/anewhope/light/eundercover.html Undercover], Art Show: Easter Eggs, Decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991108205619/http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/anewhope/light/eundercover.html Internet Archive], 8 November 1999.</ref>

=== [[Hunchback]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-hunchback-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Hunchback|alt=Hunchback original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Igor's hump from behind in Young Frankenstein.jpg|350x450px|alt=Igor (Marty Feldman) seen from behind, his hump under his cloak, in Young Frankenstein]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Igor (Marty Feldman) from behind, with his hump, in ''Young Frankenstein''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Young Frankenstein film poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=Young Frankenstein (1974)]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">''Young Frankenstein'' (1974)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' "What hump?"

In Mel Brooks's 1974 comedy ''Young Frankenstein'', Frederick Frankenstein meets his new servant Igor, who walks with a large hump. Frederick offers, as a surgeon, to help with the hump, and Igor answers "What hump?"<ref name="wq-yf">[https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Young_Frankenstein Young Frankenstein], Wikiquote. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026024831/https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Young_Frankenstein Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref> The card's lore is Igor's answer, word for word.

=== [[Jabba's Influence]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-jabbasinfluence-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Jabba's Influence|alt=Jabba's Influence original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Godfather film poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=The poster of the 1972 film The Godfather]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The poster of the 1972 film ''The Godfather''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Marlon Brando as Vito Corleone.jpg|350x450px|alt=Marlon Brando as Vito Corleone in a tuxedo, holding a cat]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Marlon Brando as Vito Corleone, the Godfather (publicity photo, 1973)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "Jabba makes offers one cannot refuse. Smugglers, thieves and competitors who do not acquiesce have been rumored to wake up with a bantha's head in their bed."

In ''The Godfather'' (1972), Vito Corleone, the Godfather of the title, played by Marlon Brando,<ref name="b13-wp-vito">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vito_Corleone Vito Corleone], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260914002956/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vito_Corleone Internet Archive], 14 September 2026.</ref> says "I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse." The American Film Institute ranked it the second-greatest quotation in American film.<ref name="wp-afiquotes">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFI%27s_100_Years...100_Movie_Quotes AFI's 100 Years...100 Movie Quotes], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261011073125/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFI%27s_100_Years...100_Movie_Quotes Internet Archive], 11 October 2026.</ref> When the film producer Jack Woltz turns the Corleone family down, he wakes up with the severed head of his prized racehorse in his bed.<ref name="wp-godfather">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Godfather The Godfather], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022220838/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Godfather Internet Archive], 22 October 2026.</ref> The lore uses both, with the head of a [[Bantha|bantha]] in place of the horse.

=== [[Leia Of Alderaan]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-leiaofalderaan-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Leia Of Alderaan|alt=Leia Of Alderaan original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Helen of Troy Pompeii fresco.jpg|350x450px|alt=Helen boards a ship for Troy (Pompeii fresco)]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Helen boards a ship for Troy (Pompeii fresco)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Doctor Faustus title page.png|350x450px|alt=Marlowe's Doctor Faustus]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Marlowe's ''Doctor Faustus''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "The face that launched a thousand starships."

In Greek legend, Helen of Troy was so beautiful that a thousand Greek ships sailed to war to win her back from Troy.<ref name="encyc198" /> Christopher Marlowe's play ''Doctor Faustus'' calls her "the face that launch'd a thousand ships".<ref name="marlowe">Christopher Marlowe, ''Doctor Faustus'' (A-text, 1604), scene 13: "Was this the face that launch'd a thousand ships?"</ref> The lore says the same of Leia, with starships.

=== [[Lift Tube Escape]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-lifttubeescape-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lift Tube Escape|alt=Lift Tube Escape original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Holden and Stone store directory 1907.jpg|350x450px|alt=The Store Directory of Holden and Stone, a Pittsfield department store, 1907: First floor, front: Umbrellas, Ladies' Neckwear, Leather Goods]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A department store's floor-by-floor "Store Directory", Pittsfield, Massachusetts, 1907</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Are You Being Served cast on the shop floor.jpg|350x450px|alt=The cast of Are You Being Served? standing at a department-store counter]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The cast of ''Are You Being Served?'' on the Grace Brothers shop floor (1970s)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "First floor: parasols and powdered blue milk. Second floor: bantha skin rugs, bog-wing drapes and juri juice tables. Third floor: a squadron of Imperial stormtroopers."

The lore is a department-store lift announcement, like the theme tune of the BBC sitcom ''Are You Being Served?'' (1972–1985), which is set in the Grace Brothers department store.<ref name="wp-aybs">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Are_You_Being_Served%3F Are You Being Served?], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250920155138/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Are_You_Being_Served%3F Internet Archive], 20 September 2025.</ref> Over the ring of a cash register, a lift girl (the voice of Stephanie Gathercole) calls out each floor and what it sells:<ref name="hiwaay-aybs">[https://home.hiwaay.net/~emilyj/theme.html "Are You Being Served?": The Theme Song], Emily's AYBS pages. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20241008054122/https://home.hiwaay.net/~emilyj/theme.html Internet Archive], 8 October 2024.</ref><ref name="bcg-aybs">[https://www.comedy.co.uk/features/comedy-rewind/are-you-being-served/ Dear Sexy Knickers: A love letter to Are You Being Served?], British Comedy Guide. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20241206221743/https://www.comedy.co.uk/features/comedy-rewind/are-you-being-served/ Internet Archive], 6 December 2024.</ref>
<blockquote>Ground floor: perfumery, stationery and leather goods, wigs and haberdashery, kitchenware and food. Going up! First floor: telephones, gents' ready-made suits, shirts, socks, ties, hats, underwear and shoes. Going up! Second floor: carpets, travel goods and bedding, material, soft furnishings, restaurant and teas. Going down!</blockquote>
Real department stores printed the same kind of floor-by-floor list. A 1907 "Store Directory" advertisement for Holden & Stone, a department store in Pittsfield, Massachusetts, begins "First floor, front: Umbrellas, Ladies' Neckwear, Leather Goods" and lists carpets, rugs and draperies further down.<ref name="hs1907">Holden & Stone advertisement, "Store Directory", ''Pittsfield Directory'' (1907), p. 555. [https://archive.org/details/pittsfield-ma-directory-collection Pittsfield + Berkshire County MA Directory Collection], Internet Archive, file Pittsfield_MA_Directory_1907. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/pittsfield-ma-directory-collection Internet Archive] (item pittsfield-ma-directory-collection).</ref> The card's second floor has the same goods in Star Wars form: rugs for carpets, drapes for furnishings, and tables for the restaurant. Its third floor, which the song never reaches, holds the stormtroopers. The goods are:
* '''Parasols''': sunshades, in place of the umbrella counter.
* '''Powdered blue milk''': [[Blue Milk]], the "nutrient-rich beverage common in moisture farm communities" of its card's lore, sold as a powder.
* '''Bantha skin rugs''': rugs made from the hide of a [[Bantha]], a pack animal "three meters tall".
* '''Bog-wing drapes''': curtains named for the [[Bog-wing (Dark)|bog-wing]], a winged predator of Dagobah's jungle.
* '''Juri juice tables''': tables for [[Juri Juice]], a drink "served in many cantinas and tapcafes".
* '''A squadron of Imperial stormtroopers''': the Empire's [[Stormtrooper]]s, waiting on the third floor.
