=== [[Lost In Space]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-lostinspace-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lost In Space|alt=Lost In Space original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Lost in Space Robot.jpg|350x450px|alt=Dr. Smith and the Robot, Lost in Space]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Dr. Smith and the Robot, ''Lost in Space''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Lost in Space logo.png|350x450px|alt=The title logo of the 1965 television series Lost in Space]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The title logo of the 1965 television series ''Lost in Space''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Kelly Tires Worry-Free ad 1959.jpg|350x450px|alt=A 1959 Kelly tire ad: the greatest joy in driving is driving WORRY-FREE!]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A 1959 Kelly tire ad: "the greatest joy in driving is driving WORRY-FREE!"</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "Congratulations on purchasing the TIE/ln starfighter by Sienar. … it should provide you with years of worry-free subjugation."

''Lost in Space'' (1965–1968) was a CBS television series about a family lost in space with their Robot.<ref name="wp-lostinspace">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_in_Space Lost in Space], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012143625/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_in_Space Internet Archive], 12 October 2026.</ref> The title fits a TIE fighter stranded in space. The lore is written as a cheerful product warranty, and "worry-free" was stock advertising copy: a 1959 Kelly-Springfield tire ad promised that "the greatest joy in driving is driving Worry-Free!"<ref name="kelly1959">[https://www.vintage-adventures.com/vintage-automotive-parts-service-ads/2988-1959-kelly-tires-ad-worry-free.html 1959 Kelly Tires Vintage Ad "Worry-Free"], Vintage Adventures. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250826040513/https://www.vintage-adventures.com/vintage-automotive-parts-service-ads/2988-1959-kelly-tires-ad-worry-free.html Internet Archive], 26 August 2025.</ref> The warranty ends by promising "years of worry-free subjugation": the product is a fighter, and what it gives its owner, the Empire, is the subjugation of others. A hidden picture of the Robot in the card's Effect symbol is listed at [[Easter eggs]].

=== [[Lost Relay]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-lostrelay-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lost Relay|alt=Lost Relay original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - HAL 9000 faceplate.jpg|350x450px|alt=HAL 9000, the computer that reports the AE-35 fault]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">HAL 9000, the computer that reports the AE-35 fault</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - 2001 A Space Odyssey film poster.png|350x450px|alt=The poster of the 1968 film 2001: A Space Odyssey]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The poster of the 1968 film ''2001: A Space Odyssey''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "…forwarding orders to the squadron via subspace AE-35 Transceivers."

In ''2001: A Space Odyssey'' (1968), the ship's computer HAL 9000 reports that the AE-35 unit, which keeps the ship's antenna aimed at Earth, is about to fail.<ref name="film-2001">''2001: A Space Odyssey'' (film), directed by Stanley Kubrick, Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, 1968. HAL 9000: "I've just picked up a fault in the AE-35 unit."</ref> That fault begins the film's breakdown of communications. The lore names the starfighters' comm relays "AE-35 Transceivers" on a card about lost communications.

=== [[Mobquet A-1 Deluxe Floater]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-mobqueta1deluxefloater-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Mobquet A-1 Deluxe Floater|alt=Mobquet A-1 Deluxe Floater original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Corinthian leather seats in a 1978 Chrysler New Yorker.jpg|350x450px|alt=Corinthian leather seats in a 1978 Chrysler New Yorker]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">"Corinthian leather" seats in a 1978 Chrysler New Yorker</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' "…Features include automated steering and fine Corellian leather."

"Corinthian leather" was an advertising term for the leather seats in Chrysler cars, first used in 1974. The actor Ricardo Montalbán spoke it in Chrysler's advertisements, and it is best remembered from the 1975 Chrysler Cordoba. The leather was made in Newark, New Jersey, not in Corinth.<ref name="wp-corinthian">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corinthian_leather Corinthian leather], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261013062453/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corinthian_leather Internet Archive], 13 October 2026.</ref> The lore sells the landspeeder the same way, with one letter changed: Corellian, from the Star Wars planet Corellia, in place of Corinthian.

=== [[None Shall Pass]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-noneshallpass-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=None Shall Pass|alt=None Shall Pass original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Black Knight in Monty Python and the Holy Grail.jpg|350x450px|alt=John Cleese as the Black Knight standing guard with his sword in Monty Python and the Holy Grail]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">John Cleese as the Black Knight in ''Monty Python and the Holy Grail'' (1975)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] · '''Text:''' None Shall Pass (title); "Jabba's Gamorrean guards keep a watchful eye for unwelcome guests."

In the 1975 film ''Monty Python and the Holy Grail'', the Black Knight guards a bridge and tells King Arthur "None shall pass". He refuses to stand aside even after Arthur cuts off his arms, insisting "'Tis but a scratch".<ref name="wp-blackknight">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Knight_(Monty_Python) Black Knight (Monty Python)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008135234/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Knight_(Monty_Python) Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref> The card gives the Black Knight's line to Jabba's [[Gamorrean Guard|Gamorrean guards]], who in the lore watch the palace for unwelcome guests.

=== [[Quick Draw]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-quickdraw-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Quick Draw|alt=Quick Draw original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - High Noon film poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=The poster of the 1952 film High Noon]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The poster of the 1952 film ''High Noon''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - A Fistful of Dollars US release poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=The US release poster of A Fistful of Dollars (1964)]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The US release poster of ''A Fistful of Dollars'' (1964)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Cowboy by Frederic Remington 1902.jpg|350x450px|alt=Frederic Remington's painting The Cowboy (1902): a cowboy reining in his horse on a steep slope]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A cowboy reining in his horse: Frederic Remington's ''The Cowboy'' (1902)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "It's high noon on Dagobah, his droid's reined in and Luke's got a fistful of credits."

''High Noon'' (1952) is a western that builds to a gunfight at noon, and ''A Fistful of Dollars'' (1964) is a western starring Clint Eastwood.<ref name="film-highnoon">''High Noon'' (film), directed by Fred Zinnemann, United Artists, 1952.</ref><ref name="wp-fistful">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Fistful_of_Dollars A Fistful of Dollars], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012195949/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Fistful_of_Dollars Internet Archive], 12 October 2026.</ref> The lore borrows both titles for Luke on Dagobah. "His droid's reined in" plays on a cowboy reining in his horse: to rein in is to stop or slow a horse by pulling the reins.<ref name="wikt-rein">[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/rein_in rein in], Wiktionary. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251222073029/https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/rein_in Internet Archive], 22 December 2025.</ref> Luke's droid is R2-D2, who rides in his X-wing during the attack on the Death Star and goes with him to Dagobah.<ref name="wp-r2">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R2-D2 R2-D2], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015114632/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R2-D2 Internet Archive], 15 October 2026.</ref> Read this way, R2-D2, who helps Luke handle his fighter in space, takes the place of the cowboy's horse. A "quick draw" is a fast pull of a gun from its holster.

=== <span id="R-3PO"></span>[[R-3PO (Ar-Threepio)]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-L-r3poarthreepio-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=R-3PO (Ar-Threepio)|alt=R-3PO (Ar-Threepio) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Cher from behind at Wembley Arena 1992.jpg|x600px|alt=Cher on stage, seen from behind in a backless costume and fishnet tights, with the tattoo on her backside visible]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:430px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Cher on stage at Wembley Arena, London, in 1992, with the tattoo on her backside. Photo: Brian Rasic/REX Features (Shutterstock), Wembley Arena, London, 1992</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Cher's tattoo at Wembley Arena 1992 close-up.jpg|300px|alt=Close-up of the tattoo on Cher's backside]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:300px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Close-up of the tattoo, from the same photograph. Photo: Brian Rasic/REX Features (Shutterstock)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Beavis and Butt-Head pick tattoos on butt 1993.jpg|450px|alt=The cartoon characters Beavis and Butt-Head float in front of a green on-screen menu titled "Menu: Chicks"; Butt-Head presses the box marked "Tattoos on butt"]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:450px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Beavis and Butt-Head pick "tattoos on butt" in the video for "I Got You Babe" with Cher (1993)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-thankthemaker-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Thank The Maker|alt=Thank The Maker]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Thank The Maker]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "Designed as a response to the threat of Imperial espionage droids. Joins a droid pool and uncovers spies. Has tattoo reading "Thank The Maker" on left posterior plating."

"Posterior" is a polite word for the backside, so the lore gives a prim protocol droid a tattoo on his bottom. Before the [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] set came out in 1996, tattoos on the backside were already a running joke about the singer and actress Cher. In the 1989 music video for her song "If I Could Turn Back Time", she sings to a crowd of sailors on the battleship USS ''Missouri'' in a black one-piece over a fishnet body stocking that left most of her tattooed buttocks bare, and the outfit made the video controversial.<ref name="b13-wp-itcbt">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_I_Could_Turn_Back_Time If I Could Turn Back Time], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012164614/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_I_Could_Turn_Back_Time Internet Archive], 12 October 2026.</ref><ref name="b14-yt-itcbt">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9n3A_-HRFfc Cher - If I Could Turn Back Time (Official Video)], Cher, YouTube. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015223526/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9n3A_-HRFfc Internet Archive], 15 October 2026.</ref> She kept showing the tattoo on stage: on her Love Hurts Tour, which played Wembley Arena in London on 6 and 7 May 1992, she performed in a backless costume over fishnet tights that left it in plain view.<ref name="wp-lovehurts">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Hurts_Tour Love Hurts Tour], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260106150920/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Hurts_Tour Internet Archive], 6 January 2026.</ref><ref name="rex-wembley">Photograph by Brian Rasic, "Cher Performing at the Wembley Arena, London, Britain - 1992", REX Features (Shutterstock), editorial reference 199891B.</ref> In 1993 Cher made fun of her own image by re-recording her 1965 hit "I Got You Babe" with Beavis and Butt-Head, the two snickering teenage cartoon characters of MTV's ''Beavis and Butt-Head'' (first run 1993–1997), a series in which they mostly sit on a couch and mock music videos. The song was on the album ''The Beavis and Butt-Head Experience'' (November 1993), not in an episode of the show. In its video the pair choose their dream woman from a "MENU: CHICKS", and Butt-Head says "We need a chick that's got tattoos on her butt"; the woman they get is Cher.<ref name="b13-wp-cher">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher Cher], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261017120143/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher Internet Archive], 17 October 2026.</ref><ref name="b14-latimes-bb">[https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-11-14-ca-56606-story.html Cher Gets Cheeky With Beavis and Butt-head], ''Los Angeles Times'' (14 November 1993). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260424224139/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-11-14-ca-56606-story.html Internet Archive], 24 April 2026.</ref><ref name="b14-wp-igyb">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Got_You_Babe I Got You Babe], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027023444/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Got_You_Babe Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref><ref name="b14-yt-igyb">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jyncsw3yq-k Cher, Beavis And Butt-Head - I Got You Babe], CherVEVO, YouTube. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260202111325/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jyncsw3yq-k Internet Archive], 2 February 2026.</ref> The print ads for the single reused an old photograph of Cher from behind, with the tattoo on her backside redrawn as the faces of Beavis and Butt-Head.<ref name="b14-latimes-bb" /> Years later Cher joked that her tattoos carried words: "On one cheek it said, 'Hi sailor,' and on the other it said, 'New in town.'"<ref name="b13-news24-cher">[https://www.news24.com/life/chers-first-tattoo-was-on-her-butt-20130926 Cher's first tattoo was on her butt], News24 (26 September 2013). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20230917002335/https://www.news24.com/life/chers-first-tattoo-was-on-her-butt-20130926 Internet Archive], 17 September 2023.</ref>

The words on R-3PO's tattoo are C-3PO's own catchphrase: "Thank the maker! This oil bath is going to feel so good," he says in ''Star Wars'' (1977), the droid's way of saying "thank God".<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> The [[Premiere]] card [[Thank The Maker]] takes its title from the line, and its lore says "C-3PO used phrase upon getting a much-needed cleansing oil bath." R-3PO is a red droid built like Threepio, so he wears Threepio's words where a person might have a tattoo on the backside. Lower-back tattoos, later nicknamed "tramp stamps", were also becoming popular in the late 1990s.<ref name="wp-lowerback">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower-back_tattoo Lower-back tattoo], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260915190632/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower-back_tattoo Internet Archive], 15 September 2026.</ref>

=== [[Rolling, Rolling, Rolling]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-D-rollingrollingrolling-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Rolling, Rolling, Rolling|alt=Rolling, Rolling, Rolling original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke candidate - Rawhide cast 1961.jpg|350x450px|alt=The cast of Rawhide in 1961]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Clint Eastwood, Paul Brinegar and Eric Fleming in ''Rawhide'', 1961</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' Rolling, Rolling, Rolling (title)

The theme song of the western series ''Rawhide'' (1959–1965), sung by Frankie Laine, opens "Rollin', rollin', rollin'".<ref name="silva-rawhide">[https://www.silvamasters.com/composition/MjM2MjI5NjQ5LTdhNDVjYw Theme (From "Rawhide")], Silva Screen Music, lyrics. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026153809/https://www.silvamasters.com/composition/MjM2MjI5NjQ5LTdhNDVjYw Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref><ref name="wp-rawhide">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawhide_(song) Rawhide (song)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260914154928/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawhide_(song) Internet Archive], 14 September 2026.</ref> The card's title repeats the word three times in the same way. Its lore is plain: destroyer droids "can roll up into a ball and move swiftly into a conflict."

=== [[Smoke Screen]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-smokescreen-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Smoke Screen|alt=Smoke Screen original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Winston pack with 1966 Caution label.jpg|350x450px|alt=A Winston pack in January 1966 with the warning Caution: Cigarette Smoking May Be Hazardous to Your Health]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A Winston pack, January 1966: "Caution: Cigarette Smoking May Be Hazardous to Your Health." The source of the lore's "can be hazardous to your health"</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Surgeon General's warning.jpg|350x450px|alt=A later cigarette pack with a Surgeon General's warning]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A later pack with a Surgeon General's warning, the kind that replaced the 1966 caution</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Warning: The Alderaanian Medical Association has determined that inhaling carbon-freezing smoke can be hazardous to your health."

The Federal Cigarette Labeling and Advertising Act of 1965 made cigarette packs sold in the United States carry the warning "Caution: Cigarette Smoking May Be Hazardous to Your Health." Packs carried it from January 1966.<ref name="fclaa-1965">Federal Cigarette Labeling and Advertising Act (Pub. L. 89-92, 79 Stat. 282, 1965), section 4, package warning: "Caution: Cigarette Smoking May Be Hazardous to Your Health." See also [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cigarette_Labeling_and_Advertising_Act Cigarette Labeling and Advertising Act], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260917103617/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cigarette_Labeling_and_Advertising_Act Internet Archive], 17 September 2026.</ref><ref name="ecu-winston">[https://digital.lib.ecu.edu/8750 Warning label on pack of Winston cigarettes], East Carolina University Digital Collections, Daily Reflector Negative Collection, 1–3 January 1966. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20240811125326/https://digital.lib.ecu.edu/8750 Internet Archive], 11 August 2024.</ref> The Public Health Cigarette Smoking Act, signed in 1970, replaced it with "Warning: The Surgeon General Has Determined That Cigarette Smoking Is Dangerous to Your Health." The Surgeon General is the top US health officer.<ref name="surgeon-1969">Public Health Cigarette Smoking Act of 1969 (Pub. L. 91-222), package warning: "Warning: The Surgeon General Has Determined That Cigarette Smoking Is Dangerous to Your Health." See also [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Health_Cigarette_Smoking_Act Public Health Cigarette Smoking Act], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260911143814/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Health_Cigarette_Smoking_Act Internet Archive], 11 September 2026.</ref>

The lore joins the two warnings, and the two pictures show one each:
* '''From the 1970 warning''': the opening, "Warning: The Alderaanian Medical Association has determined that", follows "Warning: The Surgeon General Has Determined That". The pack pictured is a later one: it still names the Surgeon General, but in newer wording.
* '''From the 1966 warning''': the ending, "can be hazardous to your health", follows "May Be Hazardous to Your Health" on the Winston pack, with "can" for "may".

The danger is carbon-freezing smoke, and the warning comes from an "Alderaanian Medical Association" in place of the Surgeon General.

=== [[Smuggler's Blues]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-smugglersblues-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Smuggler's Blues|alt=Smuggler's Blues original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Smuggler's Blues single cover.jpg|350x450px|alt=Glenn Frey, "Smuggler's Blues"]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Glenn Frey, "Smuggler's Blues"</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "It's the lure of easy credits. It's got a very strong appeal. Perhaps you'd understand better wearing my flight suit. It's the ultimate special modification, it's the smuggler's blues."

"Smuggler's Blues" is a Glenn Frey song about the drug trade.<ref name="encyc196">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 196. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref> Its chorus begins "It's the lure of easy money, it's got a very strong appeal" and ends "it's the smuggler's blues".<ref name="song-smug">Glenn Frey, "Smuggler's Blues", ''The Allnighter'', MCA Records, 1984.</ref> The lore follows the song line by line, swapping money for credits and the singer's shoes for a flight suit.

=== [[Sudden Impact]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-suddenimpact-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Sudden Impact|alt=Sudden Impact original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Grail Knight says He chose poorly in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade.jpg|600px|alt=The Grail Knight in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade as he says He chose poorly]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The Grail Knight in ''Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade'' (1989), at the moment he says "He chose... poorly."</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "An asteroid looming in one's path can force a quick decision. One must choose, but choose wisely. This pilot chose poorly."

In ''Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade'' (1989), the last of the knights who swore to guard the Holy Grail keeps it in a hidden temple among many false cups, and warns those who reach it: "But choose wisely, for while the true Grail will bring you life, the false Grail will take it from you."<ref name="film-ij3">''Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade'' (film), directed by Steven Spielberg, Paramount Pictures, 1989.</ref> The villain Walter Donovan lets Elsa Schneider choose for him. She hands him a jewelled gold cup, he drinks from it, ages to a skeleton in seconds and crumbles to dust, and the knight says "He chose... poorly."<ref name="wq-ij">[https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Indiana_Jones_and_the_Last_Crusade Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade], Wikiquote. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026024748/https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Indiana_Jones_and_the_Last_Crusade Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref><ref name="yt-chose">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VA7J0KkanzM Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade (10/10) Movie CLIP - He Chose Poorly (1989) HD], Movieclips, YouTube (1 June 2016), 0:00–2:23. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260925195939/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VA7J0KkanzM Internet Archive], 25 September 2026.</ref> Indiana then picks a plain cup, "the cup of a carpenter", drinks, and the knight tells him "You have chosen... wisely."<ref name="wq-ij" />

The card's lore uses the knight's words for a pilot who meets an asteroid: "An asteroid looming in one's path can force a quick decision. One must choose, but choose wisely. This pilot chose poorly." The picture shows how the pilot chose, an asteroid in a blinding white burst of impact. The game text turns the choice into a rule. Sudden Impact is deployed on an Effect or Utinni Effect, and during each of that card's owner's draw phases, if the Sudden Impact player occupies an asteroid sector, the owner "must choose" either to lose 1 Force or to cancel that Effect, so like the Grail seekers the opponent has to pick, and both choices cost something.

=== [[Swing-And-A-Miss]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-swingandamiss-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Swing-And-A-Miss|alt=Swing-And-A-Miss original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Swing and a miss.jpg|350x450px|alt=A batter swinging and missing for strike three]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A swing and a miss for strike three</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' •••Swing-And-A-Miss (title); "It's the bottom of the ninth level of Cloud City. Vader steps up to the platform. Here's the delivery. . . oooh, he took a big cut there! The Force sure wasn't with him on that one!"

The lore is written as a baseball radio call.<ref name="encyc198">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 198. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref> The "bottom of the ninth" is the last inning, a batter "steps up to the plate", the pitcher makes "the delivery", and a batter who "took a big cut" swung hard. Here Vader swings his lightsaber at Luke and misses. The three dots before the title finish the joke. A ••• card is restricted to three, and for an Interrupt that means a player may play at most three copies of it in a turn ([[Decipher Glossary 2.0#unique and restricted cards|Decipher Glossary]]). In baseball, a batter gets three strikes, and the third swing and a miss is a strikeout: three strikes and you're out.<ref name="wp-strikeout">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeout Strikeout], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260925015408/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikeout Internet Archive], 25 September 2026.</ref>

=== [[Visored Vision]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-visoredvision-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Visored Vision|alt=Visored Vision original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Blues Brothers film poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=The poster of the 1980 film The Blues Brothers]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The poster of the 1980 film ''The Blues Brothers''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "It's 15 parsecs to Kessel, we've replaced the negative power coupling, it's dark and we're wearing welding goggles. Hit it."

In ''The Blues Brothers'' (1980), Elwood says: "It's 106 miles to Chicago, we got a full tank of gas, half a pack of cigarettes, it's dark, and we're wearing sunglasses." Jake answers "Hit it."<ref name="film-blues">''The Blues Brothers'' (film), directed by John Landis, Universal Pictures, 1980.</ref><ref name="encyc196" /><ref name="forum8378">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?f=87&t=8378 Easter Eggs], Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums (27 December 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221210023930/https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?f=87&t=8378 Internet Archive], 10 December 2022.</ref> The lore copies the line with Kessel, the power coupling and welding goggles. Han and Chewbacca wear dark goggles in the image, and the "Blues Bros." copyright line is listed at [[Easter eggs]].

=== [[Yoda's Gimer Stick]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-yodasgimerstick-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Yoda's Gimer Stick|alt=Yoda's Gimer Stick original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Big stick cartoon.jpg|350x450px|alt=A 1904 cartoon of Theodore Roosevelt with his big stick]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A 1904 cartoon of Theodore Roosevelt with his big stick</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-pop-culture-reference|Pop-culture reference]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "Speak softly you may but a big stick you must carry, yes."

US President Theodore Roosevelt often quoted the saying "speak softly and carry a big stick": stay calm, but be ready to use force.<ref name="wp-bigstick">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_stick_ideology Big stick ideology], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261005132600/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_stick_ideology Internet Archive], 5 October 2026.</ref> The lore puts the saying into Yoda's backwards word order, for Yoda's own walking stick.

== <span id="type-cast-and-crew-nod"></span>Cast and crew nods ==
=== <span id="Linn'con"></span>[[Dams Denna]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-L-damsdenna.gif|350px|link=Dams Denna|alt=Dams Denna original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card: [[Dan Madsen]] as the kaadu handler in ''The Phantom Menace''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Abraham Lincoln by Alexander Gardner 1863.jpg|x490px|alt=Abraham Lincoln, photographed by Alexander Gardner in 1863]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:380px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Abraham Lincoln, photographed by Alexander Gardner on 8 November 1863 (public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-cast-and-crew-nod|Cast and crew nod]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Knowledgeable animal trainer and herd-master. Collector of Linn'con memorabilia."

[[Dan Madsen]], president of the Official Star Wars Fan Club and publisher of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'', appears uncredited in ''The Phantom Menace'' as the kaadu handler who takes the reins of Jar Jar Binks's kaadu at the victory parade in Theed.<ref name="wook-damsdenna">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dams_Denna Dams Denna], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251209030207/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dams_Denna Internet Archive], 9 December 2025.</ref> The card's title, Dams Denna, is an anagram of his name (see [[Anagrams]]), and its picture is Madsen in that scene.

The lore adds that Denna is a "collector of Linn'con memorabilia". Madsen collects Abraham Lincoln memorabilia: a 1999 profile of him in ''Westword'' says "today he collects Abraham Lincoln and Mark Twain memorabilia."<ref name="westword-madsen">Chris LaMorte, [https://www.westword.com/news/star-hustlers-5059622 "Star Hustlers"], ''Westword'' (4 March 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20200811235501/https://www.westword.com/news/star-hustlers-5059622 Internet Archive], 11 August 2020.</ref> Wookieepedia's article on Linn'con makes the same connection and cites that profile.<ref name="wook-linncon">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Linn%27con Linn'con], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260305151339/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Linn%27con Internet Archive], 5 March 2026.</ref> The name is a respelling of Lincoln rather than an anagram: Linn'con has one more n and one fewer l.

=== [[General McQuarrie]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-generalmcquarrie-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=General McQuarrie|alt=General McQuarrie original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Ralph McQuarrie 2008.jpg|350x450px|alt=Ralph McQuarrie in 2008]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Ralph McQuarrie]] in 2008</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Ralph McQuarrie Darth Vader painting.jpg|350x450px|alt=McQuarrie's production art for Star Wars]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">McQuarrie's production art for ''Star Wars''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-cast-and-crew-nod|Cast and crew nod]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' General McQuarrie (title)

The card is a nod to [[Ralph McQuarrie]], the conceptual artist of the original ''Star Wars'' trilogy, and its picture is of McQuarrie.<ref name="ins74-51">"Hoth Freezes Over: Who's Who in Echo Base", ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' #74 (2004), p. 51. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/star-wars-insider-d0e5c1/page/n46/mode/1up Internet Archive].</ref>

=== [[Lieutenant Sheckil]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-lieutenantsheckil-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lieutenant Sheckil|alt=Lieutenant Sheckil original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-bobafett-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Boba Fett (Cloud City)|alt=Boba Fett, also played by Bulloch]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Boba Fett (Cloud City)|Boba Fett]], also played by Bulloch</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-cast-and-crew-nod|Cast and crew nod]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Twin brother of a famous mercenary."

[[Jeremy Bulloch]] played the Imperial officer Sheckil in ''The Empire Strikes Back'', and he also played the bounty hunter Boba Fett.<ref name="wp-sheckil">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Sheckil Sheckil], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251210113330/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Sheckil Internet Archive]</ref> So the lore calls Sheckil the "twin brother of a famous mercenary": both were played by the same actor.<ref name="forum8378" /> The title is also listed at [[Anagrams]].

=== [[Lieutenant Watts]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-D-lieutenantwatts-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lieutenant Watts|alt=Lieutenant Watts original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Robert Watts on the Return of the Jedi set.jpg|350x450px|alt=Robert Watts at work as producer on location for Return of the Jedi, in front of Jabba's sail barge set]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Robert Watts at work as a producer, on location for ''Return of the Jedi''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-cast-and-crew-nod|Cast and crew nod]] · '''Set:''' [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] · '''Text:''' "Watts' gunnery skills produce devastating results."

Robert Watts was a co-producer of ''Return of the Jedi'' and appears in the film as an Imperial lieutenant.<ref name="wook-rwatts">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Robert_Watts Robert Watts], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260113182014/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Robert_Watts Internet Archive], 13 January 2026.</ref> Lucasfilm's obituary shows him at work on location in the California desert during the making of ''Return of the Jedi'', in front of the set of Jabba's sail barge.<ref name="lfl-watts">[https://www.lucasfilm.com/news/robert-watts-1938-2024/ Remembering Robert Watts, 1938-2024], Lucasfilm. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260416175822/https://www.lucasfilm.com/news/robert-watts-1938-2024/ Internet Archive], 16 April 2026.</ref> The card shares his name, and the lore's "produce devastating results" puns on his job. [[Major Marquand]]'s game text pairs Marquand with Watts.

=== <span id="Cast_and_crew_given_ranks"></span>[[Major Bren Derlin]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-L-majorbrenderlin-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Major Bren Derlin|alt=Major Bren Derlin original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Cliff Clavin.png|350x450px|alt=Ratzenberger as Cliff Clavin on Cheers]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Ratzenberger as Cliff Clavin on ''Cheers''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Cheers logo.png|350x450px|alt=Cheers (1982–1993)]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">''Cheers'' (1982–1993)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-cast-and-crew-nod|Cast and crew nod]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "At the Mos Eisley Cantina, everyone knows his name."

[[John Ratzenberger]] played Bren Derlin in ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="ins74-52">"Hoth Freezes Over: Who's Who in Echo Base", ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' #74 (2004), p. 52. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/star-wars-insider-d0e5c1/page/n47/mode/1up Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="encyc194">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 194. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref> He later played Cliff Clavin, a mail carrier who drinks at the Boston bar in the sitcom ''Cheers''.<ref name="wp-cliff">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliff_Clavin Cliff Clavin], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260717133538/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliff_Clavin Internet Archive], 17 July 2026.</ref> The ''Cheers'' theme song is "Where Everybody Knows Your Name", about a bar where everybody knows your name.<ref name="wp-wekyn">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_Everybody_Knows_Your_Name Where Everybody Knows Your Name], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260303093158/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_Everybody_Knows_Your_Name Internet Archive], 3 March 2026.</ref> The lore moves that bar to the Mos Eisley Cantina. Decipher's Art Show listed the line among its Easter eggs.<ref name="artshow-derlin">[http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/hoth/light/emajorbrenderlin.html Major Bren Derlin], Art Show: Easter Eggs, Decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000505095607/http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/hoth/light/emajorbrenderlin.html Internet Archive], 5 May 2000.</ref>

<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-D-majormarquand-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Major Marquand|alt=Major Marquand original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Richard Marquand.png|350x450px|alt=Director Richard Marquand]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Director Richard Marquand</div></div></div>

Marquand".<ref name="encyc199">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 199. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026024957/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Marquand Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref> The lore says he "directed" a counterattack against the Ewoks, a pun on his job.

=== [[Sabe]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Cor-L-sabe-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Sabe|alt=Sabe original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke candidate - Keira Knightley 2005.jpg|350x450px|alt=Keira Knightley in 2005]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Keira Knightley, who played Sabé, in 2005</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-cast-and-crew-nod|Cast and crew nod]] · '''Set:''' [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]] · '''Text:''' "Female chosen as a handmaiden by Panaka due to her resemblance to Amidala."

Keira Knightley played Sabé in ''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace'' (1999). She was cast because she looked very like Natalie Portman, who played Padmé Amidala, and Portman dubbed her lines.<ref name="wp-keira">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keira_Knightley Keira Knightley], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015063339/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keira_Knightley Internet Archive], 15 October 2026.</ref> The lore's "resemblance to Amidala" matches the casting, read as a nod to the two actresses.

== <span id="type-film-in-joke"></span>Film in-jokes ==
=== [[3,720 To 1]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-3720to1-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=3,720 To 1|alt=3,720 To 1 original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "What are the odds of having a Corellian, a Wookiee and a protocol droid together with an Alderaanian princess who happens to be the daughter of the Dark Lord of the Sith?"

The title is the odds Threepio gives Han for getting through the asteroid field in ''The Empire Strikes Back'', "approximately three thousand, seven hundred and twenty to one".<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> The lore asks for the odds of the ''Falcon''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s crew coming together at all.

=== <span id="Admiral_Ozzel"></span><span id="Death_Squadron_Star_Destroyer"></span>Admiral Ozzel and Death Squadron Star Destroyer ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-admiralozzel-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Admiral Ozzel|alt=Admiral Ozzel original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Admiral Ozzel]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-deathsquadronstardestroyer-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Death Squadron Star Destroyer|alt=Death Squadron Star Destroyer original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Death Squadron Star Destroyer]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Sets:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]], [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' Admiral Ozzel: "Leader of the Emperor's Death Squadron assigned to hunt down and crush the Rebellion. As clumsy as he is stupid. Has just failed Darth Vader for the next-to-last time." · Death Squadron Star Destroyer: "Vader's infamous Death Squadron, which blockaded the fleeing Rebels at the Battle of Hoth, boasts the finest captains of the Imperial fleet – and Ozzel."

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Vader calls Admiral Ozzel "as clumsy as he is stupid", then chokes him with "You have failed me for the last time, Admiral."<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The [[Admiral Ozzel]] card has him failing Vader "for the next-to-last time", and [[Death Squadron Star Destroyer]] praises "the finest captains of the Imperial fleet – and Ozzel". All the cards where Vader chokes or kills his own officers are together in the running gag [[#Vader choking people|Vader choking people]].

=== [[Bothan Spy]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-bothanspy-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bothan Spy|alt=Bothan Spy original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "…Discovered the location of the second Death Star. Ambitious. Resourceful. Furry. Tend to die in large numbers."

In ''Return of the Jedi'', Mon Mothma tells the Rebel briefing: "Many Bothans died to bring us this information."<ref name="imsdb-rotj-briefing">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref> The lore lists that line among the species' traits, after "Ambitious. Resourceful. Furry."

=== [[Bowcaster]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-bowcaster-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bowcaster|alt=Bowcaster original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Hand-crafted weapon of choice among Wookiees. Fires explosive 'quarrels' (which look like blaster bolts). Requires great strength to use. Extra ammo carried on bandoleers." Game text: "Use X Force to deploy on any warrior where X = (7 - warrior's power). X must be at least 1. ..."

The bowcaster is Chewbacca's weapon in the films, a hand-made Wookiee gun shaped like a crossbow. A quarrel is the bolt that a crossbow shoots,<ref name="wikt-quarrel">[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/quarrel quarrel], Wiktionary. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260831043557/https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/quarrel Internet Archive], 31 August 2026.</ref> and StarWars.com describes the bowcaster as more powerful and accurate than a blaster, "firing a metal quarrel encased in plasma energy".<ref name="sw-bowcaster">[https://www.starwars.com/databank/bowcaster Bowcaster], StarWars.com Databank. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261014053221/https://www.starwars.com/databank/bowcaster Internet Archive], 14 October 2026.</ref> The card's designers had to explain why anyone would carry this bulky, hand-crafted weapon instead of an ordinary blaster, so the lore gives it explosive quarrels. On screen, though, its shots are glowing bolts like everyone else's blaster fire, and the lore owns up to the mismatch in brackets: the quarrels are "(which look like blaster bolts)". The explanation the card wants and the film's special effects do not quite line up.

The rest of the lore is written into the rules. "Requires great strength to use" becomes the deploy cost: the Force needed is 7 minus the power of the warrior carrying it, so the stronger the Wookiee, the cheaper the bowcaster.

=== [[Bravo Fighter]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-L-bravofighter-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Bravo Fighter|alt=Bravo Fighter original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Phantom Menace film poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=The poster of the 1999 film Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The poster of the 1999 film ''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' "Flown by an unknown pilot who likes to spin a lot."

In ''The Phantom Menace'', young Anakin Skywalker flies a Naboo starfighter, tells himself "Try spinning, that's a good trick", and destroys the Droid Control Ship.<ref name="film-tpm" /> The lore's "unknown pilot who likes to spin a lot" is Anakin. His pilot icon is listed at [[Easter eggs]].

=== [[Cease Fire!]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-D-ceasefire.gif|350px|link=Cease Fire!|alt=Cease Fire! original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - OOM-9 orders Cease fire in The Phantom Menace.jpg|600px|alt=The battle droid commander OOM-9 waves his arm on a tank as shells still burst on the Gungan energy shield]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The battle droid commander OOM-9 orders "Cease fire!" in ''The Phantom Menace'' (1999), while the tanks' shells are still bursting on the Gungan shield</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "The amount of time it takes for a subcommand to transfer to an officer battle droid, and then to the rest of his regiment, is .396 of a second." Game text: "If a battle was just initiated, lose 2 Force to prevent all weapons from being fired for remainder of battle. ..."

In ''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace'' (1999), at the battle on the grass plains of Naboo, the battle droid commander [[OOM-9]] has his tanks shell the Gungan army. When the shells fail to get through the Gungans' energy shield, he orders the tanks to cease fire.<ref name="wook-tpm">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars:_Episode_I_The_Phantom_Menace Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015055429/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars:_Episode_I_The_Phantom_Menace Internet Archive], 15 October 2026.</ref> As he waves the order, shells are still bursting on the shield, and a tank fires again a moment after he gives it.<ref name="yt-ceasefire">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bjCLlsOvKrQ Star Wars: The Phantom Menace (1999) - "Activate the Droids" scene &#91;1080p&#93;], Screen Themes, YouTube (31 January 2022), 0:00–0:08. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027132023/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bjCLlsOvKrQ Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref>

The lore explains those extra shots with a precise, straight-faced figure: an order takes ".396 of a second" to pass from the command to an officer battle droid and on to the rest of his regiment, so the droids keep firing for a moment after "Cease fire!". The game text is the order itself, working at once: lose 2 Force and no weapons may be fired for the rest of the battle.

=== [[Chewbacca]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-chewbacca-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Chewbacca|alt=Chewbacca original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Han Solo says Laugh it up, fuzzball in The Empire Strikes Back.jpg|700px|alt=Han Solo, in profile, speaking in the medical center of the Rebel base on Hoth]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:700px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Han Solo as he says "Laugh it up, fuzzball" to Chewbacca, in the medical center of the Rebel base on Hoth in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Wookiee smuggler from Kashyyyk. Over 200 years old. Top-notch mechanic and pilot. Jabba has large bounty on this "walking carpet." Friends call him Chewie... or Fuzzball."

Both of the lore's nicknames for the Wookiee are insults from the films. "Walking carpet" is Princess Leia's: during her rescue from the Death Star in ''Star Wars'' (1977), annoyed that Chewbacca is in her way, she says "Will somebody get this big walking carpet out of my way?"<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> "Fuzzball" is Han Solo's: in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980), when Chewbacca laughs at Han's bickering with Leia in the medical center of the Rebel base on Hoth, Han tells him "Laugh it up, fuzzball."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref>

The lore says "Friends call him Chewie...or Fuzzball", as if "Fuzzball" were a pet name his friends share. It is not: only one friend ever calls him that, Han, once, when Chewbacca is laughing at him. In the scripts of the original films the word appears only in that line.<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> "Chewie", by contrast, is what Han, Luke, Leia, Lando and Threepio all call him.

=== <span id="Chewbacca_Of_Kashyyyk"></span><span id="Always_Thinking_With_Your_Stomach"></span>Chewbacca Of Kashyyyk and Always Thinking With Your Stomach ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-L-chewbaccaofkashyyyk-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Chewbacca Of Kashyyyk|alt=Chewbacca Of Kashyyyk original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Chewbacca Of Kashyyyk]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-D-alwaysthinkingwithyourstomach-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Always Thinking With Your Stomach|alt=Always Thinking With Your Stomach original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Always Thinking With Your Stomach]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] · '''Text:''' [[Chewbacca Of Kashyyyk]]: "Wookiee scout. Volunteered for Han's Endor strike team. Keeps his distance, but doesn't look like he's keeping his distance. Always thinks with his stomach." [[Always Thinking With Your Stomach]] (title)

Both lines on Chewbacca's card come from Han in ''Return of the Jedi'': "Keep your distance though, Chewie, but don't look like you're trying to keep your distance", and, after Chewbacca pulls a dead animal off a stake and springs the Ewoks' net trap, "Always thinking with your stomach."<ref name="imsdb-rotj">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref> The second line is also the title of a Dark Side card, [[Always Thinking With Your Stomach]], whose picture shows the Rebels caught in that net.

=== [[Credits Will Do Fine]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Cor-L-creditswilldofine-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Credits Will Do Fine|alt=Credits Will Do Fine original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "'No, they won't!'"

The card's lore flatly contradicts its title. In ''The Phantom Menace'', Qui-Gon Jinn tries to buy a hyperdrive from the junk dealer [[Watto]] on Tatooine with 20,000 Republic dataries. Watto refuses: "Republic credits are no good out here." Qui-Gon raises his hand and, "using his mind power", says "Credits will do fine." This is a Jedi mind trick, which makes a weak-minded listener agree with whatever the Jedi says. It fails. Watto answers "No, they won't-a", and adds "I'm a Toydarian. Mind tricks don't-a work on me – only money."<ref name="a15-imsdb-tpm">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Phantom-Menace.html Star Wars: The Phantom Menace script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260216060323/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Phantom-Menace.html Internet Archive], 16 February 2026.</ref> The card takes Qui-Gon's line as its title and gives Watto's answer as its whole lore. Its game text works only at [[Tatooine: Watto's Junkyard|Watto's Junkyard]].

=== <span id="Corporal_Beezer"></span><span id="General_Calrissian"></span><span id="Flash_Of_Insight"></span>Digs at Han, Lando and Threepio ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-L-corporalbeezer-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Corporal Beezer|alt=Corporal Beezer original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Corporal Beezer]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:DS2-L-generalcalrissian-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=General Calrissian|alt=General Calrissian original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[General Calrissian]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-flashofinsight-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Flash Of Insight|alt=Flash Of Insight original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Flash Of Insight]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Sets:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]], [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] · '''Text:''' [[Corporal Beezer]]: "She gets nervous when General Solo tries to hotwire something." [[General Calrissian]]: "Leader. Gambler. Fair pilot. Lando was given the rank of general for 'a little maneuver' at the Battle of Taanab." [[Flash Of Insight]]: "Occasionally Han was capable of such feats, even without Threepio there to tell him these things."

Each lore teases a hero with a line from the films. In ''Return of the Jedi'', Han tries to "hotwire" the door of the shield generator bunker on Endor, and Lando says he was made a general for "my little maneuver at the battle of Taanab", to which Han replies "I just said you were a fair pilot."<ref name="imsdb-rotj">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref>

Flash Of Insight digs at Threepio as well as Han. In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Threepio states the obvious, "Sir, it's quite possible this asteroid is not entirely stable", and Han snaps back: "Not entirely stable? I'm glad you're here to tell us these things. Chewie, take the professor in the back and plug him into the hyperdrive."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> The card hands Han's sarcasm back to him: Han can sometimes work things out for himself, "even without Threepio there to tell him".

=== <span id="Gimme_A_Lift!"></span><span id="Big_Boomers!"></span><span id="General_Jar_Jar"></span>Digs at Jar Jar Binks ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-L-gimmealift-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Gimme A Lift!|alt=Gimme A Lift! original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Gimme A Lift!]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-L-bigboomers-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Big Boomers!|alt=Big Boomers! original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Big Boomers!]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-L-generaljarjar-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=General Jar Jar|alt=General Jar Jar original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[General Jar Jar]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' [[Gimme A Lift!]]: "Jar Jar Binks's courage on the battlefield put quite a thorn in the Trade Federation's side. Many believed it wasn't actually courage." [[Big Boomers!]]: "Gungan weaponry can be quite sophisticated. Sometimes its users are not." [[General Jar Jar]]: "After uniting the Gungans and the Naboo, Boss Nass promoted Jar Jar Binks to General. He's still a bit clumsy."

Both lores praise the Gungans and then take it back, and the target is Jar Jar Binks's clumsiness. In ''The Phantom Menace'', Jar Jar's "courage" in the battle on the grass plains of Naboo is mostly accident: he gets tangled in a cart of the Gungans' energy balls, and the balls spill out and roll into the battle droids, blowing them up.<ref name="film-tpm">''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace'' (film), directed by George Lucas, 20th Century Fox, 1999.</ref> The picture on Big Boomers! is that spilled cart, its blue balls rolling down the hill.

[[General Jar Jar]] makes the same dig with a promotion: Boss Nass makes Jar Jar a general for uniting the Gungans and the Naboo, and the lore adds, "He's still a bit clumsy."

=== [[Dr. Evazan & •Ponda Baba|Dr. Evazan & Ponda Baba]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref2-D-drevazan&pondababa-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Dr. Evazan & •Ponda Baba|alt=Dr. Evazan and Ponda Baba original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Dr. Evazan tells Luke I don't like you either in Star Wars.jpg|600px|alt=Dr. Evazan, face to face with Luke in the Mos Eisley cantina, says I don't like you either]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Dr. Evazan tells Luke "I don't like you either" in the Mos Eisley cantina in ''Star Wars'' (1977). Luke is in the foreground, seen from behind.<ref name="yt-cantina">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPelOnd7Sik Star Wars: A New Hope - Luke Skywalker Enters the Cantina &#91;CLIP&#93; | TNT], TNT, YouTube (3 November 2020), 1:44–1:52. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027142723/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPelOnd7Sik Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref></div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy|Reflections II]] · '''Text:''' "…Gained the rights to Han Solo's old smuggling routes from Jabba the Hutt. They don't like you either…"

In the Mos Eisley cantina in ''Star Wars'', Ponda Baba shoves Luke, and Dr. Evazan tells Luke: "He doesn't like you." Luke says "I'm sorry", and Evazan answers: "I don't like you either."<ref name="imsdb-anh-cantina">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> The lore ends with the same words, but says them to the player reading the card.

=== [[DS-61-4]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-ds614-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=DS-61-4|alt=DS-61-4 original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Memphis Belle crew after 25th mission 1943.jpg|350x450px|alt=Ten airmen in front of a B-17 bomber]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The crew of the B-17 ''Memphis Belle'' after their 25th and last mission, 1943</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' "Imperial pilot nicknamed 'Dark Curse.' Survived assaults against several dissenter worlds including Ralltiir and Mon Calamari. Intends to retire after his next combat mission."

"Intends to retire after his next combat mission" sets up a stock twist in films and television, known as "retirony": the cop or soldier who is days from retirement, or flying one last mission, is the one who gets killed.<ref name="c12-tvt-retirony">[https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Retirony Retirony], TV Tropes. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261014102918/https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Retirony Internet Archive], 14 October 2026.</ref> DS-61-4's game text puts him "On Black 4", the TIE fighter that hits Luke's X-wing in ''Star Wars'' and is then shot down by Wedge Antilles,<ref name="c12-wook-black4">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Black_4 Black 4], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260412090503/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Black_4 Internet Archive], 12 April 2026.</ref> so his next combat mission is the Battle of Yavin, and he never retires. Real bomber crews in the Second World War were sent home after 25 missions, and the ''Memphis Belle'' crew was one of the first to make it.<ref name="c12-wp-belle">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Belle_(aircraft) Memphis Belle (aircraft)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260703174113/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Belle_(aircraft) Internet Archive], 3 July 2026.</ref>

=== Klaatu, Barada, Nikto ===
<span id="Klaatu"></span><span id="Barada"></span><span id="Nikto"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-klaatu-decipher-archive.gif|300px|link=Klaatu|alt=Klaatu original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:300px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Klaatu]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-barada-decipher-archive.gif|300px|link=Barada|alt=Barada original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:300px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Barada]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-nikto-decipher-archive.gif|300px|link=Nikto|alt=Nikto original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:300px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Nikto]]</div></div></div>
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Klaatu and Gort in The Day the Earth Stood Still trailer.jpg|350x450px|alt=Klaatu and the robot Gort in front of their spaceship in The Day the Earth Stood Still (1951)]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Klaatu and Gort in ''The Day the Earth Stood Still'' (1951)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Klaatu in The Day the Earth Stood Still trailer.jpg|350x450px|alt=Michael Rennie as Klaatu in The Day the Earth Stood Still (1951)]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Michael Rennie as Klaatu</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Gort in The Day the Earth Stood Still trailer.png|350x450px|alt=The robot Gort in The Day the Earth Stood Still (1951)]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The robot Gort, to whom "Klaatu barada nikto" is spoken</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] · '''Text:''' Klaatu, Barada and Nikto (titles); Klaatu: "Kadas'sa'Nikto. Barada's main assistant."

In the 1951 film ''The Day the Earth Stood Still'', the alien Klaatu tells Helen Benson that if anything happens to him she must say the words "Klaatu barada nikto" to the robot Gort.<ref name="wp-kbn">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klaatu_barada_nikto Klaatu barada nikto], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009084254/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klaatu_barada_nikto Internet Archive], 9 October 2026.</ref> Lucasfilm used the three words for names in ''Return of the Jedi'' (1983): Klaatu and Barada are two of Jabba's men, and "Nikto" is the name of a species of Jabba's guards.<ref name="wp-kbn" /> The three card titles [[Klaatu]], [[Barada]] and [[Nikto]] spell out the phrase.

=== [[Mandalorian Mishap]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-mandalorianmishap-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Mandalorian Mishap|alt=Mandalorian Mishap original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-sarlacc-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Sarlacc|alt=The Sarlacc]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The [[Sarlacc]]</div></div></div>

In ''Return of the Jedi'', the bounty hunter Boba Fett is swallowed by the Sarlacc during the fight at Jabba's sail barge.<ref name="wp-rotj">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_of_the_Jedi Return of the Jedi], Wikipedia. === [[Moff Jerjerrod]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:DS2-D-moffjerjerrod-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Moff Jerjerrod|alt=Moff Jerjerrod original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] · '''Text:''' "Leader. Found discussions with Vader to be particularly motivating. Does not want to find out if the Emperor is more forgiving than Vader."

In ''Return of the Jedi'', Vader ends his visit to Jerjerrod with "The Emperor is not as forgiving as I am."<ref name="imsdb-rotj">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref> The lore calls the threat a "particularly motivating" discussion. All the cards where Vader chokes or kills his own officers are together in the running gag [[#Vader choking people|Vader choking people]].

=== <span id="Jawa_(Dark)_(Coruscant)"></span><span id="Tusken_Raider_(Dark)"></span>Podrace spectators ===
