<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Cor-D-jawa-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Jawa (Dark) (Coruscant)|alt=Jawa original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Jawa (Dark) (Coruscant)|Jawa]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Cor-D-tuskenraider-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Tusken Raider (Dark)|alt=Tusken Raider original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Tusken Raider (Dark)|Tusken Raider]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]] · '''Text:''' [[Jawa (Dark) (Coruscant)|Jawa]]: "Every now and then, Jawas will pause in their scavenging duties to take in a Podrace. Many believe this is only because they want to be first to a crash scene." [[Tusken Raider (Dark)|Tusken Raider]]: "Tusken Raiders are constantly taking bets to see who can hit the most Podracers on the Boonta Eve racetrack."

In ''The Phantom Menace'', Tusken Raiders take shots at the podracers during the Boonta Eve race.<ref name="film-tpm">''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace'' (film), directed by George Lucas, 20th Century Fox, 1999.</ref> The Jawas, scavengers of wrecked machines, are said to watch only so they can reach the crashes first.

=== [[Princess Leia]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CloudCity-L-princessleia-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Princess Leia|alt=Princess Leia original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Han and Leia kiss before the carbon freeze in The Empire Strikes Back.jpg|600px|alt=Han Solo and Princess Leia kiss in the carbon-freezing chamber, watched by a stormtrooper]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Han and Leia kiss in the carbon-freezing chamber on Cloud City, just before "I love you" and "I know", in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980).<ref name="sw-carbon-freeze">[https://www.starwars.com/video/carbon-freeze Carbon-Freeze], StarWars.com, 0:36. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008223717/https://www.starwars.com/video/carbon-freeze Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref></div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Prominent leader in the struggling Alliance. Former member of the Imperial Senate. Beginning to discover her true heritage. Likes scoundrels."

For most of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980), Leia denies having any feelings for Han Solo. On Hoth, when Han claims she "expressed her true feelings" for him, she calls him a "stuck up, half-witted, scruffy-looking nerf-herder". Aboard the ''Millennium Falcon'' she will admit only that he is all right "when you aren't acting like a scoundrel"; Han answers "You like me because I'm a scoundrel. There aren't enough scoundrels in your life", and she insists "I happen to like nice men." Only when Han is about to be frozen in carbonite on Cloud City does she tell him "I love you!", and he replies "I know."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref>

Her Cloud City card simply states what she spends the film denying: she "Likes scoundrels." The lore even makes it plural, although there is only one scoundrel she likes. Han does offer her a second. When he decides to hide on Bespin with Lando Calrissian, he describes Lando as "a card player, gambler, scoundrel. You'd like him." Leia's only reply is "Thanks."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref>

=== <span id="Proton_Torpedoes_(Theed_Palace)"></span>[[Proton Torpedoes (Theed Palace)|Proton Torpedoes]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-L-protontorpedoes-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Proton Torpedoes (Theed Palace)|alt=Proton Torpedoes original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' "Mainstay weapon of Naboo Defense Fighters. Anakin Skywalker used them to surprising effect, as soon as he found the trigger."

In ''The Phantom Menace'', young Anakin, alone in a Naboo starfighter, presses the wrong buttons before he finds the one that fires, then destroys the droid control ship.<ref name="film-tpm">''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace'' (film), directed by George Lucas, 20th Century Fox, 1999.</ref>

=== [[R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-r2d2-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)|alt=R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - C-3PO and R2-D2 aboard the Tantive IV in A New Hope.jpg|600px|alt=C-3PO and R2-D2 in a white corridor of Princess Leia's ship as rebel troopers run past]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Threepio and Artoo aboard Princess Leia's ship, the ''Tantive IV'', at the start of ''Star Wars'' (1977)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Feisty. Loyal. Heroic. Insecure. Rebel spy. Excels at trouble. Incorrigible counterpart of a mindless philosopher. Has picked up a slight flutter. A bit eccentric."

At the start of ''Star Wars'' (1977), as Imperial troops board Princess Leia's ship, R2-D2 beeps something at C-3PO, and Threepio snaps back: "Don't call me a mindless philosopher, you overweight glob of grease!"<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> The audience never hears what Artoo said, but Threepio's reply shows that Artoo had called him a "mindless philosopher". The card turns the insult around: Artoo is the "incorrigible counterpart" (the partner who cannot be reformed) "of a mindless philosopher", so the phrase now describes Threepio, the [[C-3PO (See-Threepio)|protocol droid]] who never stops talking.

The last two phrases of the lore are Threepio's own excuses for Artoo later in the film. When Artoo tells Luke that the recording of Leia is a private message for Obi-Wan Kenobi, Threepio apologises that "this little R2 unit has become a bit eccentric", and when Artoo then pretends there is no message at all, Threepio says "he appears to have picked up a slight flutter".<ref name="imsdb-anh" />

=== [[R5-D4 (Arfive-Defour)]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-r5d4.gif|350px|link=R5-D4 (Arfive-Defour)|alt=R5-D4 (Arfive-Defour) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[R5-D4 (Arfive-Defour)]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-r2d2-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)|alt=R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - R5-D4's motivator blows in A New Hope.jpg|600px|alt=Smoke pours from the red astromech R5-D4 as Luke Skywalker and C-3PO turn round at the Lars homestead]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">R5-D4's motivator blows in a cloud of smoke as Luke and C-3PO turn round, in ''Star Wars'' (1977).<ref name="sw-bad-motivator">[https://www.starwars.com/video/bad-motivator Bad Motivator], StarWars.com, 0:42. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261007112431/https://www.starwars.com/video/bad-motivator Internet Archive], 7 October 2026.</ref></div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Cheap astromech droid commonly referred to as 'Red.' Purposely blew his motivator to prevent splitting up R2-D2 and C-3PO on Tatooine. Poor navigator but skilled mechanic."

In ''Star Wars'' (1977), Owen Lars buys the red astromech from the Jawas together with C-3PO. As Luke leads them away, a plate pops off the droid's head and it sparks wildly, and Luke calls out: "This R2 unit has a bad motivator. Look!" Threepio then points out that R2-D2 "is in prime condition", and Owen takes R2-D2 instead.<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> The film plays it as a breakdown, and anyone watching would assume the cheap droid simply failed. The lore says the opposite: he blew his motivator on purpose, a noble sacrifice to keep R2-D2 and C-3PO together.

The last line of the lore adds a second irony. He is a "skilled mechanic", so blowing up his own motivator was no great sacrifice after all: he could fix himself later. His game text makes him a repairman too, since aboard a starship damaged by an ion cannon he "restores armor/maneuver and hyperspeed".

The card's numbers add one more irony. R5-D4's game text reads "While aboard any starship, adds 1 to power and maneuver." The [[R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)]] card from the same set, the droid he stepped aside for, reads "While aboard any starfighter, adds 2 to power, maneuver and hyperspeed (3 on Red 5)." The droid R5-D4 gave up his place for is worth twice as much in a starfighter, so on the cards the sacrifice was a good trade.

=== [[Red 6]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-red6-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Red 6|alt=Red 6 original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-ivegotaproblemhere-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=I've Got A Problem Here|alt=I've Got A Problem Here original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[I've Got A Problem Here]] (Premiere): Jek Porkins</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Jek Porkins' X-wing at Battle of Yavin. Instrumental in success of strafing attacks against Death Star. Skipped last inspection of computer and flight control systems." Game text: "May add 1 pilot. Opponent may add 2 to destiny drawn for I've Got A Problem Here when played against Red 6. Must have pilot aboard to use power, maneuver or hyperspeed."

In ''Star Wars'', Porkins, flying as Red Six in the Death Star attack, reports trouble with his X-wing and is shot down.<ref name="wp-sw77">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_(film) Star Wars (film)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261023152740/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_(film) Internet Archive], 23 October 2026.</ref> Wookieepedia describes the cause: his fighter struck debris from a tower he and Biggs Darklighter had just destroyed, began to malfunction, and drifted over the Death Star's turbolasers, and Porkins ignored Biggs's warnings to pull out.<ref name="wook-porkins">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jek_Tono_Porkins Jek Tono Porkins], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260828034322/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jek_Tono_Porkins Internet Archive], 28 August 2026.</ref> The lore ends by blaming a skipped inspection of the very systems that failed.

Red 6 pairs with the Dark Side Interrupt [[I've Got A Problem Here]] from Premiere, which shows Porkins in his cockpit and tells the same story: "Debris fragments damaged Jek Porkins' X-wing, causing a cascade of computer and flight control failures." The Interrupt targets a starfighter after a battle, and the starfighter is lost if a destiny draw is greater than its maneuver. Red 6's game text names that card and helps it along: the opponent may add 2 to the destiny when it is played against Red 6.

Red 6 also has no immunity to attrition. Of the three Red Squadron X-wings in the A New Hope set, [[Red 2]] is immune to attrition < 3 if Wedge is piloting and [[Red 5]] is immune to attrition < 4 if Luke is piloting, while Red 6 has no immunity whoever flies it. It is not the only unique Red X-wing without immunity: the Premiere cards [[Red 1]] and [[Red 3]] have none either.

=== [[Slight Weapons Malfunction]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-slightweaponsmalfunction-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Slight Weapons Malfunction|alt=Slight Weapons Malfunction original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "Han was gifted in the art of understatement."

In ''Star Wars'', Han, having just shot up the detention block, tells the officer on the intercom "had a slight weapons malfunction. But, uh, everything's perfectly all right now."<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref>

=== [[Tauntaun]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-L-tauntaun-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Tauntaun|alt=Tauntaun original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-L-ithoughttheysmelledbad-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=I Thought They Smelled Bad On The Outside|alt=I Thought They Smelled Bad On The Outside]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[I Thought They Smelled Bad On The Outside]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "First native creatures found on Hoth. Roam the icy plains in herds. Ill-tempered and easily spooked. Smell bad on the outside. Trained as steeds for Rebel patrols."

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Han Solo cuts open the dead tauntaun to keep Luke warm in the snow and says "I thought they smelled bad on the outside!"<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The Hoth card [[I Thought They Smelled Bad On The Outside]] takes its title from the line. The Tauntaun card's own lore says plainly that the creatures "smell bad on the outside", repeating the first half of Han's joke as a fact about the species.

=== <span id="This_Is_Still_Wrong"></span><span id="This_Is_Just_Wrong"></span><span id="You_Do_Have_Your_Moments"></span><span id="This_Is_More_Like_It"></span><span id="This_Is_Absolutely_Right"></span>This Is Just Wrong and This Is Still Wrong ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-thisisjustwrong-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=This Is Just Wrong|alt=This Is Just Wrong original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[This Is Just Wrong]] (Hoth): Leia kisses Luke</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-thisisstillwrong-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=This Is Still Wrong|alt=This Is Still Wrong original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[This Is Still Wrong]] (Cloud City): Leia and Luke again</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-youdohaveyourmoments-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=You Do Have Your Moments|alt=You Do Have Your Moments original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[You Do Have Your Moments]] (Dagobah): Leia kisses Han</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-thisismorelikeit-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=This Is More Like It|alt=This Is More Like It original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[This Is More Like It]] (Dagobah): Han and Leia</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-thisisevenbetter-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=This Is Even Better|alt=This Is Even Better original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[This Is Even Better]] (Cloud City): Han and Leia</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-L-thisisabsolutelyright-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=This Is Absolutely Right|alt=This Is Absolutely Right original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[This Is Absolutely Right]] (Endor): "He's my brother."</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Sets:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]], [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]], [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] · '''Text:''' This Is Just Wrong: "'Why, I guess you don't know everything about women yet.'" · This Is Still Wrong: "Han: 2. Luke: 2. Chewie: 0." · This Is Absolutely Right: "'He's my brother.'"

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', in the medical center of the Rebel base on Hoth, Leia, to annoy Han, says "Why, I guess you don't know everything about women yet?" and kisses Luke on the lips, leaving "everyone in the room slightly dumbstruck".<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> [[This Is Just Wrong]] shows that kiss, and its lore is Leia's line. In ''Return of the Jedi'', Luke tells Leia on Endor, "The Force is strong in my family. My father has it...I have it...and...my sister has it", and she answers "I know. Somehow...I've always known."<ref name="imsdb-rotj" /> Leia is Luke's twin sister, so seen from the third film, kissing him is wrong. [[This Is Still Wrong]] shows a second kiss from the same film: on the ''Millennium Falcon'' after the escape from Cloud City, Luke rests on a cot and Leia "gently wipes his face", then "kisses him" before she leaves.<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> Its lore is a bare score, "Han: 2. Luke: 2. Chewie: 0.", which reads as a tally of who has kissed Leia, with her brother level with Han. Chewie's 0 recalls Leia's put-down on Hoth, "I'd just as soon kiss a Wookiee", and Han's reply, "I can arrange that."<ref name="imsdb-esb" />

The Light Side answers with Han and Leia's own kisses. [[You Do Have Your Moments]] and [[This Is More Like It]] show Leia kissing Han on the ''Falcon'', [[This Is Even Better]] shows their kiss before Han is frozen in carbonite, and [[This Is Absolutely Right]] shows them kissing on Endor, with Leia's line to Han in ''Return of the Jedi'' as its lore: "He's my brother."<ref name="imsdb-rotj" /> The game text keeps score too: This Is More Like It cancels This Is Just Wrong, and This Is Even Better and This Is Absolutely Right cancel This Is Still Wrong.

=== [[Transmission Terminated]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-transmissionterminated-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Transmission Terminated|alt=Transmission Terminated original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke candidate - Mirth Without Mischief 1780 title page.jpg|350x450px|alt=The 1780 title page of Mirth Without Mischief]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The first known printing of "The Twelve Days of Christmas", 1780</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "…fifteen system errors: ten computer malfunctions, four power failures and one asteroid."

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', a Star Destroyer captain is speaking to Darth Vader by hologram when an asteroid smashes into his bridge and cuts him off.<ref name="film-esb" /> The lore lists that crash, deadpan, as "one asteroid" among the communications errors, and the title names the cut-off message.

The lore also resembles "The Twelve Days of Christmas", first printed in the children's book ''Mirth Without Mischief'' (1780), which counts down to "a partridge in a pear tree".<ref name="wp-12days">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twelve_Days_of_Christmas_(song) The Twelve Days of Christmas (song)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261001001025/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twelve_Days_of_Christmas_(song) Internet Archive], 1 October 2026.</ref> Like the song, the lore counts down (ten, four, one) and ends on an odd last item, the asteroid.

=== [[Womp Rat]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-womprat-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Womp Rat|alt=Womp Rat original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Death Star thermal exhaust port in Star Wars.jpg|600px|alt=The Death Star thermal exhaust port at the end of the trench, with a proton torpedo glowing just below it]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The Death Star's thermal exhaust port in ''Star Wars'' (1977), as Luke's proton torpedoes reach it.<ref name="yt-port">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MSIDI9JwPI4 Luke Destroys the Deathstar], Rich Cathers, YouTube (17 March 2022), 0:29–0:32. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027142614/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MSIDI9JwPI4 Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref></div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-film-in-joke|Film in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "Carnivorous rodents. Typically found in Beggar's Canyon. About the size of an average thermal exhaust port."

In ''Star Wars'', General Dodonna says the Death Star's target "is only two meters wide. It's a small thermal exhaust port". Luke answers: "I used to bull's-eye womp rats in my T-sixteen back home. They're not much bigger than two meters."<ref name="imsdb-anh-briefing">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> Luke measures the exhaust port in womp rats. The lore turns it round and measures womp rats in exhaust ports. The card's game text also makes it lost if "bullseyed" by Luke's T-16 Skyhopper.

== <span id="type-wordplay"></span>Wordplay ==
=== [[Armament Dismantled]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref3-L-armamentdismantled-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Armament Dismantled|alt=Armament Dismantled original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]] · '''Text:''' "Divide and conquer."

"Divide and conquer" is a saying about splitting up enemies. In ''The Phantom Menace'', Obi-Wan cuts Darth Maul's double-bladed lightsaber in two, and then cuts Maul himself in half.<ref name="film-tpm">''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace'' (film), directed by George Lucas, 20th Century Fox, 1999.</ref>

=== [[Blasted Droid]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-blasteddroid-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Blasted Droid|alt=Blasted Droid original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "'Oh my! Oh, uh, I'm, I'm terribly sorry. I. . . I didn't mean to intrude. No, no, no, please don't get up. No!'"

The lore is Threepio's line in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' as he walks into a room on Cloud City, just before "a laser bolt to Threepio's chest sends him flying in twenty directions".<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> "Blasted" means both shot and, as a mild curse, annoying, which suits Threepio.

=== [[Clash Of Sabers]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-clashofsabers-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Clash Of Sabers|alt=Clash Of Sabers original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Weoww-bzzzzt-bzt-bzzzzt-weoww-bzzzt-weoww-weow-bzt-bzt-bzt-weow-bzzzzzt!"

The whole lore is the sound of a lightsaber duel spelled out.

=== [[Cold Feet]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-coldfeet-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Cold Feet|alt=Cold Feet original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "Wampas pack snow around the appendages of captured prey, making use of Hoth's cold environment to immobilize them."

To get cold feet is to lose your nerve. In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', the wampa hangs Luke upside down in its cave with his "ankles frozen into icy stalactites", so his feet are cold in the literal sense.<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref>

=== [[Crack Shot]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-crackshot-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Crack Shot|alt=Crack Shot original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Imperial recruits are repeatedly assured that small cracks between the plates of their armor pose little risk from blaster fire. Their first day of battle often tells a different story."

A crack shot is an expert marksman. Here the shot goes through the cracks in the armor.

=== [[Despair]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-despair-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Despair|alt=Despair original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "The carbonite froze more than just Han's body."

The lore plays on "frozen". Han's body is frozen in carbonite, and the card's picture is Leia, frozen with despair as she watches. Moments earlier she had told him "I love you!", and he had answered "I know."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> So the line can also be read as the carbonite freezing Leia's heart, and the love she had only just said aloud. The game text keeps the theme: it plays when a Rebel has just been captured or "frozen", and the Rebel it goes on may not add ability toward battle destiny.

=== [[Desperate Times]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref3-L-desperatetimes-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Desperate Times|alt=Desperate Times original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Han shot first T-shirt.jpg|350x450px|alt=A fan wearing a Han shot first T-shirt]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A "Han shot first" T-shirt, 2007</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]] · '''Text:''' "Han's best tactic when outnumbered? Shoot first and don't worry about asking questions later."

To "shoot first and ask questions later" is an American idiom for acting at once, without first finding out what is going on.<ref name="wikt-shootfirst">[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/shoot_first_and_ask_questions_later shoot first and ask questions later], Wiktionary. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251119020417/https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/shoot_first_and_ask_questions_later Internet Archive], 19 November 2025.</ref> The lore takes it one step further: Han does not ask questions later either.

"Han shot first" is the slogan of fans who object to a change in the 1997 Special Edition of ''Star Wars''. In the 1977 film, Han shoots the bounty hunter Greedo in the Mos Eisley cantina. In the Special Edition, Greedo shoots first and misses.<ref name="wp-hanshotfirst">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_shot_first Han shot first], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260924082527/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_shot_first Internet Archive], 24 September 2026.</ref> [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]] came out in October 2001, four years after that change.

=== [[Disarming Creature]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-L-disarmingcreature-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Disarming Creature|alt=Disarming Creature original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-wampa-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Wampa|alt=The Wampa]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The [[Wampa]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "Luke's defensive maneuver put him out of arm's way."

"Out of harm's way" means safe from danger. In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Luke escapes the wampa's cave by cutting off the creature's arm.<ref name="film-esb">''The Empire Strikes Back'' (film), directed by Irvin Kershner, 20th Century Fox, 1980.</ref> The lore's "out of arm's way" drops the h for the pun, and the title "disarming" means both charming and removing an arm.

=== [[Effective Repairs]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-effectiverepairs-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Effective Repairs|alt=Effective Repairs original card: Han working one-handed in the floor of the Millennium Falcon]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "When the nav computer maintenance program failed to auto-repair the hyperdrive, Han decided to take matters into his own hand."

To "take matters into your own hands" is "to deal with a problem yourself because the people who should have dealt with it have failed to do so".<ref name="cam-idiom">[https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/take-matters-into-your-own-hands take matters into your own hands], Cambridge Dictionary. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20201101064904/https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/take-matters-into-your-own-hands Internet Archive], 1 November 2020.</ref> The lore uses the idiom with "hand" in place of "hands". The ship's own repair program has failed, so Han does the job himself, and the card's picture shows him in the floor of the ''Millennium Falcon'' reaching up into the machinery with one hand.

=== [[EG-6 (Eegee-Six)]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-eg6-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=EG-6 (Eegee-Six)|alt=EG-6 (Eegee-Six) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-c3po.gif|350px|link=C-3PO (See-Threepio)|alt=C-3PO (See-Threepio) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[C-3PO (See-Threepio)]] (Premiere): "Has never been memory-wiped... as far as he knows."</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] · '''Text:''' "Ambulatory power generator made by Veril Line Systems to support equipment and vehicles. Slow-witted. This EG unit is memory-wiped and doesn't know its name or serial number."

"Name, rank and serial number" are the details a captured soldier gives. This droid has been memory-wiped and does not even know those. The Premiere card [[C-3PO (See-Threepio)]] has a matching joke: "Has never been memory-wiped... as far as he knows." The qualifier gives the game away: if you had been memory-wiped, you would not remember it, so Threepio's word on the matter is worth very little.

=== [[Encampment]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-encampment-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Encampment|alt=Encampment original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-yoda-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Yoda|alt=Yoda, the surprise visitor]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Yoda]], the surprise visitor</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "A surprise visitor made Luke an unhappy camper."

An "unhappy camper" is someone annoyed or let down. In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Luke makes camp on Dagobah and is pestered by a small stranger who turns out to be Yoda.<ref name="film-esb" /> The lore says the surprise visitor made Luke "an unhappy camper", a pun on his campsite.

=== <span id="Son_Of_Skywalker"></span><span id="Owen_Lars"></span>Epithets in Yoda's word order ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-sonofskywalker-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Son Of Skywalker|alt=Son Of Skywalker original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Son Of Skywalker]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-owenlars-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Owen Lars|alt=Owen Lars original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Owen Lars]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Sets:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]], [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' [[Son Of Skywalker]]: "Luke Skywalker. Son of Anakin. Seeker of Yoda. Levitator of rocks. Ignorer of advice. Incapable of impossible. Reckless is he." [[Owen Lars]]: "Guardian of Luke Skywalker. Husband of Beru Lars. Brother of Obi-Wan Kenobi. Farmer of moisture. Disapprover of Luke's desire to leave Tatooine."

Both lores are lists of grand titles in the form "X of Y", turned on ordinary things: "Levitator of rocks", "Farmer of moisture". Son Of Skywalker ends in Yoda's word order, "Reckless is he", like the [[#Yoda|Yoda]] card.

=== [[Evader]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-evader-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Evader|alt=Evader original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-darthvader-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Darth Vader|alt=Darth Vader original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' Evader (title); "A panic move by Black 2 send Vader spinning wildly from the Death Star trench-ironically sparing his life."

The title is "Vader" with an E in front. In ''Star Wars'' (1977), the ''Millennium Falcon'' returns during the Death Star attack and knocks Vader's ship off course before he can shoot Luke.<ref name="wp-sw77">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_(film) Star Wars (film)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261023152740/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_(film) Internet Archive], 23 October 2026.</ref> The lore says Vader got away, and the title calls him the one who evades.

=== [[Ewok And Roll]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-L-ewokandroll-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Ewok And Roll|alt=Ewok And Roll original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - 1950s Rock and Roll Revival poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=Concert poster: 1950s Rock and Roll Revival, Chuck Berry, Bill Haley and the Comets, at the Spectrum]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">"Rock & Roll": a poster for a 1950s rock and roll revival concert (1973)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] · '''Text:''' "Even an All Terrain Scout Transport cannot stand on all terrain."

"Ewok and Roll" plays on "rock and roll". AT-ST stands for All Terrain Scout Transport, and in ''Return of the Jedi'' Ewoks topple AT-STs with logs.<ref name="film-rotj">''Return of the Jedi'' (film), directed by Richard Marquand, 20th Century Fox, 1983.</ref> The lore notes that even an "All Terrain" walker cannot stand on all terrain.

=== [[Ewok Log Jam]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-L-ewoklogjam-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Ewok Log Jam|alt=Ewok Log Jam original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - St. Croix River log jam 1886.jpg|350x450px|alt=A log jam on the St. Croix River in 1886]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A real log jam: the St. Croix River, Minnesota, 1886</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] · '''Text:''' "Any problem can be solved by the proper application of the principles of mass and velocity."

A log jam is a pile-up of logs that blocks a river. In ''Return of the Jedi'' the Ewoks cut loose a pile of logs that tumble under a walker's feet until it topples over, and smash another walker's head between two swinging logs.<ref name="imsdb-rotj">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref> The lore explains the method as physics: "mass and velocity".

=== [[Fall Of The Empire]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-falloftheempire-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Fall Of The Empire|alt=Fall Of The Empire original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "'Aaaaah!'"

"The fall of the Empire" sounds like the end of a whole Empire. The lore is one scream, as a single Imperial falls.

=== [[Fall Of The Legend]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-fallofthelegend-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Fall Of The Legend|alt=Fall Of The Legend original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-epicduel.gif|350x450px|link=Epic Duel|alt=The Epic Duel card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The [[Epic Duel]] card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Luke had a falling out with his estranged father."

A "falling out" is a quarrel. In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Luke learns that Darth Vader is his father and lets himself fall from Cloud City rather than join him.<ref name="film-esb" /> The lore calls that a falling out, and so turns it into a family quarrel. But Luke really does fall, and the fall would have been his death: far more serious than a family quarrel. The duel before it was a duel to the death in which Vader cut off Luke's hand, also much more than a mere quarrel. In the game, that lightsaber fight is an [[Epic Duel]], the card the game uses for such duels: father and son have just fought an Epic Duel, not had a quarrel.

=== <span id="Friendly_Fire"></span><span id="Unfriendly_Fire"></span>Friendly Fire and Unfriendly Fire ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-friendlyfire-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Friendly Fire|alt=Friendly Fire original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Friendly Fire]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-unfriendlyfire-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Unfriendly Fire|alt=Unfriendly Fire original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Unfriendly Fire]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Sets:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]], [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] · '''Text:''' [[Friendly Fire]]: "Overcrowding in heavy fire zones increases chances of accidentally shooting one's own comrades. Stormtroopers never let accuracy get in the way of victory." [[Unfriendly Fire]]: "'Get the gun! Point it at the deck!'"

"Friendly fire" is the military term for being shot by your own side. The [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] card makes a joke of the stormtroopers' bad aim, and [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] answers it with Unfriendly Fire, the earlier card's name with "un-" added.

=== [[Frozen Assets]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-frozenassets-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Frozen Assets|alt=Frozen Assets original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Han Solo in carbonite prop.jpg|350x450px|alt=The Han Solo in carbonite prop from The Empire Strikes Back]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The prop of Han Solo frozen in carbonite from ''The Empire Strikes Back''</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Cash in William Jefferson freezer.jpg|350x450px|alt=Bundles of dollar bills wrapped in foil inside a home freezer, beside frozen food]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Frozen assets: cash the FBI found in Congressman William J. Jefferson's freezer</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' Frozen Assets (title); "Molten carbonite is released into the chamber and then flash frozen, releasing a blast of air. The subject is instantly covered in the newly solidified material."

A frozen asset is, in finance, "an asset that cannot readily be turned into cash without heavy loss".<ref name="mw-frozenasset">[https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/frozen%20asset Frozen asset], Merriam-Webster. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260429215411/https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/frozen%20asset Internet Archive], 29 April 2026.</ref> In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Han Solo is frozen in carbonite at Cloud City and given to Boba Fett, who means to collect the bounty on him from Jabba the Hutt.<ref name="wp-esb" /> The title uses the money term literally: Han is the asset, and he is frozen. The lore describes the freezing. Money has been frozen literally too: FBI agents found $90,000 in cash hidden in the home freezer of the United States Congressman William J. Jefferson.<ref name="b13-wp-jefferson">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_J._Jefferson William J. Jefferson], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260928170001/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_J._Jefferson Internet Archive], 28 September 2026.</ref>

=== [[Garouf Lafoe]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-garouflafoe-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Garouf Lafoe|alt=Garouf Lafoe original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke candidate - Ice harvesting Massachusetts 1850s.jpg|350x450px|alt=Men cutting ice from a pond in the 1850s]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Cutting ice from a pond in Massachusetts, 1850s</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' "Free-trader who imports ice chunks from rings of Ohann and Adriana, outer planets in Tatoo system. Sales remain cold...due to steep Imperial taxes and bribes."

"Sales remain cold" means that business is slow, and the goods are ice.

=== [[Guri]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref2-D-guri-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Guri|alt=Guri original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - US one-cent coin 1990.jpg|350x450px|alt=A copper United States one-cent coin dated 1990]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A United States penny dated 1990, before Guri's set (2001): "worth every penny"</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy|Reflections II]] · '''Text:''' "Human-replica droid. Programmed to function as Xizor's personal bodyguard and assassin. Black Sun agent. Cost 9 million credits. Worth every decicred."

The lore ends on "worth every penny", the saying for money well spent, with "decicred", a small unit of galactic money, in place of the penny. Guri cost 9 million credits, and the lore says every last fraction of a credit was worth it.

=== [[Hero Of A Thousand Devices]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-heroofathousanddevices-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Hero Of A Thousand Devices|alt=Hero Of A Thousand Devices original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Hero with a Thousand Faces book cover.jpg|350x450px|alt=The cover of Joseph Campbell's book The Hero with a Thousand Faces]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The cover of Joseph Campbell's book ''The Hero with a Thousand Faces''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Left to his own devices, Artoo used his spunk and creativity to save his companions' lives time and time again."

''The Hero with a Thousand Faces'' (1949) is Joseph Campbell's book on the shared pattern of hero myths.<ref name="wp-hero">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hero_with_a_Thousand_Faces The Hero with a Thousand Faces], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261014041037/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hero_with_a_Thousand_Faces Internet Archive], 14 October 2026.</ref> The title swaps "Faces" for "Devices", for the gadget-filled R2-D2.

=== [[Hopping Mad]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-hoppingmad-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Hopping Mad|alt=Hopping Mad original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "'I'm standing here in pieces and you're having delusions of grandeur!'"

To be hopping mad is to be very angry. In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Threepio, still in pieces and strapped to Chewbacca's back, shouts this at R2-D2; the script has him "on one leg, yelling".<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref>

=== [[Hunting Party]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-huntingparty-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Hunting Party|alt=Hunting Party original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "Sometimes a missing person is found by the wrong search party."

A search party is meant to rescue a missing person; here the searchers are hunters.

=== [[Iasa, The Traitor Of Jawa Canyon]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-iasathetraitorofjawacanyon-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Iasa, The Traitor Of Jawa Canyon|alt=Iasa, The Traitor Of Jawa Canyon original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "While on a trip, King Kalit entrusted his credits, sandcrawler and mate to his friend Iasa. When Kalit returned, one was spent, one was sold and the other was missing."

The lore has the shape of an old joke: three things are left with a friend, and the last line pairs them off, so that the mate is the one "missing", presumably with Iasa.

=== [[It's A Hit!]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:OTSD-L-itsahit-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=It's A Hit!|alt=It's A Hit! original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Official Tournament Sealed Deck]] · '''Text:''' "Red Leader fired the first shot in the Death Star trench, causing massive internal damage. The spectacular near-miss inspired Red Squadron to double their efforts."

The title says it's a hit, and it was: Red Leader's shot struck the Death Star and caused "massive internal damage". But it missed the target that mattered. In ''Star Wars'' the shot misses the exhaust port: "It didn't go in. It just impacted on the surface."<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> Missing there leaves the Death Star free to destroy the Rebel base, so a "spectacular near-miss" is spectacular only in how bad it is, and all it "inspired" was another run down the trench.

=== <span id="Loje_Nella"></span><span id="Mosep"></span>Jabba's accountants ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-lojenella-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Loje Nella|alt=Loje Nella original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Loje Nella]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-mosep-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Mosep|alt=Mosep original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Mosep]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Spitzweg The Bookworm.jpg|350x450px|alt=A painting of an old scholar reading on a library ladder]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">''The Bookworm'', Carl Spitzweg, about 1850</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Bookworm grub in a paperback.jpg|350x450px|alt=A small white beetle grub on a printed page, among holes it has eaten]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A bookworm grub eating its way through a paperback</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Sets:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] · '''Text:''' [[Loje Nella]]: "Accountant. Descended from a species of cliff boring worms. Reluctant assistant to Mosep." [[Mosep]]: "Jabba's Nimbanel accountant. ... He knows a mistake could make him the next write-off."

Loje Nella is an accountant who is descended from worms, and accountants keep the books, so he is a '''bookworm''': a keen reader, named after the insects that eat their way through books.<ref name="c12-wikt-bookworm">[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bookworm bookworm], Wiktionary. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260121230029/https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bookworm Internet Archive], 21 January 2026.</ref> The insect bookworms are larvae of beetles, moths and other insects that "bore or chew through books seeking food",<ref name="b13-wp-bookworm">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookworm_(insect) Bookworm (insect)], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260929172138/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookworm_(insect) Internet Archive], 29 September 2026.</ref> and Loje Nella's ancestors were boring worms too. His worms are also "cliff boring", which is the old joke about accountants. Mosep, the accountant Loje Nella assists, fears being "the next write-off": a write-off is a loss struck from the accounts, and Jabba's servants who make mistakes tend to be killed.

=== [[Jabba's Palace Sabacc]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-jabbaspalacesabacc-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Jabba's Palace Sabacc|alt=Jabba's Palace Sabacc original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JabbasPalace-D-jabbathehutt-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Jabba The Hutt|alt=Jabba The Hutt]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Jabba The Hutt]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] · '''Text:''' "Jabba could lick anyone at sabacc."

To "lick" someone is slang for beating them. Jabba the Hutt has a large tongue, so "Jabba could lick anyone at sabacc" also has a literal meaning.

=== [[Joh Yowza]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-johyowza-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Joh Yowza|alt=Joh Yowza original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Bluegrass jam session 2009.jpg|450px|alt=Musicians with guitars, banjos, fiddles and a double bass playing together in a hall]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:450px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A jam session: musicians playing together informally (Wisconsin, 2009)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Yuzzum musician and thief. Singer for The Max Rebo Band." Game text: "When opponent draws destiny, Joh may 'jam' (place that card face down under Joh). Holds one card at a time. If Joh leaves table, place card under Joh in opponent's Used Pile."

The game text puts "jam" in quotes, and the word fits Joh three ways, one for each part of his lore.
* '''Musician.''' Musicians "jam" when they improvise together, at a jam session.<ref name="a15-mw-jam">[https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/jam jam], Merriam-Webster. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260917154712/https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/jam Internet Archive], 17 September 2026.</ref> Joh is the singer of the Max Rebo Band, so he jams when the opponent draws destiny.
* '''Stuck.''' A thing that "jams" becomes blocked or stuck fast, like a jammed gun or a printer jammed by paper.<ref name="a15-mw-jam" /> A drawn destiny card normally goes on to the Used Pile. Joh's jam stops it on its way, and it stays stuck under him until he leaves the table. Only then is it placed in the opponent's Used Pile, where it was headed.
* '''Thief.''' The lore also calls him a thief, and the card he jams is the opponent's. He takes it and keeps it under himself, one card at a time.

=== <span id="Lando_Calrissian"></span><span id="Lando_Calrissian_(Dark)"></span><span id="Vul_Tazaene"></span>Lando Calrissian and Vul Tazaene ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CloudCity-D-landocalrissian-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lando Calrissian (Dark)|alt=Lando Calrissian (Dark Side) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Lando Calrissian (Dark)|Lando Calrissian]] (Cloud City)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JabbasPalace-L-vultazaene-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Vul Tazaene|alt=Vul Tazaene original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Vul Tazaene]] (Jabba's Palace)</div></div></div>
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-tonnikasisters-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Tonnika Sisters|alt=Tonnika Sisters original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Tonnika Sisters]] (Premiere): "Twins."</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CloudCity-L-innocentscoundrel-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Innocent Scoundrel|alt=Innocent Scoundrel original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Innocent Scoundrel]] (Cloud City)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Sets:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]], [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] · '''Text:''' Lando Calrissian: "Had dealings with the Tonnika Sisters – twice."; Vul Tazaene: "In love with one of them, he's not sure which."

The lore of the Premiere card [[Tonnika Sisters]] begins "Twins." and names them Brea and Senni. Two later cards joke about the pair. Lando's "dealings with the Tonnika Sisters – twice" fits two sisters as well as two occasions, and Vul Tazaene, who is searching for the sisters, loves one of them but is "not sure which." [[Innocent Scoundrel]] adds that Han "regretted having introduced Lando to the Tonnika sisters."

=== [[Light Maneuvers]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-lightmaneuvers-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Light Maneuvers|alt=Light Maneuvers original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "Rookie TIE pilots often fail to grasp the gravity of their situation…"

"The gravity of the situation" means how serious it is. The lore uses the phrase for rookie TIE pilots in space, where gravity is also a physical pull, and a pun.

=== [[Lightsaber Deficiency]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-lightsaberdeficiency-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lightsaber Deficiency|alt=Lightsaber Deficiency original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Lightsaber Deficiency]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-lightsaberproficiency-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lightsaber Proficiency|alt=Lightsaber Proficiency original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Lightsaber Proficiency]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "'Ah... Uh...'"

The title turns [[Lightsaber Proficiency]], a [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] card, into its opposite, and the first thing Lightsaber Deficiency's game text does is cancel it. Lightsaber Proficiency says "A Jedi learns not only to wield a lightsaber, but how to channel the Force"; Lightsaber Deficiency shows Han Solo, no Jedi, in the snow of Hoth holding Luke's lit lightsaber, and its whole lore is "Ah... Uh...", the sound of a man who doesn't know what to do with it. In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Han uses Luke's lightsaber to cut open the dead tauntaun and keep Luke warm inside it.<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> Luke is proficient with the weapon; Han has to work it out.

=== <span id="Location,_Location,_Location"></span><span id="Ability,_Ability,_Ability"></span>Location, Location, Location and Ability, Ability, Ability ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-locationlocationlocation-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Location, Location, Location|alt=Location, Location, Location original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Location, Location, Location]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-abilityabilityability-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Ability, Ability, Ability|alt=Ability, Ability, Ability original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Ability, Ability, Ability]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Location, Location, Location book 1996.jpg|350x450px|alt=Book cover: Location Location Location, How to select the best site for your business, Luigi Salvaneschi]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">''Location, Location, Location'', a business book from 1996, the year before the Dagobah set</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Location, Location, Location title sequence.jpg|350x450px|alt=The words Location Location Location over a picture of the two presenters]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The title of Channel 4's property programme ''Location, Location, Location'', with its presenters Phil Spencer and Kirstie Allsopp</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Sets:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' Location, Location, Location (title); "Mudhole? Slimy? My home this is!" · Ability, Ability, Ability (title); "Ben. . . Ben, please! Ben. . . Leia! Hear me. Leia!"

"Location, location, location" is the estate agents' rule that the most important thing about a property is where it is.<ref name="wikt-loc">[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/location,_location,_location location, location, location], Wiktionary. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026175925/https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/location,_location,_location Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref> The earliest known use is a 1926 property advertisement in the ''Chicago Tribune'': "Attention salesmen, sales managers: location, location, location, close to Rogers Park."<ref name="nyt-safire">William Safire, [https://www.nytimes.com/2009/06/28/magazine/28FOB-onlanguage-t.html "On Language: Location, Location, Location"], ''The New York Times Magazine'' (26 June 2009). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251010080717/https://www.nytimes.com/2009/06/28/magazine/28FOB-onlanguage-t.html Internet Archive], 10 October 2025.</ref><ref name="popik-loc">Barry Popik, [https://barrypopik.com/blog/location_location_location "Location! Location! Location!" (real estate adage)], The Big Apple. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260207070113/https://barrypopik.com/blog/location_location_location Internet Archive], 7 February 2026.</ref> Classified advertisements kept using it long before the card: "BUY THIS BEAUTIFUL HOUSE For 3 Reasons: Location, Location, Location" in the ''El Paso Herald-Post'' in 1939, and "THREE THINGS To Remember In Buying Real Estate: all three are Location-Location-Location" in the ''St. Petersburg Times'' in 1950.<ref name="popik-loc" /> By the 1980s it was a chapter title in guides to franchising (1986) and house buying (1987),<ref name="b13-ia-webster">Bryce Webster, ''The Insider's Guide to Franchising'' (New York: AMACOM, 1986), chapter 4, "Location, Location, Location". Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/insidersguidetof0000webs Internet Archive] (item insidersguidetof0000webs).</ref><ref name="b13-ia-kaufman">Phyllis C. Kaufman and Arnold Corrigan, ''Understanding Buying and Selling a House'' (Stamford, Connecticut: Longmeadow Press, 1987), chapter 7, "Location, Location, Location". Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/understandingbuy00kauf Internet Archive] (item understandingbuy00kauf).</ref> and in 1996, the year before the [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] set, it was the title of a book on choosing a site for a business.<ref name="b13-ia-salv">Luigi Salvaneschi, ''Location, Location, Location: How to Select the Best Site for Your Business'' (Grants Pass, Oregon: Oasis Press/PSI Research, 1996). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/locationlocation00salv Internet Archive] (item locationlocation00salv).</ref> The phrase is so familiar that since 2000 it has been the title of a Channel 4 programme in which property experts Kirstie Allsopp and Phil Spencer find homes for buyers.<ref name="wp-lll">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Location,_Location,_Location Location, Location, Location], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260920185359/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Location,_Location,_Location Internet Archive], 20 September 2026.</ref> In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Luke calls Dagobah a "slimy mudhole" and Yoda answers "Mudhole? Slimy? My home this is."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> That answer is the lore of [[Location, Location, Location]], so the estate agents' slogan sits over Yoda standing up for his swamp.

[[Ability, Ability, Ability]], from the later [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] set, repeats the three-word title with "ability", a number printed on the game's character cards. Its game text makes the opponent deploy "a card with ability" or lose Force, and its lore is Luke hanging under Cloud City calling to Ben, then to Leia.<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref>

=== [[Main Course]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-D-maincourse-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Main Course|alt=Main Course original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-L-ihaveareallybadfeelingaboutthis-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=I Have A Really Bad Feeling About This|alt=I Have A Really Bad Feeling About This original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[I Have A Really Bad Feeling About This]] (Endor), with Threepio's line</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] · '''Text:''' "Threepio always tried to be polite to Captain Solo and to keep him from getting hot under the collar."

To get "hot under the collar" means to get angry.<ref name="wikt-hotcollar">[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/hot_under_the_collar hot under the collar], Wiktionary. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251208131733/https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/hot_under_the_collar Internet Archive], 8 December 2025.</ref> In ''Return of the Jedi'', the Ewoks put Han Solo on a spit and fill the pit under him with firewood, and Threepio tells him "it appears you are to be the main course at a banquet in my honor."<ref name="imsdb-rotj">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref> The title comes from that line, which is the lore of [[I Have A Really Bad Feeling About This]], and the card shows Han tied over the fire, so the idiom is also literal.

=== [[Mournful Roar]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-mournfulroar-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Mournful Roar|alt=Mournful Roar original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Roget's Thesaurus entry for Lamentation 1879.jpg|350x450px|alt=The start of the entry Lamentation in an 1879 edition of Roget's Thesaurus]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The entry for "Lamentation" in ''Roget's Thesaurus'', 1879</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "With the thought of losing Han, Chewbacca let out an anguished, sorrowful, lamenting, mournful, angst-ridden, tormented, agonizing roar."

The lore puts seven words of almost the same meaning in a row before "roar", like a list of synonyms in a thesaurus. In Peter Mark Roget's ''Thesaurus of English Words and Phrases'', entry 839, "Lamentation", lists "lament", "wail", "groan" and "moan", and its adjectives include "lamenting", "sorrowful" and "mournful".<ref name="roget1879">Peter Mark Roget, ''Thesaurus of English Words and Phrases'' (Philadelphia: J. B. Lippincott, 1879), pages 350–351, entry 839. Scan: [https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Thesaurus_of_English_words_and_phrases_-_classified_and_arranged_so_as_to_facilitate_the_expression_of_ideas_and_assist_in_literary_composition_(IA_thesaurusofengli00rogerich).pdf Wikimedia Commons]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026175438/https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Thesaurus_of_English_words_and_phrases_-_classified_and_arranged_so_as_to_facilitate_the_expression_of_ideas_and_assist_in_literary_composition_(IA_thesaurusofengli00rogerich).pdf Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref> The card's title takes one of the seven, "mournful". Wookiee Roar spells Chewbacca's roar out instead of describing it, in the running gag [[#Alien speech and sounds|Alien speech and sounds]].

=== [[Moving To Attack Position]] ===
