<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-movingtoattackposition-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Moving To Attack Position|alt=Moving To Attack Position original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - All Harvester products are war products poster.jpg|350x450px|alt=A wartime poster: All Harvester products are war products, either for offense or defense]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">"…either for offense or defense": the Second World War poster that illustrates the adage on Wikipedia</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-captainneeda-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Captain Needa|alt=Captain Needa]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Captain Needa]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "Sometimes the best defense is an insane offense."

"The best defense is a good offense" is an old adage of war and games: attacking keeps the enemy too busy to attack you.<ref name="wp-bdgo">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_best_defense_is_a_good_offense The best defense is a good offense], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026175955/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_best_defense_is_a_good_offense Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref> George Washington put it this way in 1799: "offensive operations, often times, is the surest, if not the only (in some cases) means of defence".<ref name="founders-1799">[https://founders.archives.gov/documents/Washington/06-04-02-0120 From George Washington to John Trumbull, 25 June 1799], Founders Online, National Archives. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250905051215/https://founders.archives.gov/documents/Washington/06-04-02-0120 Internet Archive], 5 September 2025.</ref> The lore swaps "good" for "insane". In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', the ''Millennium Falcon'' turns and flies straight at the bridge of [[Captain Needa]]'s Star Destroyer, and Needa shouts "They're moving to attack position! Shields up!"<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> The card's title is his line.

=== [[On The Payroll Of The Trade Federation]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Cor-D-onthepayrollofthetradefederation-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=On The Payroll Of The Trade Federation|alt=On The Payroll Of The Trade Federation original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Fat Boy in Politics 1907.jpg|350x450px|alt=Cartoon: a fat man in a top hat holds out a bowl labelled $alt to a donkey labelled Democracy and an elephant labelled G.O.P.]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">"He would ride either party or both into power": a 1907 cartoon of a fat man feeding both the Democratic donkey and the Republican elephant</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]] · '''Text:''' "A political agenda is no use without supporters. And in the world of politics, left and right often meet in the middle."

Left and right are the opposing wings of politics. The lore says they "meet in the middle": on the same payroll. Real companies have backed both sides in just this way. In the 1996 United States elections most of the biggest donors, among them Philip Morris and AT&T, gave to both parties, "hedging their bets".<ref name="nyt-1996">[https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/library/politics/1226campaign-funds.html In Political Money Game, the Year of Big Loopholes], David E. Rosenbaum, ''The New York Times'' (26 December 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260625053046/https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/library/politics/1226campaign-funds.html Internet Archive], 25 June 2026.</ref> Archer Daniels Midland and its chief executive, Dwayne Andreas, were among the top ten donors to both the Republican and the Democratic party over the five years before 1996.<ref name="wapo-adm">[https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1996/10/15/adm-and-its-executives-have-been-generous-to-both-parties-and-dole/c6090259-227e-4199-b056-2c14f9e4abdc/ ADM and Its Executives Have Been Generous to Both Parties and Dole], ''The Washington Post'' (15 October 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170828222824/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1996/10/15/adm-and-its-executives-have-been-generous-to-both-parties-and-dole/c6090259-227e-4199-b056-2c14f9e4abdc/ Internet Archive], 28 August 2017.</ref> Cartoonists drew the idea long before: in "The Fat Boy in Politics", a 1907 cartoon in ''The Minneapolis Journal'', a fat man in a top hat holds out a bowl of "$alt" to both the Democratic donkey and the Republican elephant, and "would ride either party or both into power if he succeeds in getting his halter on them".<ref name="b13-fatboy">[https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Fat_Boy_In_Politics_-_DPLA_-_869b9543e1af8c6af5052e2d72ecf880.jpg The Fat Boy In Politics], Wikimedia Commons, from Hennepin County Library (cartoon by Charles Lewis Bartholomew, ''The Minneapolis Journal'', 5 April 1907). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027000859/https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Fat_Boy_In_Politics_-_DPLA_-_869b9543e1af8c6af5052e2d72ecf880.jpg Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref>

=== [[Path Of Least Resistance]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-pathofleastresistance-decipher-archive-opaque.gif|350px|link=Path Of Least Resistance|alt=Path Of Least Resistance original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-yoda-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Yoda|alt=Yoda]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Yoda]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Yoda didn't say anything bad about taking the 'quick and easy corridor.'"

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Yoda tells Luke that the dark side is "Quicker, easier, more seductive", and warns him: "if you choose the quick and easy path, as Vader did, you will become an agent of evil."<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The lore swaps Yoda's "quick and easy path" for a "quick and easy corridor", which Yoda never warned against, and the card's picture is a corridor in Cloud City. The title is the saying "the path of least resistance", the easiest way to go.

=== [[Princess Leia Organa]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-princessleiaorgana-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Princess Leia Organa|alt=Princess Leia Organa original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] · '''Text:''' "Captured by Jabba. Princess Leia provided a distraction for his henchbeings. Waiting for the first chance to escape. Really made Jabba's tail wiggle."

"Made his tail wiggle" is said of a happy dog. Jabba has a real tail, and the line is a mild innuendo about Leia as his captive.

=== [[Rug Hug]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-L-rughug-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Rug Hug|alt=Rug Hug original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Flokati shag rug (Jessamyn, CC BY-SA 4.0).jpg|350x450px|alt=Close-up of a shaggy tan wool flokati rug]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A flokati, a shaggy wool rug (photo: Jessamyn, CC BY-SA 4.0)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "Wookiees are known to be creatures of great emotion and are very protective of family and friends. Chewbacca has come to treat Luke as a member of his own family."

In ''Star Wars'', Leia calls Chewbacca a "big walking carpet".<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> The title rhymes "rug" with "hug" for Chewbacca hugging Luke.

=== [[Silence Is Golden]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-silenceisgolden-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Silence Is Golden|alt=Silence Is Golden original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Silence is golden in Sartor Resartus 1901.jpg|350x450px|alt=A page of Thomas Carlyle's Sartor Resartus with the words Speech is silvern, Silence is golden]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">"Speech is silvern, Silence is golden" in Carlyle's novel ''Sartor Resartus'', 1901 edition</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' Silence Is Golden (title); "Excuse me, sir, might I in--"

"Speech is silver, silence is golden" is a proverb praising the value of silence over speech. Its earliest known use in English is in ''Sartor Resartus'' (1833–34), a novel by the Scottish writer Thomas Carlyle.<ref name="wp-sartor">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sartor_Resartus Sartor Resartus], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260923152149/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sartor_Resartus Internet Archive], 23 September 2026.</ref><ref name="wp-sisg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_is_silver,_silence_is_golden Speech is silver, silence is golden], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260922171218/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_is_silver,_silence_is_golden Internet Archive], 22 September 2026.</ref> In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', C-3PO follows Han Solo through the hangar on Hoth saying "Excuse me, sir. Might I inqu...", and Han puts his hand over Threepio's mouth.<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The lore cuts Threepio off in the middle of the word, and the card's picture shows the hand over the gold droid's mouth.

=== [[Slip Sliding Away]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-slipslidingaway-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Slip Sliding Away|alt=Slip Sliding Away original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Slip Slidin' Away single 1977.jpg|350x450px|alt=Picture sleeve of the Paul Simon single Slip Slidin' Away]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Paul Simon's single "Slip Slidin' Away" (1977)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Luke got the shaft."

The title is Paul Simon's 1977 hit "Slip Slidin' Away".<ref name="wp-slip">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slip_Slidin%27_Away Slip Slidin' Away], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008230229/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slip_Slidin%27_Away Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref> In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Luke lets go and drops down Cloud City's central shaft after his duel with Vader. He "slides to the end of the slickly polished pipe", tumbles out under the city and grabs a weather vane, then "slips back down" as he tries to pull himself up.<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> The lore is a pun on two meanings of "shaft": a vertical passage, and "harsh or unfair treatment", as in "gave them the shaft".<ref name="mw-shaft">[https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/shaft shaft], Merriam-Webster Dictionary. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251229113508/https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/shaft Internet Archive], 29 December 2025.</ref> Luke, who has just lost his hand, has got the shaft both ways. The card's game text can cancel [[Into The Ventilation Shaft, Lefty]], the Light Side card for the same fall, and can make a character at [[Weather Vane]] lost.

=== <span id="Space_Slug_(Dark)"></span><span id="Space_Slug"></span><span id="This_Is_No_Cave"></span><span id="Shot_In_The_Dark"></span>Space Slug, This Is No Cave and Shot In The Dark ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-spaceslug-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Space Slug (Dark)|alt=Space Slug (Dark Side) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Space Slug (Dark)|Space Slug]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-thisisnocave-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=This Is No Cave|alt=This Is No Cave original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[This Is No Cave]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-shotinthedark-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Shot In The Dark|alt=Shot In The Dark original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Shot In The Dark]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-millenniumfalcon-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Millennium Falcon|alt=Millennium Falcon]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Millennium Falcon]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' [[Space Slug (Dark)|Space Slug]]: "Gigantic silicon-based lifeform. Exists in the vacuum of space. Devours small vessels whole. Has difficulty keeping its modified light freighters down." [[This Is No Cave]]: "The largest space slug on record was 900 meters long. Han suspected he had discovered one that was somewhat larger." [[Shot In The Dark]]: "To test his theory that he was not in a cave, Han blasted the floor. He was right."

Three Dagobah cards joke about the giant space slug in ''The Empire Strikes Back''. To keep something down is "to retain in the stomach without vomiting".<ref name="wikt-keepdown">[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/keep_down keep down], Wiktionary. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260616121810/https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/keep_down Internet Archive], 16 June 2026.</ref> In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', the ''Millennium Falcon'' hides in an asteroid cave that turns out to be the mouth of a giant space slug, and flies out between its teeth just before the jaws close.<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> On [[Space Slug (Dark)|Space Slug]], the [[Millennium Falcon]] card is a "Modified Light Freighter", so the lore describes the Falcon's escape as food the slug could not keep down.

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', the ''Millennium Falcon'' hides in what turns out to be the mouth of a giant space slug, and Han realises "This is no cave."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> Han first fires his blaster into the ground outside the ship.<ref name="film-esb">''The Empire Strikes Back'' (film), directed by Irvin Kershner, 20th Century Fox, 1980.</ref> This Is No Cave uses understatement ("somewhat larger"), and Shot In The Dark takes the saying "a shot in the dark", a wild guess, literally, ending on a flat "He was right."

=== [[Stop Motion]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-stopmotion-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Stop Motion|alt=Stop Motion original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Phil Tippett with tauntaun stop-motion puppet.jpg|350x450px|alt=Phil Tippett beside a small tauntaun puppet with a rider on an animation table]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Phil Tippett with the stop-motion tauntaun puppet for ''The Empire Strikes Back''</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' "'Your tauntaun'll freeze before you reach the first marker.'"

Stop motion is the film technique of moving a model a little between frames. The tauntauns in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' were animated by Phil Tippett with go motion, a form of stop-motion animation.<ref name="wp-tippett">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Tippett Phil Tippett], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261005083223/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Tippett Internet Archive], 5 October 2026.</ref> Tippett animated small puppets of the tauntaun and its rider for the Hoth scenes.<ref name="b13-swc-hoth">[https://www.starwars.com/news/hoth-behind-the-scenes Creating a Winter Wonderland on Hoth], StarWars.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260916200326/https://www.starwars.com/news/hoth-behind-the-scenes Internet Archive], 16 September 2026.</ref> The lore is the warning that Han's tauntaun will freeze, that is, stop moving.

=== <span id="Stun_Blaster_(Dark)"></span>[[Stun Blaster (Dark)|Stun Blaster]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JPSD-D-stunblaster-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Stun Blaster (Dark)|alt=Stun Blaster original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-sarlacc-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Sarlacc|alt=The Sarlacc card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The [[Sarlacc]] card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-rancor.gif|350x450px|link=Rancor|alt=The Rancor card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The [[Rancor]] card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] · '''Text:''' "High-tech Merr-Sonn police immobilizer. Magnetic pulse slows victim's voluntary brain signals. Creatures with thickly insulated cerebral cavities are not affected."

"Thickly insulated cerebral cavities" is a technical way of saying thick-headed. The game text names the creatures it means: the blaster may target a character or creature "except rancor or Sarlacc". So the lore calls the [[Rancor]] and the [[Sarlacc]] thick-headed: both are big, dim beasts, not very intelligent, and the pulse that slows a victim's brain cannot get through to theirs.

=== [[Tunnel Vision]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-tunnelvision-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Tunnel Vision|alt=Tunnel Vision original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Light at the end of the tunnel.jpg|350x450px|alt=The light at the end of the tunnel]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The light at the end of the tunnel</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "Han could always see the light at the end of the tunnel."

"The light at the end of the tunnel" means a sign that a hard time is nearly over. The lore says Han "could always see" it. The title, "tunnel vision", means seeing only what is straight ahead.

=== [[Voyeur]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-voyeur-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Voyeur|alt=Voyeur original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Peeping Tom of Coventry 1826.png|350x450px|alt=A carved figure of a man peering out]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Coventry's wooden statue of Peeping Tom, drawn in 1826</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "As there are very few local authorities on Dagobah, peeping astromechs can get away with just about anything."

A voyeur is a "peeping Tom", a name taken from the legend of Lady Godiva, in which a man called Tom watched her ride naked through Coventry.<ref name="c12-wp-godiva">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Godiva Lady Godiva], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261004173758/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Godiva Internet Archive], 4 October 2026.</ref> The card shows R2-D2 in the rain on Dagobah: in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' he rises on his toes to peek through the window of Yoda's house, where Luke is eating.<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> There is a second joke in "very few local authorities". Dagobah has no government and no population to speak of,<ref name="c12-wook-dagobah">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dagobah/Legends Dagobah (Legends)], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260413065857/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dagobah/Legends Internet Archive], 13 April 2026.</ref> so its only local authority is Yoda, the great authority on the Force, and he is the one being spied on. The game text peeks too: the opponent must reveal their whole Used Pile.

=== <span id="Weather_Vane_(Dark)"></span>[[Weather Vane (Dark)|Weather Vane]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-weathervane-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Weather Vane (Dark)|alt=Weather Vane (Dark Side) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card (Dark Side)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-wordplay|Wordplay]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Not a good place to hang around."

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Luke falls out of Cloud City and hangs from a weather vane under the city until the ''Millennium Falcon'' picks him up: "Luke hangs by one arm from the crossbar of the weather vane."<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The lore uses "hang around", which means to stay somewhere, for a place where Luke literally hangs.

== <span id="type-decipher-in-joke"></span>Decipher in-jokes ==
=== [[Out Of Somewhere]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-outofsomewhere-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Out Of Somewhere|alt=Out Of Somewhere original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-outofnowhere-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Out Of Nowhere|alt=Out Of Nowhere original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The earlier Premiere card [[Out Of Nowhere]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-decipher-in-joke|Decipher in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "When the ghost-like image of Obi-Wan failed to appear, another came out of the light to rescue Luke."

The title is a play on the earlier Premiere card [[Out Of Nowhere]]. That card's lore is about starships hidden from sensors so they can strike out of nowhere; here help comes "out of somewhere", and the lore names the place: "out of the light".

=== [[Rycar's Run]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-rycarsrun-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Rycar's Run|alt=Rycar's Run original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-rycarryjerd-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Rycar Ryjerd|alt=The Rycar Ryjerd card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The [[Rycar Ryjerd]] card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-decipher-in-joke|Decipher in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "The infamous smuggler Rycar Ryjerd does this all the time. He's an idiot."

The lore calls the smuggler [[Rycar Ryjerd]] an idiot, as a joke, for flying asteroid runs "all the time".

=== [[They'd Be Crazy To Follow Us]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-theydbecrazytofollowus-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=They'd Be Crazy To Follow Us|alt=They'd Be Crazy To Follow Us original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-hansolo-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Han Solo|alt=The Han Solo card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The [[Han Solo]] card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-rycarryjerd-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Rycar Ryjerd|alt=The Rycar Ryjerd card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The [[Rycar Ryjerd]] card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-decipher-in-joke|Decipher in-joke]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "Flying into an asteroid field is considered to be certain death except by Han Solo, Rycar Ryjerd and the terminally insane."

The lore jokes that only Han Solo, the smuggler [[Rycar Ryjerd]] and the "terminally insane" would fly into an asteroid field, as Han does in ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="wp-esb">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Empire_Strikes_Back The Empire Strikes Back], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261023180200/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Empire_Strikes_Back Internet Archive], 23 October 2026.</ref>

It is also a joke about plot armor, the story's protection of its heroes. Han can pull off the asteroid run because he is the hero of the film, and the plot will not let him die. Anyone without that plot armor who tried it would be "terminally insane" in both senses: insane, and terminal, because they would be dead very quickly.

== <span id="type-design-gag"></span>Design gags ==
=== [[Commander Desanne]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CloudCity-D-commanderdesanne-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Commander Desanne|alt=Commander Desanne original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Officer from Kalist VI. Due to a political blunder, was stripped of most official duties. Relegated to shuttling dignitaries and high-ranking Imperials." Game text: "Adds 2 to power of any starship he pilots. Your shuttling, landing and taking off to or from same location is free. During your control phase, may search your Reserve Deck, take any one Lambda shuttle or Landing Craft into hand and reshuffle."

The lore describes a punishment: after a political blunder, Desanne lost most of his duties and was left flying shuttles for important passengers. The game text turns that demotion into his strength. "Shuttling" is also a game term for moving characters between a starship and a site, and with Desanne on the table your shuttling, landing and taking off are free. He can also fetch a Lambda shuttle or a Landing Craft from your deck every turn. The job he was demoted to is the job the card makes him best at.

=== [[E Chu Ta]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-echuta.gif|350px|link=E Chu Ta|alt=E Chu Ta original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "'How rude!'" Game text: "One of your protocol droids 'insults' one character present, canceling that character's game text for remainder of turn. OR During your battle phase, initiate a battle where both players have droids (but no presence or spies). Both sides add one battle destiny."

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', as the group walks through Cloud City, Threepio passes a silver protocol droid like himself and says "Nice to see a familiar face". The droid mumbles "E chu ta!", and Threepio answers "How rude!"<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The card's title is the insult and its lore is Threepio's reply.

The joke goes deeper than the quote. A protocol droid is built for communication; Threepio says on Hoth, "I am fluent in six million forms of communication."<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The card makes communication the protocol droid's weapon. One of your protocol droids "insults" a character, and the insult shuts that character up: its game text, everything it can say in the game, is canceled for the rest of the turn. The second option starts a battle that only droids can fight, with no presence on either side. Other cards that print alien speech with no translation are in the running gag [[#Alien speech and sounds|Alien speech and sounds]].

=== <span id="Han's_Back"></span><span id="Luke's_Back"></span><span id="Leia's_Back"></span><span id="The_Empire's_Back"></span>Han's Back, Luke's Back, Leia's Back and The Empire's Back ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-hansback-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Han's Back|alt=Han's Back original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Han's Back]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-lukesback-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Luke's Back|alt=Luke's Back original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Luke's Back]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-leiasback-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Leia's Back|alt=Leia's Back original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Leia's Back]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-theempiresback-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=The Empire's Back|alt=The Empire's Back original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[The Empire's Back]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] · '''Text:''' Titles, with pictures of each character from behind. Lore: [[Han's Back]]: "'Didn't we just leave this party?'" [[Luke's Back]]: "'It looks like I'm going nowhere.'" [[Leia's Back]]: "'It's not over yet!'" [[The Empire's Back]]: "'No star system will dare oppose the Emperor now.'"

"Han's back" normally means Han has returned, and each card's game text does bring the character back, from the Lost Pile or the Reserve Deck. But each picture also shows the character from behind, so the cards literally show Han's, Luke's and Leia's backs, and [[Grand Moff Tarkin]]'s for the Empire: The Empire's Back shows Tarkin from behind, and its lore is his line to Leia. The lores are lines from ''Star Wars''; Han's "Didn't we just leave this party?" is said on coming back to the Death Star hangar they had escaped from.<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref>

=== [[Lieutenant Venka]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-lieutenantvenka.gif|350px|link=Lieutenant Venka|alt=Lieutenant Venka original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Worked hard for a transfer to the Executor. One of the many noncommissioned personnel promoted to replace the vast number of officers lost during the Death Star disaster." Game text: "Power +2 when at an Executor site or same site as Tarkin or Chief Bast, or if the Death Star has been 'blown away.' ..."

At the end of ''Star Wars'' (1977) the Death Star is destroyed with nearly everyone aboard.<ref name="imsdb-anh" /> Venka's lore says he was one of the many noncommissioned crew promoted to fill the officers' places after that "Death Star disaster", so he owes his rank to it. His game text makes him power +2 once the Death Star has been "blown away", the game's term for a destroyed system: he is stronger after the disaster that got him his job. He is also power +2 beside Tarkin or Chief Bast, two of the officers lost with the Death Star.

=== [[Lobel]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-lobel.gif|350px|link=Lobel|alt=Lobel original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Powerful magnetic fields in the Lobel physiology make the operation of nearby navigation devices impossible. Pilots claim these fields also produce headaches." Game text: "Subtracts 2 from forfeit of each opponent's pilot at same site. Prevents characters from moving to or from same or adjacent site using Elis Helrot or Nabrun Leids."

Lobel's game text does two unusual things. It stops characters moving to or from the same or an adjacent site with [[Elis Helrot]] or [[Nabrun Leids]], two Interrupts named after pilots for hire that "transport" any of your characters at one site to any other site in a single move. It also makes each opposing pilot at the same site worth 2 less when forfeited.

The lore invents a piece of alien biology to justify both rules. Magnetic fields from the Lobel's body make nearby navigation devices useless, so the pilots of those quick transports cannot find their way in or out. The same fields give pilots headaches, which is why pilots near Lobel are weaker. The headache line reads like a throwaway at the end of the lore, but it is the reason for half the card.

=== <span id="NOOOOOOOOOOOO!"></span><span id="Hypo"></span>NOOOOOOOOOOOO! and Hypo ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-noooooooooooo-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=NOOOOOOOOOOOO!|alt=NOOOOOOOOOOOO! original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[NOOOOOOOOOOOO!]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANewHope-D-hypo-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Hypo|alt=Hypo original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Hypo]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Sets:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' [[NOOOOOOOOOOOO!]] lore: "Sometimes, the truth isn't very pretty." Game text: "USED: If you just answered 'no' to a Hypo question, opponent loses 3 Force. LOST: Cancel Why Didn't You Tell Me? or I Am Your Father..." [[Hypo]] game text: "You may ask one yes-or-no question about the cards in opponent's hand. Opponent must tell the truth or refuse to answer by losing 1 Force."

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Darth Vader tells Luke "No. I am your father." Luke answers "No. No. That's not true! That's impossible!" Vader says "Search your feelings. You know it to be true", and Luke screams "No! No! No!"<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> The Cloud City card's title is that scream, and its lore, "Sometimes, the truth isn't very pretty", is about the truth he cannot accept. Its Lost use cancels [[I Am Your Father]], the line that made him scream. Hypo is the large hypodermic needle on the torture droid that Vader brings to Leia's cell in ''Star Wars'' to make her reveal the location of the Rebel base.<ref name="imsdb-anh" /> The card's lore says the needle holds truth drugs, and its game text forces the opponent to tell the truth to one yes-or-no question about their hand. NOOOOOOOOOOOO! connects the two: a player forced to tell the truth gets to answer the way Luke did, "no", and the question then costs the asker 3 Force.

=== [[Ortolan]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-ortolan.gif|350px|link=Ortolan|alt=Ortolan original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Squat, floppy-eared food lovers. Ortolans come from the frigid planet Orto. Communicate above the auditory range of most species." Game text: "Power and forfeit +2 on Hoth or at Dining Room. ..."

The lore gives two facts about the species: Ortolans love food, and they come from a frigid planet. The game text makes them stronger in exactly the two places those facts point to: at [[Cloud City: Dining Room]], the only Dining Room site in the game, and on Hoth, the ice planet.

=== [[Star Destroyer!]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-stardestroyer-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Star Destroyer!|alt=Star Destroyer! original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Leia's perception increased as she became more attuned to the Force. She attained the uncanny ability to spot objects at long distances." Game text: "If opponent just deployed or moved a Star Destroyer, say 'Star Destroyer!' ..."

The game text makes the player call out "Star Destroyer!" as part of playing the card, a spoken line that is a rule. It is Leia's line in ''The Empire Strikes Back'': as the ''Falcon'' flees Cloud City, she recognizes a new blip on the scanner and says "Star Destroyer."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> The card's picture is that moment, with Leia pointing out of the cockpit, and the lore treats spotting it as an uncanny Force power.

=== <span id="Trooper_Utris_M'toc"></span><span id="Trooper_Jerrol_Blendin"></span>Trooper Utris M'toc and Trooper Jerrol Blendin ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-trooperutrismtoc-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Trooper Utris M'toc|alt=Trooper Utris M'toc original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Trooper Utris M'toc]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CloudCity-D-trooperjerrolblendin-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Trooper Jerrol Blendin|alt=Trooper Jerrol Blendin original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Trooper Jerrol Blendin]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' [[Trooper Utris M'toc]] lore: "Imzig Cloud City trooper and Wing Guard leader. Attempts to protect Cloud City citizens from less reputable members of local constabulary. Never accepts a bribe." [[Trooper Jerrol Blendin]] lore: "Corrupt captain of the Cloud City Wing Guard... Easily bribed. Keeps the peace through intimidation." Blendin game text: "Opponent may use 2 Force to 'bribe' Blendin to not participate in a battle."

The Wing Guard is Cloud City's police force (its "constabulary"), and the Cloud City set gives it one honest officer on the Light Side and one crooked one on the Dark Side. Utris M'toc "never accepts a bribe" and protects citizens from the less reputable members of his own force. Blendin, the Wing Guard's corrupt captain, is "easily bribed", and his game text makes that a rule: the opponent can pay 2 Force, the bribe, and Blendin stays out of the battle. Utris's card has no such text.

=== [[Yoda]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-yoda-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Yoda|alt=Yoda original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-design-gag|Design gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "Help you I can, yes. … Judge me by my size do you? Mm? And well you should not!" and "Deploy on Dagobah I must, but move elsewhere I may, yes. … To attrition, immune am I."

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Yoda often puts the object or complement before the subject and verb: "Help you I can", "Judge me by my size, do you?"<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> This object–subject–verb order is the best-known trait of his speech.<ref name="wp-osv">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object%E2%80%93subject%E2%80%93verb_word_order Object–subject–verb word order], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261017150030/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object%E2%80%93subject%E2%80%93verb_word_order Internet Archive], 17 October 2026.</ref> The lore quotes his lines from the film. The game text, plain rules wording on other cards, is written in the same inverted order: "Deploy on Dagobah I must", "Where present am I, battles and attacks happen not unless present a Dark Side character of ability > 3 there is" and "To attrition, immune am I." The lore of [[Yoda's Gimer Stick]] uses the same order.

== <span id="type-deadpan-lore"></span>Deadpan lore ==
=== [[Artoo & •Threepio|Artoo & Threepio]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref2-L-artoo&threepio-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Artoo & •Threepio|alt=Artoo & Threepio original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Heroes trapped in the Death Star trash compactor in A New Hope.jpg|600px|alt=Leia, Luke, Han and Chewbacca standing in murky water among garbage in the Death Star's garbage masher]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Leia, Luke, Han and Chewbacca trapped in the Death Star's garbage masher in ''Star Wars'' (1977)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - R2-D2 plugged into the Death Star computer in A New Hope.jpg|600px|alt=R2-D2 with his computer arm plugged into a wall socket on the Death Star]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Artoo plugged into the Death Star's computer, from which he shuts the garbage mashers down</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - R2-D2 lays a smoke screen on Cloud City in The Empire Strikes Back.jpg|600px|alt=R2-D2 sprays a cloud of white smoke in a Cloud City corridor as stormtroopers come up behind]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Artoo lays a smoke screen to cover the escape from Cloud City in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - R2-D2 repairs the Queen's ship in The Phantom Menace.jpg|600px|alt=R2-D2 on the hull of the silver Naboo royal starship as an explosion bursts nearby]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Artoo repairs Queen Amidala's ship under fire at the blockade of Naboo in ''The Phantom Menace'' (1999)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy|Reflections II]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Threepio's extensive experience 'talking' to the ''Falcon''<nowiki/>'s computer allowed him to pilot the freighter while on Coruscant. Artoo, an R-unit droid, provided moral support." Game text: "May pilot only ''Falcon''. ..."

The lore gives the credit to the wrong droid. R2-D2 is an astromech, a repair droid built to work on and help fly starships, and in the films he is the one who gets the heroes out of trouble again and again, while C-3PO, a protocol droid made for etiquette and translation, mostly worries. Even Threepio's "talking" to the ''Millennium Falcon'' goes badly: in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980) he whistles at its control panel, sighs "Oh, where is Artoo when I need him?", and reports that the ship "has the most peculiar dialect".<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> Yet the card says Threepio flew the ''Falcon'' and Artoo only "provided moral support".

What Artoo actually does in the films:
* '''The Death Star garbage masher''' (''Star Wars'', 1977). Artoo plugs into the battle station's computer and finds where Princess Leia is held. Later the walls of a garbage masher close in on Luke, Han, Leia and Chewbacca, and Luke shouts over his comlink: "Shut down all the garbage mashers on the detention level!" Threepio can only relay the order ("Shut them all down! Hurry!") and lament "Curse my metal body!" while Artoo does it and saves them.<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref>
* '''Cloud City and the ''Falcon''<nowiki/>'s hyperdrive''' (''The Empire Strikes Back''). Artoo opens the doors for the escape and "lays a cloud fog" to hide the group from the stormtroopers. He also learns from the city's central computer that the Empire has deactivated the ''Falcon''<nowiki/>'s hyperdrive. Once aboard, Threepio, still in pieces, scolds him: "You don't know how to fix the hyperdrive. Chewbacca can do it. I'm standing here in pieces, and you're having delusions of grandeur!" Artoo fixes it, the ship jumps to lightspeed just ahead of Darth Vader's Star Destroyer, and Threepio can only say "Oh, you did it!"<ref name="imsdb-esb" />
* '''The blockade of Naboo''' (''The Phantom Menace'', 1999). As Queen Amidala's ship runs the Trade Federation's blockade, Artoo goes out on the hull under fire and restores the power. "That little droid did it," says the pilot, and Captain Panaka tells the Queen that "without a doubt, it saved the ship, as well as our lives."<ref name="a15-imsdb-tpm">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Phantom-Menace.html Star Wars: The Phantom Menace script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260216060323/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Phantom-Menace.html Internet Archive], 16 February 2026.</ref>

In any real emergency it is Artoo, not Threepio, who solves the problem, so "moral support" is a large understatement. The card's picture shows the two droids together in the ''Falcon''<nowiki/>'s cockpit.

=== [[At Last We Are Getting Results]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-D-atlastwearegettingresults-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=At Last We Are Getting Results|alt=At Last We Are Getting Results original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' "First sign that your blockade is going well: the Queen's on the comlink."

The lore reads like advice from a manual for invaders.

=== [[AT-AT Driver]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-atatdriver.gif|350px|link=AT-AT Driver|alt=AT-AT Driver original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Piloting walkers high above the battlefield, AT-AT drivers are protected by 15 centimeters of reinforced armor. Accordingly, they are regarded with contempt by the infantry."

The lore states the infantry's resentment as a plain matter of cause and effect. The drivers sit high above the fighting behind 15 centimeters of armor, while the troopers on the ground have none, and "Accordingly" the troopers despise them. The safest job in the battle earns the scorn of everyone else in it, and the card reports this as calmly as it reports the thickness of the armor.

=== [[Battle Droid Officer]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-D-battledroidofficer-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Battle Droid Officer|alt=Battle Droid Officer original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' "Leader. Officer battle droids contain programming that permits them to adapt to unusual situations. Known to malfunction from time to time."

The lore praises the officer droids' clever programming and then adds, flatly, that they break down now and then.

=== [[Boba Fett's Blaster Rifle]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-bobafettsblasterrifle-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Boba Fett's Blaster Rifle|alt=Boba Fett's Blaster Rifle original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Sawed-off shotgun.jpg|350x450px|alt=A sawed-off lever-action shotgun]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A sawed-off shotgun</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Sawed off BlasTech EE-3 blaster rifle. Although its barrel is a few centimeters under the legal limit, no one has lived to file an official complaint."

In the United States, shotguns with barrels shorter than 18 inches, often made by sawing the barrel off, have been restricted since 1934.<ref name="wp-sbs">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short-barreled_shotgun Short-barreled shotgun], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260908150746/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short-barreled_shotgun Internet Archive], 8 September 2026.</ref> The lore gives Boba Fett's "sawed off" rifle the same kind of legal limit, then ends with the deadpan point that nobody it was used on has lived to complain.

=== [[Caller (Dark)|Caller]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-caller-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Caller (Dark)|alt=Caller (Dark Side) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card (Dark Side)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-caller-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Caller|alt=Caller (Light Side) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The Light Side [[Caller]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Cracken's Rebel Field Guide cover.jpg|350x450px|alt=Cover of Cracken's Rebel Field Guide, a 1991 Star Wars roleplaying sourcebook]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide'' (West End Games, 1991), which lists a "Restraining Bolt & Owner"</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] · '''Text:''' "…Used throughout the galaxy. Also called 'owners.'" (Dark Side) · "…Used by many species. Also called “restraining bolt activators.”" (Light Side)

A caller is the hand-held remote for a droid's [[Restraining Bolt|restraining bolt]]: the droid has to obey whoever holds it. The Light Side card gives its other name as the plain, technical "restraining bolt activators". The Dark Side card says callers are "also called 'owners'", naming the device after the person holding it: on the Dark Side, holding the remote is what makes you the droid's owner. Its game text fits that reading, letting an Imperial or a [[Jawa]] steal a droid that is under a Restraining Bolt, and its picture is a hooded Jawa with a caller. In ''Star Wars'' the Jawas sell R2-D2 and C-3PO to the Lars family, and the film keeps asking who owns R2: Luke thinks he "might have been stolen", Uncle Owen says "It belongs to us now", Threepio tells R2 "Master Luke here is your rightful owner", and Ben says he doesn't "remember ever owning a droid".<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref>

The name was not made up for the card. West End Games' ''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide'' (1991), a sourcebook for ''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', already lists the device as a "Restraining Bolt & Owner", and Wookieepedia records "owner" as one of the caller's names from that book.<ref name="sparks-owner">[http://sparks.wikidot.com/owner-equipment Owner Equipment], Sparks, transcribing ''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide'' (West End Games, 1991), p. 16. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260513162852/http://sparks.wikidot.com/owner-equipment Internet Archive], 13 May 2026.</ref><ref name="wook-caller">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Droid_caller/Legends Droid caller (Legends)], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260721021020/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Droid_caller/Legends Internet Archive], 21 July 2026.</ref> The Dark Side lore repeats that name; the joke is what it says about whoever is holding the caller.

The lore ends by ranking the Gungan captain like a sportsman, "in the top ten" of a contest called the "Big Nasty Free-For-All", which sounds like a brawl.

=== <span id="Concussion_Grenade"></span><span id="Bossk's_Mortar_Gun"></span><span id="Bossk.27s_Mortar_Gun"></span>Concussion Grenade and Bossk's Mortar Gun ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-L-concussiongrenade-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Concussion Grenade|alt=Concussion Grenade original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Concussion Grenade]] (Hoth)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-bossksmortargun-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bossk's Mortar Gun|alt=Bossk's Mortar Gun original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Bossk's Mortar Gun]] (Dagobah)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Sets:''' [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]], [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' Concussion Grenade: "Mier-Lan V-59 grenade. Blows stuff up." · Bossk's Mortar Gun: "Relby-v10 micro grenade launcher. Modified version of the limited range CSPL 'Caspel' Projectile Launcher. Blows lots of stuff up."

Both lores open with a weapon's model name and technical detail, then sum the weapon up in three plain words. The Hoth grenade "Blows stuff up." Bossk's bigger launcher, from Dagobah, "Blows lots of stuff up."

=== [[Dianoga]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-dianoga.gif|350px|link=Dianoga|alt=Dianoga original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "'Garbage squid' from Vodran's jungles. Changes color to match last meal. When unfed, turns transparent. Eats almost anything. Flexible eyestalk. 7 tentacles. Up to 6 meters long." Game text: "Ferocity = (power/ferocity of last character or creature eaten) + destiny. ..."

The dianoga is the creature in the Death Star's garbage masher in ''Star Wars'' that wraps a tentacle around Luke's throat and drags him under.<ref name="imsdb-anh" /> The lore reads like a field guide, and slips in that it "changes color to match last meal" and "when unfed, turns transparent", so you could tell what it last ate by looking at it. The game text keeps the same record: its ferocity is the power or ferocity of the last character or creature it ate, plus destiny.

=== [[Dodge]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-dodge-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Dodge|alt=Dodge original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>

In the duel on Cloud City in ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Vader knocks Luke off balance and Luke "rolls down the stairs to the circular carbon-freezing platform".<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> Vader is Luke's father, so the lore treats it as bad parenting.

The pilots of the "Incident at Anoat" are remembered as a lesson in what not to do, and "posthumously" tells the reader they did not survive it.

=== [[Feltipern Trevagg's Stun Rifle]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-feltiperntrevaggsstunrifle.gif|350px|link=Feltipern Trevagg's Stun Rifle|alt=Feltipern Trevagg's Stun Rifle original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-feltiperntrevagg-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Feltipern Trevagg|alt=Feltipern Trevagg original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Feltipern Trevagg]] (Premiere)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "Assault rifle modified by Feltipern. Used by the Gotal bounty hunter before he became a tax collector. Occasionally brought along to 'ease' Feltipern's collection duties."

The Premiere card [[Feltipern Trevagg]] calls him a "Corrupt tax collector" and a bounty hunter. His old bounty-hunting rifle now comes along on tax rounds, and the quotation marks around "ease" say what it is really for: people pay their taxes faster when the collector is carrying an assault rifle.

=== <span id="Gamorrean_Guard"></span><span id="Thok_&_Thug"></span><span id="Thok_.26_Thug"></span>Gamorrean Guard and Thok & Thug ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-gamorreanguard-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Gamorrean Guard|alt=Gamorrean Guard original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Gamorrean Guard]] (Jabba's Palace)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref3-D-thok&thug-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Thok & Thug|alt=Thok & Thug original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Thok & Thug]] (Reflections III)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - MASH Check-Up 1974.jpg|350x450px|alt=A frame from the M*A*S*H episode Check-Up]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">''M*A*S*H'', "Check-Up" (1974): Trapper, holding his X-ray, moments after Hawkeye's "big, strong, dumb, silent types" line</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke candidate - Gamorrean Guard costume 2007.jpg|350x450px|alt=A fan dressed as a Gamorrean Guard]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A fan dressed as a Gamorrean Guard, 2007</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Sets:''' [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]], [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]] · '''Text:''' Gamorrean Guard: "Big. Strong. Dumb." · Thok & Thug: "Jabba the Hutt knew that having a big, strong, dumb guard was good, but having lots of them is better."

The whole lore of [[Gamorrean Guard]] is three one-word sentences. Gamorreans guard Jabba's palace in ''Return of the Jedi''. The lore echoes a line from the ''M*A*S*H'' episode "Check-Up" (season 3, episode 7, first aired on CBS on 22 October 1974), in which Hawkeye tells Trapper: "You big, strong, dumb, silent types can't handle the tension."<ref name="mash-checkup">[https://mash.fandom.com/wiki/Check-Up_(TV_series_episode) Check-Up (TV series episode)], M*A*S*H Wiki. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250720000616/https://mash.fandom.com/wiki/Check-Up_(TV_series_episode) Internet Archive], 20 July 2025.</ref><ref name="ss-checkup">[https://www.springfieldspringfield.co.uk/view_episode_scripts.php?episode=s03e07&tv-show=mash M*A*S*H s03e07 episode script], Springfield! Springfield!. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251016212200/https://www.springfieldspringfield.co.uk/view_episode_scripts.php?episode=s03e07&tv-show=mash Internet Archive], 16 October 2025.</ref>

[[Thok & Thug]], from [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]] (2001), puts the same three words into one phrase, "a big, strong, dumb guard", on a card with two Gamorrean guards.

The Premiere card [[Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi]] shows the hologram.

=== [[Interrogation Array]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-interrogationarray-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Interrogation Array|alt=Interrogation Array original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Galileo before the Holy Office 1847.jpg|350x450px|alt=Galileo standing before the cardinals of the Inquisition]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">''Galileo before the Holy Office'', Joseph-Nicolas Robert-Fleury, 1847</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Torture rack so visually frightening it sometimes yields the desired results without even being switched on."

The joke is that the machine works without being used: one look at it and prisoners spill everything. Real courts relied on the same thing. In early modern Europe, a prisoner could be taken into the torture chamber and shown the instruments, a step called ''territio realis'', in the hope that fear alone would bring a confession before any torture began.<ref name="c12-wp-torturechamber">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torture_chamber Torture chamber], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261001183140/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torture_chamber Internet Archive], 1 October 2026.</ref> Galileo was questioned by the Inquisition in 1633 under the threat of torture, and recanted.<ref name="c12-wp-galileo">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_affair Galileo affair], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015074558/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_affair Internet Archive], 15 October 2026.</ref>

=== [[Leia, Rebel Princess]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref3-L-leiarebelprincess.gif|350px|link=Leia, Rebel Princess|alt=Leia, Rebel Princess original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]] · '''Text:''' "After attracting Luke's attention and then Han's attention, Leia should not have been surprised when she got more attention than desired from Jabba."

The lore counts Leia's admirers in film order, Luke and then Han, and adds Jabba as the third. In ''Return of the Jedi'', Jabba catches Leia after she frees Han from carbonite and keeps her chained beside his throne.<ref name="imsdb-rotj" /> The lore calls that "more attention than desired", and says she "should not have been surprised".

=== <span id="This_Is_Even_Better"></span><span id="Weapon_Levitation"></span>Lists of what went wrong ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-thisisevenbetter-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=This Is Even Better|alt=This Is Even Better original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[This Is Even Better]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-weaponlevitation-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Weapon Levitation|alt=Weapon Levitation original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Weapon Levitation]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' [[This Is Even Better]]: "It took escape from Hoth, asteroids, slugs, capture, refreshments with Vader, torture, and the inevitable carbon-freezing to get Leia to reveal her true feelings for Han." [[Weapon Levitation]]: "Vader confiscated Han's blaster, his ship, his Wookiee, his girl and his only hope of escape."

Both lores sum up ''The Empire Strikes Back'' as a list, like [[#Haven|Haven]]. "Refreshments with Vader" is Lando's invitation on Cloud City, "Will you join me for a little refreshment?", which leads into the dining room where Darth Vader is waiting; there Han's blaster "zips into Vader's hand", the moment Weapon Levitation is named for.<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> Its lore then lists everything Han loses, from his blaster to "his girl".

=== [[Lord Vader]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:DS2-D-lordvader-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lord Vader|alt=Lord Vader original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-apologyaccepted-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Apology Accepted|alt=Apology Accepted original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Apology Accepted]] (Dagobah)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:DS2-D-moffjerjerrod-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Moff Jerjerrod|alt=Moff Jerjerrod original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Moff Jerjerrod]] (Death Star II)</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] · '''Text:''' "Forgiving administrator of Imperial policy."

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Vader tells Admiral Ozzel "You have failed me for the last time" as he chokes him, and answers Captain Needa's apology with "Apology accepted, Captain Needa" as Needa chokes to death.<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The lore calls him "forgiving" with a straight face. Other cards play on the same word: [[Apology Accepted]] says "Needa discovered that Vader was only slightly more forgiving than the Emperor", and [[Moff Jerjerrod]], from the same set as Lord Vader, "Does not want to find out if the Emperor is more forgiving than Vader." See also [[#Admiral Ozzel|Admiral Ozzel]]. All the cards where Vader chokes or kills his own officers are together in the running gag [[#Vader choking people|Vader choking people]].

=== [[Nien Nunb]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:DS2-L-niennunb-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Nien Nunb|alt=Nien Nunb original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] · '''Text:''' "Brilliant navigator. Former SoroSuub employee. Turned to pirating when that corporation backed the Empire. Tall for a Sullustan."

After a serious biography, the lore ends on a backhanded compliment: "Tall for a Sullustan."

=== <span id="Lieutenant_Cecius"></span><span id="Uutkik"></span><span id="Danz_Borin"></span><span id="Chevin"></span><span id="Weequay_Hunter"></span><span id="SSA-306"></span>One-line put-downs ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-lieutenantcecius-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lieutenant Cecius|alt=Lieutenant Cecius original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Lieutenant Cecius]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-uutkik-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Uutkik|alt=Uutkik original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Uutkik]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-danzborin-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Danz Borin|alt=Danz Borin original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Danz Borin]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-chevin-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Chevin|alt=Chevin original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Chevin]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-weequayhunter-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Weequay Hunter|alt=Weequay Hunter original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Weequay Hunter]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-D-ssa306-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=SSA-306|alt=SSA-306 original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[SSA-306]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Sets:''' [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]], [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]], [[Special Edition]], [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' [[Lieutenant Cecius]]: "Hasn't had a date in years." [[Uutkik]]: "Het Nkik's ugliest cousin." [[Danz Borin]]: "To his companions' delight, he's nearly as good as he boasts." [[Chevin]]: "Wear clothing only because others do." [[Weequay Hunter]]: "Tusken Raiders tend not to appreciate this." [[SSA-306]]: "His shift can only be ended by a blaster shot."

Each lore reads like an ordinary character sketch and then ends on a dry one-line dig. Lieutenant Cecius's service record ends on his love life. Uutkik is a hooded Jawa, so his face is never seen, yet he is called the ugliest of [[Het Nkik]]'s cousins. Danz Borin's boasting is only "nearly" true. The Weequay hunters capture banthas, the animals Tusken Raiders ride, to sacrifice them, and the battle droid SSA-306 can only go off duty by being shot.

=== [[Prepare The Chamber]] ===
