<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-preparethechamber-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Prepare The Chamber|alt=Prepare The Chamber original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] · '''Text:''' "Coolant emitted by the TCF32 Carbonite Encasement Apparatus is rumored to have a mildly euphoric effect on Ugnaughts. Individuals on TCF32 duty are regarded with envy."

The carbon-freezing chamber that freezes Han is described as a coveted posting: its coolant is rumored to make Ugnaughts mildly euphoric, so the workers on duty there are envied. The title matches the stage direction for the scene in the script of ''The Empire Strikes Back'': "Six Ugnaughts frantically prepare the chamber for use."<ref name="imsdb-esb" />

=== [[Sacrifice]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-sacrifice-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Sacrifice|alt=Sacrifice original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "Jabba's minions could be expected to be sacrificed to save the Hutt, to destroy one of the Hutt's enemies or to provide the Hutt and his minions with a good laugh."

The list of reasons for dying for Jabba ends with entertainment.

=== <span id="Senate_Hovercam_(Dark)"></span>[[Senate Hovercam]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-L-senatehovercam.gif|350px|link=Senate Hovercam|alt=Senate Hovercam (Light Side) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Senate Hovercam]] (Light)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-D-senatehovercam.gif|350px|link=Senate Hovercam (Dark)|alt=Senate Hovercam (Dark Side) original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Senate Hovercam (Dark)]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' [[Senate Hovercam]]: "Senate hovercams report back to Chancellor Valorum at the conclusion of a Senate session. Mysteriously, the droid monitoring Amidala in the Senate never reported back." [[Senate Hovercam (Dark)]]: "Used to monitor and record events inside the Galactic Senate. By law, hovercams are required to be present in every Senate session, a law Senator Palpatine opposed."

In ''The Phantom Menace'', Senator Palpatine persuades Queen Amidala to call for a vote of no confidence in Chancellor Valorum, and Palpatine is then nominated to replace him.<ref name="film-tpm" /> The Light card calls it a mystery that the hovercam watching Amidala never reported back to Valorum. The Dark card adds that Palpatine opposed the law requiring the cameras. Neither card names a culprit, but read together they point to Palpatine.

=== [[Shut Him Up Or Shut Him Down]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-shuthimuporshuthimdown-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Shut Him Up Or Shut Him Down|alt=Shut Him Up Or Shut Him Down original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] · '''Text:''' "Some droids are disliked due to their annoying personality. Several highly publicized berserk assassin droid incidents haven't helped their public image."

The title is Han's order to Leia about Threepio in ''The Empire Strikes Back'': "Shut him up or shut him down!"<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> The lore talks about killer droids in the language of public relations, as if a few "incidents" had hurt sales.

=== [[Slayn & Korpil Facilities]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-slaynkorpilfacilities-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Slayn & Korpil Facilities|alt=Slayn & Korpil Facilities original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Alligator coat ad, Oregon Statesman 1952 (quality line close-up).jpg|350x450px|alt=Close-up of a 1952 Alligator coat advertisement]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A 1952 Alligator coat advertisement: "It's Alligator, of course, and that means quality." ([[:File:Joke reference - Alligator coat ad, Oregon Statesman 1952.jpg|whole ad]])</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Buick Regal ad, Call and Post 1976 (and that means quality).jpg|350x450px|alt=Part of a 1976 Buick Regal advertisement]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A 1976 Buick Regal advertisement: "Regal is a Buick. And that means quality."</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Trane XL 1200 ad, Air Conditioning Heating & Refrigeration News 1987 (quality line close-up).jpg|600px|alt=Close-up of a 1987 Trane air conditioner advertisement, with the quality line highlighted]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A 1987 Trane air conditioner advertisement: "And, most important, it's made by Trane. And that means quality."</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]] · '''Text:''' "Based in the Roche Asteroid Field. Worked with Admiral Ackbar to develop the B-wing fighter. Verpine owned, and that means quality."

"…owned, and that means quality" has the ring of an advertising slogan, as if the B-wing's makers were selling cars. Real advertising used the same form. "The Old Spice Sea Shanty", the Old Spice jingle written in 1953, has the line "'Old Spice means quality,' said the Captain to the Bosun".<ref name="neatorama-jingles">[https://www.neatorama.com/2015/02/20/Jingle-Fever-the-Stories-Behind-Ad-Jingles/ Jingle Fever: The Stories Behind 5 Ad Jingles], Neatorama (20 February 2015). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027131154/https://www.neatorama.com/2015/02/20/Jingle-Fever-the-Stories-Behind-Ad-Jingles/ Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref><ref name="ads-l-oldspice">[https://listserv.linguistlist.org/pipermail/ads-l/2018-August/152427.html 21st-Century Advertising Slogans], American Dialect Society mailing list (ADS-L), 9 August 2018 (recalls the Old Spice jingle). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027124528/https://listserv.linguistlist.org/pipermail/ads-l/2018-August/152427.html Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref> A 1952 newspaper advertisement for Alligator coats, placed by The Man's Shop of Salem, Oregon, says "It's Alligator, of course, and that means quality."<ref name="statesman-1952">[https://oregonnews.uoregon.edu/lccn/sn85042470/1952-10-10/ed-1/seq-4/ocr/ ''The Oregon Statesman'' (Salem), 10 October 1952, page 4], Historic Oregon Newspapers. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027124604/https://oregonnews.uoregon.edu/lccn/sn85042470/1952-10-10/ed-1/seq-4/ocr/ Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref> Later ads used it as well. A 1976 Buick ad says "Regal is a Buick. And that means quality."<ref name="callpost-1976-buick">[https://archive.org/details/columbuscallpost63lync_14 ''Call and Post'' (Columbus, Ohio), 17 April 1976, page 14A] (Buick Regal advertisement, "You've earned it."), Internet Archive.</ref> A 1987 Trane ad for its XL 1200 air conditioner ends "And, most important, it's made by Trane. And that means quality."<ref name="achrnews-1987-trane">[https://archive.org/details/micro_IA40706924_0238 ''Air Conditioning, Heating & Refrigeration News'', 6 April 1987] (Trane XL 1200 advertisement), Internet Archive.</ref>

=== [[SSA-1015]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Theed-D-ssa1015.gif|350px|link=SSA-1015|alt=SSA-1015 original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Theed Palace]] · '''Text:''' "Security battle droid whose programming assured him a Jedi could be subdued. Supposed to be designated SSA-101, but a mistake in production pushed him back to 1015."

The droid's long number is explained as a factory slip: he should have been SSA-101, and a stray digit "pushed him back" to 1015, as if a bigger serial number were a demotion. The first sentence has its own joke: his programming "assured him" a Jedi could be subdued.

=== [[Thrown Back]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Cor-L-thrownback-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Thrown Back|alt=Thrown Back original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]] · '''Text:''' "Being sent to dispose of two Jedi is the battle droid equivalent of a really bad day at the office."

Being sent against two Jedi means being cut apart or hurled aside, yet the lore files it as "a really bad day at the office": stressful and annoying, but not life-threatening. In ''The Phantom Menace'' the battle droids sent against Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi are destroyed in numbers.<ref name="film-tpm">''Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace'' (film), directed by George Lucas, 20th Century Fox, 1999.</ref>

=== [[Weapon Of A Fallen Mentor]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref3-L-weaponofafallenmentor.gif|350px|link=Weapon Of A Fallen Mentor|alt=Weapon Of A Fallen Mentor original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Reflections III]] · '''Text:''' Lore: "Darth Maul's complacency in what seemed like imminent victory over the Padawan was his downfall. That, and the lightsaber of Obi-Wan's fallen teacher." Game text: "If your non-[Permanent Weapon] lightsaber was just lost (or stolen) from a site, deploy on your character of ability > 4 at same site. Relocate that lightsaber to this character, who may use that lightsaber, and it may not be stolen. ..."

In ''The Phantom Menace'', Darth Maul knocks Obi-Wan Kenobi's lightsaber down a shaft and moves in for the kill; Obi-Wan leaps up, calls his dead master Qui-Gon Jinn's lightsaber to his hand and cuts Maul down.<ref name="film-tpm" /> The lore gives Maul's complacency as the reason he lost, and only then adds, as an afterthought, the thing that actually killed him: "That, and the lightsaber of Obi-Wan's fallen teacher." The game text replays the scene: when your lightsaber is lost, another of your characters at the same site takes it up and fights with it.

=== [[YT-1300 Transport]] ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-L-yt1300transport-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=YT-1300 Transport|alt=YT-1300 Transport original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The original Decipher card</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-deadpan-lore|Deadpan lore]] · '''Set:''' [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] · '''Text:''' "Reliable and durable. Widely used freighter made by Corellian Engineering Corporation. Sales have dramatically increased in proportion to the fame of Han Solo's ship."

The ''Millennium Falcon'' is a YT-1300. The lore treats its fame as good for sales of the model, much as a famous film car sells real ones.

== <span id="type-running-gag"></span>Running gags ==
=== <span id="The_cantina_band's_instruments"></span>Figrin D'an's band ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Sets:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]], [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Special Edition]]

The Bith band in the Mos Eisley cantina shares two jokes across its cards: Figrin D'an has won most of his own musicians' instruments from them at cards, and he is a better musician and a better gambler than everyone around him, his older brother included. [[Tedn Dahai]], the band's Fanfar player, is in [[#Union jokes|Union jokes]].

<span id="Figrin_D'an"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-figrindan-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Figrin D'an|alt=Figrin D'an original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Figrin D'an]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Figrin D'an]]''' ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]]): "A male Bith. Musician who leads the Mos Eisley Cantina band, Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes. Expert gambler and card shark." The bandleader is also a card shark, and his game text makes a "wager" every turn.
<span id="Ickabel_G'ont"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-ickabelgont-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Ickabel G'ont|alt=Ickabel G'ont original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Ickabel G'ont]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Ickabel G'ont]]''' ([[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]): "His favorite cantina song is 'Tears of Aquanna' (mainly because it features him on Fanfar)." Ickabel's favourite song is the one with his own solo.
<span id="Tech_Mo'r"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-techmor-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Tech Mo'r|alt=Tech Mo'r original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Tech Mo'r]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Tech Mo'r]]''' ([[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]): "Male Bith musician. Plays Ommni Box in Figrin D'an's band. Lost ownership of instrument to Figrin while gambling." He still plays the ommni box, but it now belongs to his bandleader.
<span id="Lirin_Car'n"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-lirincarn-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lirin Car'n|alt=Lirin Car'n original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Lirin Car'n]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Lirin Car'n]]''' ([[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]): "Only musician, besides Doikk, who has not lost ownership of his instrument to Figrin." So the rest of the band, all but [[Doikk Na'ts]] and Lirin, have lost theirs.
<span id="Barquin_D'an"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-barquindan-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Barquin D'an|alt=Barquin D'an original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Barquin D'an]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Barquin D'an]]''' ([[Special Edition]]): "Bith musician and gambler. Estranged older brother of Figrin D'an. Plays kloo horn, but not as well as his brother. Briefly jammed with Max Rebo's band." The gag runs in the family: Barquin is a musician and a gambler too, but the lesser one. His "wager" game text has both players draw two destiny, where Figrin draws three against the opponent's two. "Jammed" is musicians' slang for playing together informally, here with [[Max Rebo]]'s band.

=== Food and being fat ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Sets:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]], [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]], [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]], [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]

Several cards joke about food and about being fat: a dining room that lets in the heavy pilot cheaply and doubles the food, a band leader who signs his life away for meals, a droid who gets spat out because he tastes bad, and the same droid called "overweight". Other food jokes have blocks of their own: [[#Frozen Dinner|Frozen Dinner]], [[#Main Course|Main Course]] and [[#Chewbacca Of Kashyyyk and Always Thinking With Your Stomach|Chewbacca Of Kashyyyk and Always Thinking With Your Stomach]]. [[Ortolan]], whose lore calls the species "Squat, floppy-eared food lovers", is under [[#Ortolan|Ortolan]] in Design gags.

<span id="Cloud_City:_Dining_Room"></span><span id="Jek_Porkins"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-cloudcitydiningroom-decipher-archive-flipped.gif|490px|link=Cloud City: Dining Room|alt=Cloud City: Dining Room original card, turned upside down so the Light Side text reads the right way up]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:490px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Cloud City: Dining Room]] (Dark Side card), shown upside down so the Light Side text reads the right way up</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-jekporkins-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Jek Porkins|alt=Jek Porkins original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Jek Porkins]] (Light Side card)</div></div></div>
'''[[Cloud City: Dining Room]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]], Dark Side card), Light Side game text: "If you control, Blue Milk, Beru Stew and Yoda Stew are doubled. Jek is deploy -2 here." '''[[Jek Porkins]]''' ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]], Light Side card), lore: "Piloted Red 6 at Battle of Yavin. Specializes in strafing runs. Served in Tierfon Yellow Aces squadron at Tierfon Rebel Outpost. Free trader from Bestine system."

Jek Porkins, Red Six in ''Star Wars'' (1977), was played by William Hootkins, who remembered reading the part: "I thought because I'm a heavy guy, what's this word Porkins? I saw all the amazing creature effects they were doing and I thought wait a minute, if they are giving me a name like Porkins, is somebody going to come over and stick ears and a snout on my face?"<ref name="slashfilm-porkins">Jenna Busch, [https://www.slashfilm.com/1457494/star-wars-a-new-hope-pilot-sweat-explosives/ "Playing A Pilot In The First Star Wars Was A Sweaty, Explosive Job"], SlashFilm (4 December 2023). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260208084709/https://www.slashfilm.com/1457494/star-wars-a-new-hope-pilot-sweat-explosives/ Internet Archive], 8 February 2026.</ref> Porkins, as in pork, as in pig: the name is a joke about the heavy pilot's size. Porkins is shot down at the Battle of Yavin (see [[#Red 6|Red 6]]) and never goes near Cloud City, yet the Dining Room names him. The one character the Light Side text lets into the dining room for 2 less is "Jek", the fat pilot, and the same line doubles the three food cards Blue Milk, Beru Stew and Yoda Stew, so he arrives cheaply to a table with double helpings.

<span id="Blue_Milk"></span><span id="Beru_Stew"></span><span id="Yoda_Stew"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-bluemilk-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Blue Milk|alt=Blue Milk original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Blue Milk]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-berustew-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Beru Stew|alt=Beru Stew original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Beru Stew]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-yodastew.gif|350px|link=Yoda Stew|alt=Yoda Stew card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Yoda Stew]]</div></div></div>
* '''[[Blue Milk]]''' ([[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]): "Nutrient-rich beverage common in moisture farm communities. Rumored to have medicinal qualities. Popular in cantinas among those who can't hold their juri juice."
* '''[[Beru Stew]]''' ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]]): "Moisture farmers grow enough food to sustain Tatooine's population. Beru Lars has devised many dishes using herbs and roots naturally found in Tatooine's desert."
* '''[[Yoda Stew]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "'For the Jedi it is time to eat as well.'" In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Yoda, whom Luke has not yet recognised, says it as he serves Luke a meal in his hut, then adds "Eat, eat. Hot. Good food, hm?"<ref name="imsdb-esb" />

<span id="Max_Rebo"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-maxrebo-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Max Rebo|alt=Max Rebo original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Max Rebo]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Max Rebo]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]), lore: "Ortolan musician and gambler. Head of The Max Rebo Band. Signed a lifetime contract to Jabba in exchange for unlimited food." Game text: "Power +2 on Hoth. ..." Max Rebo is an Ortolan, and the [[Ortolan]] card calls the species "Squat, floppy-eared food lovers" from "the frigid planet Orto". Max lives up to both halves: he signs himself to Jabba for life, and the price is food. Like the plain Ortolan card, he is also stronger on [[Hoth]], the ice planet.

<span id="WHAAAAAAAAAOOOOW!"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-whaaaaaaaaaoooow-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=WHAAAAAAAAAOOOOW!|alt=WHAAAAAAAAAOOOOW! original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[WHAAAAAAAAAOOOOW!]]</div></div></div>
'''[[WHAAAAAAAAAOOOOW!]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]), lore: "'You're lucky you don't taste very good.'" Game text: "If one of your characters was just defeated by a Dragonsnake, Rancor, Sarlacc, Dianoga or Wampa, instead of being 'eaten' that character is 'hurled' (relocated) to an adjacent site, if possible." In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Artoo falls into the Dagobah swamp, a bog beast pulls him under the water and then spits him out onto the moss, and Luke tells him "You're lucky you don't taste very good."<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The card's picture shows Artoo in mid-air. The game text does the same for any of your characters: a creature that would eat one spits it out instead, to the next site.

<span id="Oh,_Switch_Off"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-ohswitchoff-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Oh, Switch Off|alt=Oh, Switch Off original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Oh, Switch Off]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Oh, Switch Off]]''' ([[Hoth Limited|Hoth]]), lore: "Mindless philosophy for an overweight glob of grease." At the start of ''Star Wars'', Artoo beeps at Threepio, and Threepio answers "Don't call me a mindless philosopher, you overweight glob of grease!"<ref name="imsdb-anh" /> On Hoth in ''The Empire Strikes Back'', when Artoo whistles a protest at him, Threepio says "Oh, switch off."<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The Hoth card takes its title from the second line and its lore from the first, so the lore ends on the fat joke: the short, round astromech is the "overweight glob of grease". [[#R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)|R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)]] uses the other half of the same insult.

=== <span id="Polarized_Negative_Power_Coupling_and_Through_The_Force_Things_You_Will_See"></span>Hard-to-read cards ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Sets:''' [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]

Three cards are printed so that they are hard to read, two of them upside down and one in mirror image, and each lore explains why. Cards whose lore cannot be read because it is in an alien language are in [[#Alien speech and sounds|Alien speech and sounds]].

<span id="Polarized_Negative_Power_Coupling"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-polarizednegativepowercoupling-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Polarized Negative Power Coupling|alt=Polarized Negative Power Coupling original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Polarized Negative Power Coupling]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Polarized Negative Power Coupling original turned over.gif|350x450px|alt=The card turned over: Chewbacca is the right way up]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The card turned over: Chewbacca is the right way up</div></div></div>
'''[[Polarized Negative Power Coupling]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "Replacement often requires an inverted engineer." The picture shows the engineer, Chewbacca, upside down. Turn the card over and he is the right way up.
<span id="Through_The_Force_Things_You_Will_See"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-throughtheforcethingsyouwillsee-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Through The Force Things You Will See|alt=Through The Force Things You Will See original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Through The Force Things You Will See]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Through The Force Things You Will See original turned over.gif|350x450px|alt=The card turned over: it reads normally]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The card turned over: it reads normally</div></div></div>
'''[[Through The Force Things You Will See]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "One training exercise for a Jedi's apprentice is to invert one's view to see things from a different perspective." The title, lore and game text are printed upside down, and the picture shows Luke upside down. Turned over, the card reads normally and Luke stands upright: a "different perspective".
<span id="Hindsight"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CloudCity-L-hindsight-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Hindsight|alt=Hindsight original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Hindsight]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Hindsight]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]): "'I'm backwards! You fleabitten furball... only an overgrown mophead like you would be stupid enough—'" The whole card, title and picture included, is printed in mirror image. In ''The Empire Strikes Back'' Chewbacca puts Threepio's head on backwards, and Threepio cries "I'm backwards, you stupid furball".<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> The title is taken literally too: Threepio's sight is behind him.

=== I have a bad feeling about this ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Sets:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]], [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]], [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]]

In each film of the original trilogy a hero says "I have a bad feeling about this", and the cards keep adding versions of the line, set after set: "got a", "very", "really", "Artoo," and Yoda's "Bad Feeling Have I".

<span id="I've_Got_A_Bad_Feeling_About_This"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-ivegotabadfeelingaboutthis-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=I've Got A Bad Feeling About This|alt=I've Got A Bad Feeling About This original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[I've Got A Bad Feeling About This]]</div></div></div>
'''[[I've Got A Bad Feeling About This]]''' ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]]): "Han's smuggling adventures in Corporate Sector and Hutt Space put him in many tight scrapes. He's about to be in another." Han's line in the Death Star's trash compactor ("I've got a very bad feeling about this" in the script).<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref>
<span id="I_Have_A_Very_Bad_Feeling_About_This"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-ihaveaverybadfeelingaboutthis-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=I Have A Very Bad Feeling About This|alt=I Have A Very Bad Feeling About This original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[I Have A Very Bad Feeling About This]]</div></div></div>
'''[[I Have A Very Bad Feeling About This]]''' ([[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]): "'Look at him, he's heading for that small moon.' Luke became apprehensive when Obi-Wan informed him, 'That's no moon. It's a space station.'" Luke's line as the ''Millennium Falcon'' is pulled toward the Death Star, one word stronger than the Premiere title.<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref>
<span id="Ng'ok"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-ngok-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Ng'ok|alt=Ng'ok original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Ng'ok]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Ng'ok]]''' ([[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]): "Dejarik hologram of a Ng'ok war beast. Foul temper gives rise to bad feelings." The Dark Side's version in the same set: a hologame monster that gives rise to "bad feelings", with the same game text, word for word, as I Have A Very Bad Feeling About This.
<span id="I_Have_A_Bad_Feeling_About_This"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-ihaveabadfeelingaboutthis-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=I Have A Bad Feeling About This|alt=I Have A Bad Feeling About This original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[I Have A Bad Feeling About This]]</div></div></div>
'''[[I Have A Bad Feeling About This]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "'This ground sure feels strange. Doesn't feel like rock. I don't know...'" Leia's line inside the space slug in ''The Empire Strikes Back''; the lore is what she says just before it.<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref>
<span id="Bad_Feeling_Have_I"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-badfeelinghavei-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bad Feeling Have I|alt=Bad Feeling Have I original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Bad Feeling Have I]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Bad Feeling Have I]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "'Ready are you? What know you of ready?'" The title says it in Yoda's word order (see [[#Yoda|Yoda]]), and the lore is Yoda's line to Luke.<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> Its game text ends the gag for the opponent: "opponent may not play any cards with the words 'bad feeling' in the title."
<span id="Artoo,_I_Have_A_Bad_Feeling_About_This"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-artooihaveabadfeelingaboutthis-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Artoo, I Have A Bad Feeling About This|alt=Artoo, I Have A Bad Feeling About This original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Artoo, I Have A Bad Feeling About This]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Artoo, I Have A Bad Feeling About This]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]): "'He says our instructions are to give it only to Jabba himself. I'm terrible sorry. I'm afraid he's ever so stubborn about these sort of things.'" Threepio's line as Bib Fortuna leads the droids into Jabba's palace in ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="imsdb-rotj">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref>
<span id="I_Have_A_Really_Bad_Feeling_About_This"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Endor-L-ihaveareallybadfeelingaboutthis-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=I Have A Really Bad Feeling About This|alt=I Have A Really Bad Feeling About This original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[I Have A Really Bad Feeling About This]]</div></div></div>
'''[[I Have A Really Bad Feeling About This]]''' ([[Endor (expansion)|Endor]]): "'I'm rather embarrassed, General Solo, but it appears you are to be the main course at a banquet in my honor.'" Han's line in the Ewok village, where he is tied up to be cooked; the lore is Threepio's explanation (see also [[#Main Course|Main Course]]).<ref name="imsdb-rotj">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref>

=== <span id="It_Could_Be_Worse"></span><span id="It's_Worse"></span>It Could Be Worse and It's Worse ===
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-itcouldbeworse-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=It Could Be Worse|alt=It Could Be Worse original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[It Could Be Worse]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-itsworse-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=It's Worse|alt=It's Worse original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[It's Worse]]</div></div></div>
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] · '''Text:''' [[It Could Be Worse]] lore: "After escaping Detention Block AA-23. Rebels found themselves in the trash compactor. Leia pointed out, 'It could be worse.' It soon was." [[It's Worse]] game text: "If It Could Be Worse was just played, it is canceled..."

In ''Star Wars'', Luke, Han, Leia and Chewbacca escape the Death Star's detention block by jumping into a garbage chute and land in a trash compactor. Leia says "It could be worse...", a horrible moan comes up from the murky water, and Han answers "It's worse." Seconds later a creature drags Luke under.<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> The two Premiere cards play the exchange out. The Light Side card ends its lore on a flat punchline, "It soon was." The Dark Side card takes Han's answer as its title, and its game text cancels It Could Be Worse, so in the game, too, Leia's hopeful line is answered by Han's. Its lore picks up where the scene goes next: "Things went from bad to worse when Luke was attacked by a dianoga".

=== <span id="Desperate_Reach_and_Bionic_Hand"></span><span id="Into_The_Ventilation_Shaft.2C_Lefty"></span><span id="It.27s_A_Trap.21"></span>Luke's lost hand ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]

In ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Darth Vader cuts off Luke's right hand in their duel on Cloud City.<ref name="wp-esb">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Empire_Strikes_Back The Empire Strikes Back], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261023180200/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Empire_Strikes_Back Internet Archive], 23 October 2026.</ref> Seven Cloud City cards joke about it.

<span id="Desperate_Reach"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-desperatereach-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Desperate Reach|alt=Desperate Reach original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Desperate Reach]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Desperate Reach]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]): "If only someone had given Luke a hand." To "give someone a hand" means to help them; here it is also literal.
<span id="Bionic_Hand"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-bionichand-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bionic Hand|alt=Bionic Hand original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Bionic Hand]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Lee Majors as Steve Austin.jpg|350x450px|alt=Lee Majors as bionic Steve Austin]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Lee Majors as bionic Steve Austin</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - The Six Million Dollar Man logo.png|350x450px|alt=The title logo of the television series The Six Million Dollar Man]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The title logo of the television series ''The Six Million Dollar Man''</div></div></div>
'''[[Bionic Hand]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]): "They had the technology. They could make it better, stronger, faster." The Alliance gives him one, in the words of ''The Six Million Dollar Man'', a 1970s TV series about astronaut Steve Austin, rebuilt with bionic limbs after a crash, whose opening says "We have the technology… Better . . . stronger . . . faster."<ref name="wp-6m">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Six_Million_Dollar_Man The Six Million Dollar Man], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261026024705/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Six_Million_Dollar_Man Internet Archive], 26 October 2026.</ref> The "$6,000,000" etched on the hand is listed at [[Easter eggs]].
<span id="Captive_Pursuit"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-captivepursuit-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Captive Pursuit|alt=Captive Pursuit original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Captive Pursuit]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Captive Pursuit]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]): "Han could have used a hand. Fortunately, Luke still had one to give." The same idiom, with one hand left.
<span id="Haven"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CloudCity-L-haven-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Haven|alt=Haven original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Haven]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Haven]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]): "After pursuit, asteroids, a slug, Jedi training, capture, torture, escape, a duel, losing Han and losing a hand, Luke and Leia finally made it to the Alliance's rendezvous point." A list of the film's ordeals that ends with two almost identical phrases: "losing Han and losing a hand".
<span id="Into_The_Ventilation_Shaft,_Lefty"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CloudCity-L-intotheventilationshaftlefty-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Into The Ventilation Shaft, Lefty|alt=Into The Ventilation Shaft, Lefty original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Into The Ventilation Shaft, Lefty]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-intothegarbagechuteflyboy-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Into The Garbage Chute, Flyboy|alt=Into The Garbage Chute, Flyboy: the Premiere card the title copies]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Into The Garbage Chute, Flyboy]], the Premiere card the title copies</div></div></div>
'''[[Into The Ventilation Shaft, Lefty]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]): "'Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa . . .'" The title has the shape of the Premiere card [[Into The Garbage Chute, Flyboy]], Leia's order to Han in ''Star Wars''. After losing his right hand, Luke drops down Cloud City's central air shaft; "Lefty" is a nickname for a left-handed person, and the lore is his scream as he falls.
<span id="It's_A_Trap!"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-L-itsatrap-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=It's A Trap!|alt=It's A Trap! original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[It's A Trap!]]</div></div></div>
'''[[It's A Trap!]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]): "Luke's decision to ignore Leia's warning about the trap cost him an arm and a. . . well, just a hand actually." Something that "costs an arm and a leg" is very expensive; the lore starts the phrase and corrects itself.
<span id="Mostly_Armless"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CC-D-mostlyarmless-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Mostly Armless|alt=Mostly Armless original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Mostly Armless]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Mostly Harmless book cover.jpg|350x450px|alt=The cover of Douglas Adams's novel Mostly Harmless]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The cover of Douglas Adams's novel ''Mostly Harmless''</div></div></div>
'''[[Mostly Armless]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]): "One lesson learned in Jedi training is that when you have been injured, don't panic." ''Mostly Harmless'' is a novel in Douglas Adams's comic ''Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'' series,<ref name="wp-mostlyharmless">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mostly_Harmless Mostly Harmless], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008112519/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mostly_Harmless Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref> whose Guide has "Don't Panic" printed on its cover.<ref name="wp-hhgg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hitchhiker%27s_Guide_to_the_Galaxy The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015121621/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hitchhiker%27s_Guide_to_the_Galaxy Internet Archive], 15 October 2026.</ref> The title swaps "Harmless" for "Armless", and the lore ends with "don't panic".

=== Plotting to kill Jabba ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]

Seven members of Jabba's court in [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] have lore that ends the same way: "Plotting to kill Jabba." Two more cards finish the story.

<span id="Bane_Malar"></span><span id="Bib_Fortuna"></span><span id="Garon_Nas_Tal"></span><span id="J'Quille"></span><span id="Ree-Yees"></span><span id="Tessek"></span><span id="Velken_Tezeri"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-banemalar-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bane Malar|alt=Bane Malar original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Bane Malar]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-bibfortuna-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bib Fortuna|alt=Bib Fortuna original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Bib Fortuna]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-garonnastal-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Garon Nas Tal|alt=Garon Nas Tal original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Garon Nas Tal]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-jquille-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=J'Quille|alt=J'Quille original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[J'Quille]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-reeyees-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Ree-Yees|alt=Ree-Yees original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Ree-Yees]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-tessek-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Tessek|alt=Tessek original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Tessek]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-velkentezeri-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Velken Tezeri|alt=Velken Tezeri original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Velken Tezeri]]</div></div></div>
* '''[[Bane Malar]]''': "Mysterious bounty hunter of an unknown species. Rumored to be somewhat telepathic. Infrequent member of Jabba's court. Plotting to kill Jabba."
* '''[[Bib Fortuna]]''': "Twi'lek leader and majordomo of Jabba's palace. Succeeded Jabba's last majordomo, Naroon Cuthus. Plotting to kill Jabba."
* '''[[Garon Nas Tal]]''': "Saurin combat expert. Hired by Jabba to train his Gamorrean guards. Regrets taking the job. Dislikes Jabba and his henchbeings. Plotting to kill Jabba."
* '''[[J'Quille]]''': "Whiphid spy in league with Lady Valarian. Yearns for battle. Enjoys hearing the screams of his victims. Plotting to kill Jabba."
* '''[[Ree-Yees]]''': "Gran convicted of murder. Exiled from his homeworld. Smuggler and bounty hunter. Slowly going insane. Fond of making things explode. Plotting to kill Jabba."
* '''[[Tessek]]''': "Quarien accountant. Embezzling from Jabba. Leader. Escaped Mon Calamari after its subjugation by the Empire. Plotting to kill Jabba and free the Hutt's captives."
* '''[[Velken Tezeri]]''': "Assigned by Jabba to work with Hermi Odle. Former technician for the Empire. Developed a method to remotely control seekers. Plotting to kill Jabba."

Both sides of the court are at it, Light and Dark, and so is Jabba's own majordomo.

<span id="Bubo"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-bubo-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bubo|alt=Bubo original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Bubo]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Bubo]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]): "Watchbeast. Unwittingly foiled Ree Yees' plot to kill Jabba with a thermal detonator when it ate a crucial component." One plot fails by accident: Jabba's pet eats part of [[Ree-Yees]]'s bomb.
<span id="Ephant_Mon"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-D-ephantmon-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Ephant Mon|alt=Ephant Mon original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Ephant Mon]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Ephant Mon]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]): "Chevin smuggler. One of Jabba's few truly loyal associates. Keeps Jabba informed as to the various plots against his life." The punchline: the one loyal friend, whose job is keeping track of all the others.

=== The Good, the Bad and the Ugly ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Set:''' [[Special Edition]]

''The Good, the Bad and the Ugly'' is Sergio Leone's 1966 western, and its title names its three gunmen: [[Blondie (The Good, the Bad and the Ugly)|Blondie]] (Clint Eastwood), the Good; [[Angel Eyes (The Good, the Bad and the Ugly)|Angel Eyes]] (Lee Van Cleef), the Bad; and Tuco (Eli Wallach), the Ugly.<ref name="wp-gbu">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly The Good, the Bad and the Ugly], Wikipedia (Cast: "Clint Eastwood as 'Blondie' (the Man with No Name): The Good"; "Lee Van Cleef as 'Angel Eyes': The Bad"; "Eli Wallach as Tuco Benedicto Pacífico Juan María Ramírez (known as 'The Rat' according to Blondie): The Ugly"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027184439/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref> In the film Blondie and Tuco run a bounty scam: Blondie hands Tuco over for the reward, then shoots through the noose as Tuco is about to be hanged, and the two split the money. When Blondie tires of him, he keeps the money and leaves Tuco in the desert; later the two have to work together to find buried Confederate gold, which Angel Eyes, a mercenary, is hunting too.<ref name="wp-gbu-plot">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly The Good, the Bad and the Ugly], Wikipedia (Plot: "Blondie severs the noose with a rifle bullet and the two escape to split the bounty"; "Blondie grows weary of Tuco's complaints, keeps the money, and strands Tuco in the desert"; "The two reluctantly agree to work together"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027184439/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref> Three [[Special Edition]] characters play the trio. [[Debnoli]] is an anagram of Blondie and [[Gela Yeens]] of Angel Eyes, while [[Bron Burs]] is an anagram of the Decipher artist [[Rob Burns]].<ref name="jkartists">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/artists/index.html Jedi Knights: Artists], decipher.com (2000), "Decipher's studio artists". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001207231800/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/artists/index.html Internet Archive], 7 December 2000.</ref> The fan list "Anagramed Decipherians" names the film beside all three cards and tags Gela Yeens BAD and Bron Burs UGLY.<ref name="geo">[https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians] at oocities.org (GeoCities mirror): "Bron Burs (UGLY)", "Artist--Good, The Bad & The Ugly"; "Debnoli", "Blondie", "Good, The Bad & Ugly"; "Gela Yeens (BAD)", "Angel Eyes", "Good, The Bad & Ugly". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008200413/https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref> The three anagrams are also rows of the [[Anagrams]] table. The cards are shown in the order of the title: the Good, the Bad, then the Ugly. The Virtual reprints [[Debnoli (V)]], [[Gela Yeens (V)]] and [[Bron Burs (V)]] keep the same lore. Two other cards nod to Clint Eastwood's westerns: [[#Quick Draw|Quick Draw]] ("a fistful of credits") and [[#Rolling, Rolling, Rolling|Rolling, Rolling, Rolling]] (the ''Rawhide'' theme).

The giveaway is the first word of each card's lore, which is that card's part of the film's title, in the same order: [[Debnoli]] opens "Good-natured",<ref name="dec-debnoli">[http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/specialedition/light/images/debnoli.gif Debnoli card image], decipher.com, Special Edition Light Side card list (lore: "Good-natured patron of Mos Eisley cantina"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030105193857/http://decipher.com:80/starwars/cardlists/specialedition/light/images/debnoli.gif Internet Archive], 5 January 2003.</ref> [[Gela Yeens]] opens "Bad-tempered"<ref name="dec-gelayeens">[http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/specialedition/dark/images/gelayeens.gif Gela Yeens card image], decipher.com, Special Edition Dark Side card list (lore: "Bad-tempered smuggler"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010815200852/http://decipher.com:80/starwars/cardlists/specialedition/dark/images/gelayeens.gif Internet Archive], 15 August 2001.</ref> and [[Bron Burs]] opens "Ugly scars".<ref name="dec-bronburs">[http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/specialedition/light/images/bronburs.gif Bron Burs card image], decipher.com, Special Edition Light Side card list (lore: "Ugly scars cover this former commando"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010817071821/http://decipher.com:80/starwars/cardlists/specialedition/light/images/bronburs.gif Internet Archive], 17 August 2001.</ref> The names are anagrams, but the lore says which third of the title each card plays.<ref name="wp-gbu" />

<span id="Debnoli"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-debnoli-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Debnoli|alt=Debnoli original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Debnoli]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Anagram reference - Blondie in his poncho in The Good, the Bad and the Ugly.jpg|350x450px|alt=Blondie (Clint Eastwood) in his poncho with a cigarillo]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Blondie (Clint Eastwood), the Good, in his poncho at Sad Hill cemetery, in ''The Good, the Bad and the Ugly'' (1966)</div></div></div>
'''[[Debnoli]]''' ([[Special Edition]]): "Good-natured patron of Mos Eisley cantina, until the Empire impounded his starship. Expert marksman. Seeking revenge on the Empire." ''Debnoli'' uses exactly the letters of Blondie, the Good,<ref name="geo" /> and the lore opens with "Good-natured". Blondie's part of the bounty scam is a marksman's trick, a rifle shot through the noose,<ref name="wp-gbu-plot" /> and Debnoli is an "Expert marksman" whose game text adds 1 to his total weapon destiny when he fires a character weapon and sets the forfeit of anyone he hits to 0.
<span id="Gela_Yeens"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-gelayeens-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Gela Yeens|alt=Gela Yeens original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Gela Yeens]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Anagram reference - Angel Eyes in The Good, the Bad and the Ugly.jpg|400px|alt=Angel Eyes (Lee Van Cleef)]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:400px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Angel Eyes (Lee Van Cleef), the Bad, at the final standoff in ''The Good, the Bad and the Ugly'' (1966)</div></div></div>
'''[[Gela Yeens]]''' ([[Special Edition]]): "Bad-tempered smuggler. Makes a few credits more helping Jabba collect debts. Highly regarded for his uncanny anticipation in battle. Searching for Debnoli." ''Gela Yeens'' uses exactly the letters of Angel Eyes, the Bad,<ref name="geo" /> and the lore opens with "Bad-tempered". "Makes a few credits more" turns the title of ''For a Few Dollars More'' (1965), the Leone western before ''The Good, the Bad and the Ugly'', in which Lee Van Cleef and Clint Eastwood play two bounty hunters,<ref name="wp-fafdm">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_a_Few_Dollars_More For a Few Dollars More], Wikipedia ("a 1965 spaghetti Western film directed by Sergio Leone. It stars Clint Eastwood and Lee Van Cleef as bounty hunters"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015181342/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_a_Few_Dollars_More Internet Archive], 15 October 2026.</ref> into credits, as [[#Quick Draw|Quick Draw]] turns ''A Fistful of Dollars'' into "a fistful of credits". In ''The Good, the Bad and the Ugly'' Angel Eyes is a mercenary who always finishes a job he is paid for, "usually tracking and assassination",<ref name="wp-gbu-angel">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly The Good, the Bad and the Ugly], Wikipedia (Cast: "Lee Van Cleef as 'Angel Eyes': The Bad, a ruthless, confident, sadistic mercenary who takes pleasure in killing and always finishes a job for which he is paid, usually tracking and assassination"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027184439/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref> and Gela Yeens, the card that is Angel Eyes, ends his lore "Searching for Debnoli", the card that is Blondie.
<span id="Bron_Burs"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-L-bronburs-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bron Burs|alt=Bron Burs original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Bron Burs]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Tuco in the desert in The Good, the Bad and the Ugly.jpg|350x450px|alt=Tuco (Eli Wallach), unshaven, in the desert with a coil of rope over his shoulder]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Tuco (Eli Wallach), the Ugly, in the desert with a hangman's rope on his shoulder, in ''The Good, the Bad and the Ugly'' (1966)</div></div></div>
'''[[Bron Burs]]''' ([[Special Edition]]): "Ugly scars cover this former commando from southern Nentan. Likes to be on his own. Crack shot. Off and on partner of Debnoli. Relies on intuition to survive." The title scrambles the name of Rob Burns, one of Decipher's studio artists,<ref name="jkartists" /> but the lore casts him as Tuco, the Ugly. It opens with "Ugly scars", and it makes him the "off and on partner" of Debnoli, the card that is Blondie, just as Tuco is Blondie's partner off and on in the film: sold for the bounty and cut down from the rope, then left in the desert, then taken back as a partner to find the gold.<ref name="wp-gbu-plot" /> The fan list tags the card UGLY.<ref name="geo" />

=== Union jokes ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Sets:''' [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]], [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]], [[Jedi Pack]]

Three cards, from three different sets, describe galactic characters in the language of trade unions.

<span id="Tedn_Dahai"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Jedi-L-tedndahai-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Tedn Dahai|alt=Tedn Dahai original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Tedn Dahai]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - American Federation of Musicians seal.png|350x450px|alt=The seal of the American Federation of Musicians]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The seal of the American Federation of Musicians</div></div></div>
'''[[Tedn Dahai]]''' ([[Jedi Pack]]): "Member in good standing of the Intergalactic Federation of Musicians." "Member in good standing" is the union phrase for a paid-up member, and the Intergalactic Federation of Musicians echoes the American Federation of Musicians, the musicians' union of the United States and Canada.<ref name="wp-afm">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Federation_of_Musicians American Federation of Musicians], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260904184127/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Federation_of_Musicians Internet Archive], 4 September 2026.</ref>
<span id="Ardon_'Vapor'_Crell"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JP-L-ardonvaporcrell-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Ardon 'Vapor' Crell|alt=Ardon 'Vapor' Crell original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Ardon 'Vapor' Crell]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Teamsters Local 636 hall McKees Rocks 2024.jpg|350x450px|alt=The hall of Teamsters Local 636, with TEAMSTERS LOCAL 636 carved over the door]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">The hall of Teamsters Local 636 in McKees Rocks, Pennsylvania, 2024</div></div></div>
'''[[Ardon 'Vapor' Crell]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]): "Representative from the Moisture Farmers of Tatooine (local 253)." American union branches are numbered "locals": the American Federation of Musicians has 162 of them, and New York's is Local 802.<ref name="wp-afm">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Federation_of_Musicians American Federation of Musicians], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260904184127/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Federation_of_Musicians Internet Archive], 4 September 2026.</ref> The moisture farmers of Tatooine have one too, local 253.
<span id="Televan_Koreyy"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Cor-D-televankoreyy-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Televan Koreyy|alt=Televan Koreyy original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Televan Koreyy]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - A Union of Beggars newspaper 1907.jpg|350x450px|alt=A Union of Beggars, a 1907 newspaper article with a drawing of the organizer of the beggars' trade union in France]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">"A Union of Beggars", with its organizer, in ''The Loup City Northwestern'', 4 July 1907</div></div></div>
'''[[Televan Koreyy]]''' ([[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]]): "Leader of Tatooine's Street Performers And Panhandlers' Guild." Real street performers and beggars have organized too: Boston's street musicians formed a Street Performers Guild in 1978,<ref name="c13-sab-guild">[http://www.buskersadvocates.org/StreetArts.html Street Arts and Buskers Advocates], Community Arts Advocates. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260519124015/http://www.buskersadvocates.org/StreetArts.html Internet Archive], 19 May 2026.</ref> and in 1907 American newspapers reported "A Union of Beggars", a trade union of beggars founded in Marseille.<ref name="c13-neb-1907">[https://nebnewspapers.unl.edu/lccn/2018270203/1907-07-04/ed-1/seq-4/ "A Union of Beggars"], ''The Loup City Northwestern'' (Loup City, Nebraska), 4 July 1907, page 4, Nebraska Newspapers. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027000545/https://nebnewspapers.unl.edu/lccn/2018270203/1907-07-04/ed-1/seq-4/ Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref>

=== Alien speech and sounds ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Sets:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]], [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]], [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]], [[Special Edition]], [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]], [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]]

<span id="Untranslated_alien_speech"></span>In the films, aliens speak their own languages, and the audience understands them only when someone translates. In ''Return of the Jedi'' (1983) Jabba the Hutt speaks only Huttese, which the film subtitles. When Luke arrives at Jabba's palace and tells Jabba's majordomo, Bib Fortuna, "I must be allowed to speak", Bib turns to Jabba and repeats it in Huttese, and the subtitle reads "He must be allowed to speak."<ref name="imsdb-rotj">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref> Decipher's cards print alien speech and alien noises in their lore with no subtitles at all, so a reader who knows no Huttese can pick out only the names. Sixteen cards are shown one at a time in release order, and alphabetically within each set; [[MSE-6 'Mouse' Droid]], from Premiere, is shown beside [[Wookiee Roar]], the card that scares it off. Cards printed upside down or backwards are in [[#Hard-to-read cards|Hard-to-read cards]]. Chewbacca's roar, described in seven words, is [[#Mournful Roar|Mournful Roar]], and Threepio's "How rude!" in answer to an untranslated insult is [[#E Chu Ta|E Chu Ta]].

<span id="Myo"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-myo-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Myo|alt=Myo original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Myo]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Myo]]''' ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]]): "A regenerating, primitive, violent, desert dwelling, fearless, mercenary-loving, Lirin Car'n-befriending, cyclopian Abyssin from Byss. Calling him 'monoc' will start a fight." The card never says what "monoc" means, only that the word is enough to start a fight with the one-eyed Abyssin. Wookieepedia defines it as an insult for one-eyed species and lists this card as its first source.<ref name="wook-monoc">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Monoc Monoc], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20191210190812/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Monoc Internet Archive], 10 December 2019.</ref> Before the warning, nine descriptions pile up ahead of his name, the last ones oddly specific ("Lirin Car'n-befriending"), the same gag as the run of adjectives on [[#Mournful Roar|Mournful Roar]]. The later errata text has "mercenary-joining"; the original card says "mercenary-loving".
<span id="Jawa_Blaster"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANewHope-D-jawablaster-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Jawa Blaster|alt=Jawa Blaster original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Jawa Blaster]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Jawa Blaster]]''' ([[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]): "An etching on this stock warns 'datinni greb zroom.'" A warning no reader can understand, on a gun whose game text says it can explode and be lost with the character firing it.
<span id="Oo-ta_Goo-ta,_Solo?"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-D-ootagootasolo-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Oo-ta Goo-ta, Solo?|alt=Oo-ta Goo-ta, Solo? original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Oo-ta Goo-ta, Solo?]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Oo-ta Goo-ta, Solo?]]''' ([[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]): "Greedo cheskopokuta klees ruya Solo. Hoko yanee boopa gush Cantina. Cheeco wa Solo's anye nyuma Greedo vakee. Jabba kul steeka et en anpaw." The title is Greedo's question to Han in ''Star Wars'', which the film subtitles "Going somewhere, Solo?".<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> The lore gets no subtitles: only "Greedo", "Solo", "Cantina" and "Jabba" can be read.
<span id="Wookiee_Roar"></span><span id="MSE-6_'Mouse'_Droid"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:ANH-L-wookieeroar-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Wookiee Roar|alt=Wookiee Roar original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Wookiee Roar]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-mse6mousedroid-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=MSE-6 'Mouse' Droid|alt=MSE-6 'Mouse' Droid original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[MSE-6 'Mouse' Droid]]</div></div></div>
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - A mouse droid meets Chewbacca on the Death Star in Star Wars.jpg|600px|alt=A mouse droid rolls along a Death Star corridor towards Chewbacca, who walks between two stormtroopers]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">A mouse droid rolls up to Chewbacca and his two "guards", Luke and Han in stormtrooper armour, in a Death Star corridor in ''Star Wars'' (1977)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Chewbacca roars at the mouse droid in Star Wars.jpg|600px|alt=Chewbacca, between two stormtroopers, opens his mouth to roar at something on the floor in front of him]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Chewbacca roars down at the mouse droid, which squeals and flees</div></div></div>
'''[[Wookiee Roar]]''' ([[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]]) and '''[[MSE-6 'Mouse' Droid]]''' ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]]): Wookiee Roar's whole lore is the roar itself, spelled out: "'GHRRRRAARRRRHG!'" There is nothing to translate, and the card's picture is Chewbacca with his mouth wide open. One of its three game text options is "Scare off (lose) one 'mouse' droid on table", and the mouse droid's own lore ends "Easily frightened." Together the two cards play out a moment in ''Star Wars'' (1977). Luke and Han, disguised as stormtroopers, are marching Chewbacca through the Death Star as their "prisoner" when a mouse droid rolls up to them; Chewbacca roars at it, and it squeals and races away.<ref name="wook-g7">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/MSE-6-G735Y MSE-6-G735Y], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260124100120/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/MSE-6-G735Y Internet Archive], 24 January 2026.</ref> StarWars.com says mouse droids are given to "exploding into panicked squeals when confused or frightened".<ref name="sw-mousedroid">[https://www.starwars.com/databank/mouse-droid Mouse Droid], StarWars.com Databank. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261005164956/https://www.starwars.com/databank/mouse-droid Internet Archive], 5 October 2026.</ref> On the table, one roar is enough to make the droid lost.
<span id="Res_Luk_Ra'auf"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-reslukraauf-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Res Luk Ra'auf|alt=Res Luk Ra'auf original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Res Luk Ra'auf]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Res Luk Ra'auf]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "Rek guza kias n'ek kriesuk zief. Rek res fesruk T'doshok kulesuk luk g'razzurg koref selukra fes k'nel. Kren'ef, T'doshok res luk rek grien forek res fel luraken." The title is Bossk's line in ''The Empire Strikes Back'',<ref name="c13-sw-bossk">[https://www.starwars.com/databank/bossk Bossk], StarWars.com Databank. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008205807/https://www.starwars.com/databank/bossk Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref> where he is one of the bounty hunters on Vader's bridge and Admiral Piett says "Bounty hunters. We don't need that scum."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> The whole lore is in the bounty hunter's own language, with no translation (see also [[#I Don't Need Their Scum, Either|I Don't Need Their Scum, Either]]).
<span id="We'll_Find_Han"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:CloudCity-L-wellfindhan-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=We'll Find Han|alt=We'll Find Han original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[We'll Find Han]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Chewbacca wails beside Lando in the Millennium Falcon in The Empire Strikes Back.jpg|600px|alt=Chewbacca, mouth wide open, in the cockpit of the Millennium Falcon, with Lando Calrissian turning towards him]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Chewbacca's wail, beside Lando in the cockpit of the ''Millennium Falcon'', at the end of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980)</div></div></div>
'''[[We'll Find Han]]''' ([[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]]): "'I promise.' 'Auuuuuug!'" The card's picture is Lando Calrissian and Chewbacca in the cockpit of the ''Millennium Falcon'' at the end of ''The Empire Strikes Back''. Han has been frozen in carbonite and flown off by the bounty hunter Boba Fett, and the two are setting off to find him. Lando tells Leia over the comlink, "Princess, we'll find Han. I promise." Luke adds, "Chewie, I'll be waiting for your signal", and the script's only answer is "Chewie's wail comes over the comlink."<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The title and the first half of the lore are Lando's promise; the second half is Chewbacca's reply, spelled out as "Auuuuuug!" with no translation, so the reader understands as much of it as Luke does. The game text keeps the promise: it can deploy Han to the same site as Chewie or your Lando.
