<span id="Bantha_Fodder"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JabbasPalace-D-banthafodder-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bantha Fodder|alt=Bantha Fodder original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Bantha Fodder]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Bantha Fodder]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]): "Uu a'kingsa riika pagh bagla bis kachata weenow con bantha poodoo." Only the last two words can be made out, and the title translates them: "bantha poodoo" is Huttese for "bantha fodder", food for banthas, said of a person who is worth nothing more.<ref name="wook-banthafodder">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Bantha_fodder Bantha fodder], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251018181424/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Bantha_fodder Internet Archive], 18 October 2025.</ref> Banthas are the elephant-sized, horned beasts the Sand People ride in ''Star Wars''.<ref name="imsdb-anh" /> In ''Return of the Jedi'' Jabba says it to Han Solo, just freed from the carbonite, and the film subtitles it "It's too late for that, Solo. You may have been a good smuggler, but now you're Bantha fodder."<ref name="imsdb-rotj" /> The card's picture is Han in Jabba's palace. The rest of the lore gets no subtitle. One of the card's game text options searches your Reserve Deck for a bantha.
<span id="Hutt_Bounty"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JabbasPalace-D-huttbounty-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Hutt Bounty|alt=Hutt Bounty original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Hutt Bounty]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Hutt Bounty]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]): "Chissaa, picha gawanki Chewbacca. Yupon cogorato kama walpa kyess kashung kawa Wookiee." The only words a reader can pick out are "Chewbacca" and "Wookiee". The card's picture is Chewbacca with the bounty hunter Boushh, who is Princess Leia in disguise. In ''Return of the Jedi'' Boushh leads Chewbacca into Jabba's palace and says, in Ubese, which the film subtitles, "I have come for the bounty on this Wookiee." Jabba answers in Huttese, subtitled "At last we have the mighty Chewbacca", and Threepio translates his offer of twenty-five thousand.<ref name="imsdb-rotj" /> The card's lore is all Huttese and gets neither subtitles nor Threepio. Its game text pays out when a bounty hunter brings a captured smuggler, gambler or thief to Jabba's dungeon.
<span id="I_Must_Be_Allowed_To_Speak"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JabbasPalace-L-imustbeallowedtospeak-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=I Must Be Allowed To Speak|alt=I Must Be Allowed To Speak original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[I Must Be Allowed To Speak]]</div></div></div>
'''[[I Must Be Allowed To Speak]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]): "Jedi mod spienko eek." The title is Luke's line to Bib Fortuna in ''Return of the Jedi'', which Bib repeats to Jabba in Huttese, subtitled "He must be allowed to speak."<ref name="imsdb-rotj" /> The lore is a line in an alien language in which only "Jedi" can be read, with no subtitle, so the card about being allowed to speak speaks in words the reader cannot follow. The card's picture is Luke, hooded, in Jabba's palace.
<span id="Information_Exchange"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JabbasPalace-D-informationexchange-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Information Exchange|alt=Information Exchange original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Information Exchange]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Information Exchange]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]): "Chisa nyooda ishaley. Kun Jabba neguda len malta." "Ikkit ui! Yobbit, yobbit. Nelan tui ke bada." The lore is two quoted lines, as if from the two aliens talking in the card's picture, a Rodian and a Jawa, and only "Jabba" can be read. The title promises an exchange of information; the reader gets none of it. The game text is about information brokers, and lets you look at the top four cards of your opponent's Reserve Deck.
<span id="Ke_Chu_Ke_Kukuta?"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:JabbasPalace-L-kechukekukuta-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Ke Chu Ke Kukuta?|alt=Ke Chu Ke Kukuta? original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Ke Chu Ke Kukuta?]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Jabba's gatekeeper droid looks Threepio over in Return of the Jedi.jpg|600px|alt=A round mechanical eye on a jointed arm, pushed out of a door, faces C-3PO]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Jabba's gatekeeper droid looks Threepio over at the palace door in ''Return of the Jedi'' (1983)</div></div></div>
'''[[Ke Chu Ke Kukuta?]]''' ([[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]): "Balka. Hachu ma blinki?" Here even the title is alien. The card's picture is the eye of the gatekeeper droid at the door of Jabba's palace.<ref name="wook-tt8l">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/TT-8L_gatekeeper_droid/Legends TT-8L gatekeeper droid], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260521041018/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/TT-8L_gatekeeper_droid/Legends Internet Archive], 21 May 2026.</ref> In ''Return of the Jedi'', when Threepio knocks, the eye pops out on its arm and says something no one translates, which the script spells "Tee chuta hhat yudd!" Threepio answers "Artoo Detoowha bo Seethreepiowha ey toota odd mischka Jabba du Hutt", and the eye laughs and goes back in.<ref name="imsdb-rotj" /> Neither the film nor the card says what the gatekeeper asks. The game text does the gatekeeper's job: an Imperial who has just deployed to a Jabba's Palace site is sent back to its owner's hand and may not be deployed again that turn.
<span id="Bossk_In_Hound's_Tooth"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-bosskinhoundstooth-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Bossk In Hound's Tooth|alt=Bossk In Hound's Tooth original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Bossk In Hound's Tooth]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Bossk In Hound's Tooth]]''' ([[Special Edition]]): "Bossk once said of his ship, 'Greeezeg uut nikek!'" The lore quotes what Bossk said about the ''Hound's Tooth'', but not what it means.
<span id="Jabba's_Through_With_You"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:SE-D-jabbasthroughwithyou-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Jabba's Through With You|alt=Jabba's Through With You original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Jabba's Through With You]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Jabba's Through With You]]''' ([[Special Edition]]): "'Klees ka tlanko ya oska.'" The title is a line from the Mos Eisley cantina in ''Star Wars''. Greedo, a bounty hunter working for Jabba the Hutt, holds Han at gunpoint and tells him, in his own language with English subtitles, "Jabba's through with you. He has no time for smugglers who drop their shipments at the first sign of an Imperial cruiser."<ref name="imsdb-anh" /> The lore is a different line. When Greedo says Jabba may only take Han's ship, Han answers "Over my dead body", and Greedo's last words are subtitled "That's the idea. I've been looking forward to this for a long time."<ref name="wook-greedo-legends">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Greedo/Legends Greedo], Wookieepedia (Legends). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260526042401/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Greedo/Legends Internet Archive], 26 May 2026.</ref> The short story "A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale", in the book ''Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina'' (1995), writes that reply out in Greedo's language as "Ukle nyuma cheskopokuta klees ka tlanko ya oska", and the card's lore is its last five words.<ref name="wermo-huttese">[https://www.completewermosguide.com/hutttranscript.html Huttese Transcript], The Complete Wermo's Guide to Huttese & Other Star Wars Languages (section on ''Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina''). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260705043914/https://www.completewermosguide.com/hutttranscript.html Internet Archive], 5 July 2026.</ref> So the card is titled with one of Greedo's lines, in English, and quotes another without its subtitle. The picture is Han and Greedo across the cantina table, and the game text rewards a bounty hunter who has just fired a character weapon. Greedo's opening question to Han is [[#Oo-ta Goo-ta, Solo?|Oo-ta Goo-ta, Solo?]], above.
<span id="Losing_Track"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Tatooine-L-losingtrack-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Losing Track|alt=Losing Track original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Losing Track]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Losing Track]]''' ([[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]]): "'Wha-? Chuba da noya!'" The card is about the podrace across the Tatooine desert in ''The Phantom Menace'' (1999), and its picture is podracers streaking over the sand. Only "Wha-?" is English, the sound of someone who has lost track of what is going on. "Chuba" is Huttese, and Wookieepedia gives "Chuba!" as "Hey you!";<ref name="wook-huttese">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Huttese Huttese], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719152557/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Huttese Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> the rest gets no translation, and the card does not say who is speaking. The race in the film is hosted by Jabba the Hutt, who has no interest in the sport, falls asleep during it, and has to be woken by Bib Fortuna when it is over.<ref name="wook-jabba-legends">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jabba_Desilijic_Tiure/Legends Jabba Desilijic Tiure], Wookieepedia (Legends). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260731134326/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jabba_Desilijic_Tiure/Legends Internet Archive], 31 July 2026.</ref> The game text is about the race, not the speaker: it can put a card from the opponent's Lost Pile back on their Reserve Deck, "repair" your Podracer, or "damage" another.
<span id="Ewok_Celebration"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Ref3-L-ewokcelebration-decipher-archive.jpg|350px|link=Ewok Celebration|alt=Ewok Celebration original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Ewok Celebration]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Ewok Celebration]]''' ([[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]]): "'Na na, beecha na noooooooooooooooowa.'" The card's picture is the party in the Ewok village at the end of ''Return of the Jedi'', after the Empire is beaten on Endor,<ref name="imsdb-rotj" /> with Ewoks beating on captured stormtrooper helmets like drums. In the 1983 film the Ewoks sing "Ewok Celebration", better known as "Yub Nub". Its Ewokese words were written by the film's sound designer, Ben Burtt, and it has published English words too ("Freedom, we got freedom").<ref name="wook-ewokcelebration">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Ewok_Celebration Ewok Celebration], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260306040452/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Ewok_Celebration Internet Archive], 6 March 2026.</ref> The card's line is not in those lyrics, and the reader gets no English for it, only a "no" held for sixteen o's. In the 1997 Special Edition of the film the song was replaced by a new piece, "Victory Celebration".<ref name="wook-ewokcelebration" /> The game text makes Ewoks better in battle at Endor sites.

=== Vader choking people ===
'''Type:''' [[#type-running-gag|Running gag]] · '''Sets:''' [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]], [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]], [[Jedi Pack]], [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]], [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]]

In the films, Darth Vader punishes his own officers by strangling them with the Force, from across the room and without touching them. In ''Star Wars'' (1977) he chokes Admiral Motti, who has mocked the Force, until Grand Moff Tarkin orders "Vader, release him!"<ref name="imsdb-anh">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Star Wars: A New Hope script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260720032511/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-A-New-Hope.html Internet Archive], 20 July 2026.</ref> In ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980) he kills two officers this way: Admiral Ozzel, over a video link, with "You have failed me for the last time, Admiral", and Captain Needa, who has come to apologise for losing the ''Millennium Falcon'', with "Apology accepted, Captain Needa."<ref name="imsdb-esb">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260719123444/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-The-Empire-Strikes-Back.html Internet Archive], 19 July 2026.</ref> In ''Return of the Jedi'' (1983) he warns Jerjerrod, the commander of the second Death Star, that "The Emperor is not as forgiving as I am."<ref name="imsdb-rotj">[https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Star Wars: Return of the Jedi script], IMSDb. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260802212158/https://imsdb.com/scripts/Star-Wars-Return-of-the-Jedi.html Internet Archive], 2 August 2026.</ref> Fourteen Decipher cards, from Premiere to Death Star II, joke about it or turn it into game text. They are shown one at a time in release order, and alphabetically within each set.

<span id="Alter"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-alter-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Alter (Dark) (Premiere)|alt=Alter original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Alter (Dark) (Premiere)|Alter]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Alter (Dark) (Premiere)|Alter]]''' ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]]): "A user of the Force can subjugate the will of others or alter the environment at a distance, as when Vader 'disciplines' those whose lack of faith disturbs him." The quotation marks around "disciplines" do the same work as the ones around "alternative" on Demotion, the next card: the word stands for the choke. "Those whose lack of faith disturbs him" are officers like Motti, and the card's picture is Vader with his gloved hand raised.
<span id="Demotion"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-L-demotion-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Demotion|alt=Demotion original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Demotion|Demotion]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Vader chokes Admiral Motti in A New Hope.jpg|600px|alt=Admiral Motti clutches his throat as Darth Vader stands over him]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Vader chokes Admiral Motti in ''Star Wars'' (1977)</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Vader chokes Admiral Ozzel in The Empire Strikes Back.jpg|600px|alt=Admiral Ozzel chokes on a viewscreen while Captain Piett looks on]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Admiral Ozzel chokes to death on a viewscreen, watched by Captain Piett, in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980)</div></div></div>
'''[[Demotion]]''' ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]]): "Repercussions for failure are severe in the Imperial military. Many officers prefer demotion to 'alternative' punishment from Darth Vader." The lore never says what the "'alternative' punishment" is; the quotation marks leave it to the reader. Anyone who has seen the films knows it: the choke, which Motti survives only because Tarkin stops it, and which kills Ozzel and Needa. Compared with that, a demotion is the lucky outcome. The game text, "Use 2 Force to deploy on any Imperial, except Darth Vader, Emperor Palpatine or Stormtrooper. That Imperial is power -2 and cannot use its 'game text.'", only costs the officer 2 power and his game text.
<span id="I_Find_Your_Lack_Of_Faith_Disturbing"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Premiere-D-ifindyourlackoffaith-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=I Find Your Lack Of Faith Disturbing|alt=I Find Your Lack Of Faith Disturbing original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[I Find Your Lack Of Faith Disturbing|I Find Your Lack Of Faith Disturbing]]</div></div></div>
'''[[I Find Your Lack Of Faith Disturbing]]''' ([[Premiere Limited|Premiere]]): "Darth Vader ruthlessly used the Force to strike down enemies and soldiers who displeased him. He could choke victims from afar without touching them." The title is what Vader says to Motti as he chokes him (the first film still with Demotion, above),<ref name="imsdb-anh" /> and the card's picture is Motti with his hand at his throat. The lore counts "soldiers who displeased him" among Vader's victims, next to his enemies.
<span id="Vader"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:P2P-D-vader-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Vader (Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game)|alt=Vader original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Vader (Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game)|Vader]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Vader (Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game)|Vader]]''' ([[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]]): this Vader chokes his own side when things go badly. His game text: "If in a losing battle, draw destiny. If destiny > 4, 'choke' (lose) one Imperial present (your choice)." When he loses a battle, the Dark Side player may have to give up one of their own Imperials at that battle, as the officer Vader takes it out on.
<span id="Motti"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Jedi-D-motti-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Motti|alt=Motti original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Motti|Motti]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Motti]]''' ([[Jedi Pack]]): "Considered an overrated leader by many subordinates. Has a disturbing lack of faith. Became a member of the Death Star's command triumvirate despite his failings." "A disturbing lack of faith" is Vader's line to Motti just before he chokes him; the lore files it as a character trait.
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-D-admiralozzel-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Admiral Ozzel|alt=Admiral Ozzel original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Admiral Ozzel|Admiral Ozzel]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Admiral Ozzel]]''' ([[Hoth Limited|Hoth]]): "Leader of the Emperor's Death Squadron assigned to hunt down and crush the Rebellion. As clumsy as he is stupid. Has just failed Darth Vader for the next-to-last time." "As clumsy as he is stupid" is what Vader says about Ozzel just before he kills him<ref name="imsdb-esb" />; the last time is the next card. Full entry: [[#Admiral Ozzel and Death Squadron Star Destroyer|Admiral Ozzel and Death Squadron Star Destroyer]].
<span id="You_Have_Failed_Me_For_The_Last_Time"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Hoth-L-youhavefailedmeforthelasttime-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=You Have Failed Me For The Last Time|alt=You Have Failed Me For The Last Time original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[You Have Failed Me For The Last Time|You Have Failed Me For The Last Time]]</div></div></div>
'''[[You Have Failed Me For The Last Time]]''' ([[Hoth Limited|Hoth]]): "'Lord Vader, the fleet has moved out of lightspeed and we're preparing to aah . . . ukh . . . uh . . . uuuuukkk!'" The title is Vader's line to Ozzel, and the lore is Ozzel's report, cut off as the choke takes hold; in the script he gets as far as "we're preparing to... Aaagh!"<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The card's picture is Ozzel on the viewscreen, the scene in the second still with Demotion above. Its game text makes the target "immediately lost (placed out of play if Ozzel)": Ozzel does not come back.
<span id="Apology_Accepted"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-apologyaccepted-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Apology Accepted|alt=Apology Accepted original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Apology Accepted|Apology Accepted]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Captain Needa dead at Vader's feet in The Empire Strikes Back.jpg|400px|alt=Captain Needa lies dead on the floor of the bridge at Darth Vader's feet]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:400px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Captain Needa dead at Vader's feet, in a promotional photograph for ''The Empire Strikes Back'' (1980)</div></div></div>
'''[[Apology Accepted]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "'I shall assume full responsibility for losing them and apologize to Lord Vader.' Needa discovered that Vader was only slightly more forgiving than the Emperor." The first sentence is Captain Needa's line after the ''Millennium Falcon'' escapes him; the title is Vader's answer as he chokes him.<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The card's picture is Needa choking. The game text makes the Dark Side player lose one of their own Imperials who survived a battle they lost.
<span id="Captain_Needa"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-captainneeda-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Captain Needa|alt=Captain Needa original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Captain Needa|Captain Needa]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Captain Needa]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "Able leader and captain of the ''Avenger''. Was given his command by Admiral Ozzel. Treated with suspicion by Darth Vader and the Emperor, who distrust Ozzel's close advisors." Needa owes his ship to Ozzel, and Vader chokes them both in the same film, Ozzel first. The lore calls it suspicion.
<span id="Field_Promotion"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-fieldpromotion-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Field Promotion|alt=Field Promotion original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Field Promotion|Field Promotion]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Field Promotion]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "Imperial officers are fiercely competitive, especially on the ''Executor''. Lord Vader's flagship is a place where devious political calculation prospers. The naive are doomed to failure." A field promotion is one made on the spot, like Captain Piett's on Vader's bridge: as Ozzel chokes, Vader tells Piett "You are in command now, Admiral Piett."<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> The card protects against the other cards in this gag: the Imperial it is on is "immune to Demotion, Report To Lord Vader and What Is Thy Bidding, My Master?".
<span id="Report_To_Lord_Vader"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-L-reporttolordvader-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Report To Lord Vader|alt=Report To Lord Vader original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Report To Lord Vader|Report To Lord Vader]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Report To Lord Vader]]''' ([[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]): "An evil Lord of the Sith, Darth Vader used fear as a powerful motivational factor. The Emperor demanded results. Vader settled for no less." After the Light Side wins a battle, an Imperial who took part has to report to Vader, and the game text says what happens when he gets there: "When target reaches Vader, lose Utinni Effect and draw destiny. If destiny > 2, target lost."
<span id="Imperial_Command"></span><div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:DS2-D-imperialcommand-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Imperial Command|alt=Imperial Command original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Imperial Command|Imperial Command]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Dagobah-D-apologyaccepted-decipher-archive.gif|350x450px|link=Apology Accepted|alt=Apology Accepted original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Apology Accepted]] (Dagobah), whose picture is Captain Needa choking</div></div></div>
'''[[Imperial Command]]''' ([[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]]): "The Emperor's high command is subjected to close scrutiny by the Imperial bureaucracy. Despite this apparent lack of trust, many turn out to be fine commanders." The Empire runs on distrust. Its officers scheme against one another, and one of its own security services, the Imperial Security Bureau, was charged with protecting it against threats from within the Empire and ensuring the loyalty of its subjects, not only with hunting Rebels.<ref name="wook-isb">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Imperial_Security_Bureau Imperial Security Bureau], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260626220611/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Imperial_Security_Bureau Internet Archive], 26 June 2026.</ref> Its commanders also have Vader to answer to, and he kills the ones who fail him, like Ozzel and Needa.<ref name="imsdb-esb" /> Against that background the lore notes, in a calm, official tone, that the high command is "subjected to close scrutiny" and that "many turn out to be fine commanders". Many, not all. The card's picture is Vader with a line of Imperial officers; the card that pictures one of them being choked is [[Apology Accepted]], shown beside it.
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:DS2-D-lordvader-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Lord Vader|alt=Lord Vader original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Lord Vader|Lord Vader]]</div></div></div>
'''[[Lord Vader]]''' ([[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]]): "Forgiving administrator of Imperial policy. Emperor Palpatine's most trusted leader. Believes converting Skywalker is key to the Alliance's downfall." The lore calls the man who kills Ozzel and Needa "forgiving", with a straight face. Full entry: [[#Lord Vader|Lord Vader]].
<div style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:16px; align-items:flex-end; justify-content:flex-start; margin:0.4em 0 0.6em;"><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:DS2-D-moffjerjerrod-decipher-archive.gif|350px|link=Moff Jerjerrod|alt=Moff Jerjerrod original card]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:350px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">[[Moff Jerjerrod|Moff Jerjerrod]]</div></div><div style="flex:0 1 auto; max-width:100%; text-align:center;">[[File:Joke reference - Vader chokes Moff Jerjerrod in a scene cut from Return of the Jedi.jpg|600px|alt=Moff Jerjerrod clutches his throat between two Royal Guards]]<div style="font-size:95%; max-width:600px; margin:0.2em auto 0;">Vader chokes Jerjerrod, in a scene cut from ''Return of the Jedi'' (1983)</div></div></div>
'''[[Moff Jerjerrod]]''' ([[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]]): "Leader. Found discussions with Vader to be particularly motivating. Does not want to find out if the Emperor is more forgiving than Vader." Vader ends his visit to Jerjerrod in ''Return of the Jedi'' with "The Emperor is not as forgiving as I am."<ref name="imsdb-rotj" /> Wookieepedia lists photographs of Vader choking Jerjerrod among the deleted scenes from the film.<ref name="wook-vaderchoke">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/File:Vaderchoke.jpg File:Vaderchoke.jpg], Wookieepedia: "Darth Vader Force chokes Moff Tiaan Jerjerrod", from ''Return of the Jedi'' (deleted scene). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20190325212802/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/File:Vaderchoke.jpg Internet Archive], 25 March 2019.</ref> In that scene, as Wookieepedia tells it, Jerjerrod bars Vader's way to the Emperor's throne room, and Vader lets him go when he gasps out that it is the Emperor's command.<ref name="wook-jerjerrod">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Tiaan_Jerjerrod Tiaan Jerjerrod], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260718185317/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Tiaan_Jerjerrod Internet Archive], 18 July 2026.</ref> Full entry: [[#Moff Jerjerrod|Moff Jerjerrod]].
